proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing open threat models, defense-in-depth patterns, privacy-preserving execution architectures, and security guardrails for autonomous agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical body chartered with establishing security baselines, threat modeling frameworks, privacy-preserving execution architectures, and defensive guardrails across agent lifecycles[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e]. Operating as an intersecting layer across all AAIF working groups, it evaluates execution vulnerabilities, confidential data protection, secrets handling, and containment mechanisms for agentic systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

# Scope and Charter Themes

The working group organizes its problem space around pre-competitive defensive standards and operational boundaries across several core themes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]:

- **Privacy and Sensitive Data**: Defining conventions for personally identifiable information (PII) obfuscation, regulated records handling (such as HIPAA), and secrets management that distinguishes traditional credentials (API keys, environment variables) from proprietary context and confidential training data[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Private Agentic Workflows**: Investigating privacy-preserving execution architectures, including Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), zero-knowledge (ZK) assertion proofs, and encrypted vector databases to prevent unauthorized external data leakage during processing[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Blast Radius and Rogue Agent Containment**: Formulating containment boundaries, measurement metrics for rogue agent impact, and out-of-band kill controls[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Commerce and Transaction Guardrails**: In coordination with the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md), narrowing commercial scope strictly to defensive boundaries, including fund depletion prevention, account isolation, and tool invocation limits on payment agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Identity and Authorization Hooks**: Coordinating with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) on capability-based authorization, agent-to-agent (A2A) authentication, agent-to-MCP-server verification, and runtime checkpointing[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e].
- **Attack Surface and Resilience**: Addressing prompt injection mitigation, red teaming practices, social engineering resistance, and multi-agent persuasion vectors[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e].
- **Internal Taxonomy**: Developing an internal vocabulary of security and privacy definitions before submitting standardized terms to the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

## Scope Boundaries and Deferrals

- **Ethics and Value Judgments**: Inquiries regarding model bias, business ethics, and responsible AI governance are formally deferred to the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Hallucinations and Reliability**: General accuracy metrics fall under the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md), though guardrails addressing non-malicious agent misbehavior, agent derailment, and unintended sabotage remain actively evaluated for defensive scope[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

# Operational Structure and Governance

The working group operates under the governance model overseen by the AAIF [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and the Linux Foundation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e]:

- **Leadership**: Alex Frazer serves as the elected chair, with co-chair roles open to member self-nomination and LFX ranked-choice voting[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Membership and Cadence**: Open across associate, silver, gold, and platinum member tiers, operating on a bi-weekly meeting rhythm supported by Discord and GitHub repositories[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **External Alignment**: Actively cross-references initiatives with external efforts, including the OWASP Agentic AI project, to prevent redundant work[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group bridging global AI policy developments and technical agentic systems, tracking compliance architectures, risk assessment protocols, and regulatory gaps.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body bridging global AI policy developments and technical agentic systems. It tracks compliance architectures, risk assessment protocols, and regulatory gaps across emerging jurisdictions, operating under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and governed by the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].

# Architecture / Specification

## Working Model and Scope

The working group operates under a three-phase methodology focused on pre-competitive alignment[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]:
1. **Landscape Analysis**: Cataloging existing standards, industry frameworks, regulations, and production use cases relevant to agentic systems.
2. **Gap Analysis**: Identifying areas where established compliance and risk governance frameworks fail to address autonomous, agent-specific failure modes.
3. **Distilled Guidance and Principles**: Developing synthesized guidance and implementation recommendations for organizations deploying agentic systems.

Key policy and regulatory touchpoints evaluated include the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act (EU AI Act), eIDAS 2, GDPR data protection and PII redaction controls, probabilistic risk assessment frameworks, and regulatory co-creation models such as those from Singapore authorities[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

## Operational Infrastructure

The working group meets on a biweekly cadence, maintaining collaborative working drafts in Google Docs, secondary community discussions on Discord, and public meeting records in repository markdown files[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]. Meeting note authoring follows standardized agent instructions defined in AGENTS.md and TEMPLATE.md, capturing LFX resource links, topics, decisions, deliverables, and action item ownership in reverse-chronological order[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-6fa126354b0b-2d7e8a4a][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d7a6875f36a3-5c7bc654].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-02-19**: Working group kickoff meeting covering Linux Foundation governance, antitrust rules, chair nomination procedures, and initial regulatory landscape priorities[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].
- **2026-03-05**: Working group formalizes its three-step deliverable model, establishes biweekly operational rhythm under elected co-chairs Ryan and Junjie, and initializes submissions for landscape and problem-set analyses[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: Governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation overseeing technical vision, project lifecycle policy, working groups, and resource priorities.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) is the primary technical governance body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), established by the Governing Board (GB) to evaluate project proposals, oversee technical vision, and manage the project and working group lifecycles [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]. Operating as a directed fund of The Linux Foundation, the TC facilitates communication and coordination across technical projects and the broader open-source community [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# Architecture / Specification
The operational structure, authority, and procedural rules of the TC are defined by its formal Charter [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]:

- **Composition**: Each Platinum Member of AAIF is entitled to appoint one representative to the TC [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Leadership**: The TC annually elects a Chair and optional Co-Chair to preside over meetings and represent the technical community [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Responsibilities**: The committee is tasked with establishing, managing, and archiving Working Groups; recommending technical projects and resource priorities to the Governing Board; deciding lifecycle stage transitions; and applying the Project Lifecycle Policy [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Voting and Consensus**: The TC operates primarily on consensus. When formal votes occur, each voting member has one vote. A meeting quorum requires at least 50% of voting members [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Lazy Consensus**: Routine decisions may proceed via lazy consensus under a 72-hour silence-as-agreement window; any formal objection requires an electronic majority vote of all voting members [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Charter Amendments**: Modifying the TC Charter requires a two-thirds majority vote of the TC along with Governing Board approval [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# Lifecycle History
The Governing Board charter for the Technical Committee was formally adopted on March 3, 2026 [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# References
- [../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md)
- [../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md)

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing open threat models, shared taxonomies, and design patterns to advance security and privacy as a shared discipline.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an AAIF technical body focused on establishing security and privacy engineering as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]. Co-chaired by Alex Frazer and Junjie Bu (Google), the group produces open threat models, shared taxonomies, and defensive design patterns that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to enforce shared responsibility for trustworthy agentic systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its mandate and inter-group coordination across several core pillars [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]:

- **Mission Statement**: Formally adopted on March 31, 2026, the group's mission is to advance the AAIF's purpose by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the ecosystem, producing open threat models, a shared taxonomy, and design patterns [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
- **Scope and Focus Areas**: Key technical focus areas include threat modeling and attack surface mapping, security architecture and design patterns (explicitly encompassing agent skills), and technical privacy engineering such as data minimization, memory isolation, and sensitive data protection [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
- **Planned Deliverables**: Identified deliverables include a living taxonomy of security terms, an agentic threat modeling framework, security and privacy design patterns, a security best practices guide, and a cross-workgroup review checklist [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec].
- **Cross-WG Collaboration**: The group establishes complementary boundaries with other AAIF working groups: providing security and audit logging requirements to [../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) while deferring core identity mechanisms; collaborating with [../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) on anomaly detection; coordinating payment security with [../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md); and aligning with [../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) on regulatory monitoring [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].

# Lifecycle History
In March 2026, Junjie Bu was introduced as co-chair alongside Alex Frazer [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec]. On March 31, 2026, the working group unanimously voted to adopt its formal mission statement (Option G) and expanded its design patterns scope to cover agent skills [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, cross-boundary trace correlation, and agent behavior trace models.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) is an AAIF technical body that convenes practitioners, vendors, and standards organizations to build a shared understanding of AI agent observability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]. Led by Chair Pavan Sudheendra, the group functions as a coordination forum that aligns existing industry efforts, identifies telemetry gaps across multi-turn and multi-tool agent workflows, and produces specifications only when no existing body addresses the need [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's charter defines its operational scope, principles, and foundational focus areas [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]:

- **Coordination Forum Model**: The OT-WG is explicitly not a competing standards body; it coordinates and upstreams contributions to adjacent groups including the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, W3C Trace Context, and OWASP Automated Operational Safety (AOS) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Guiding Principles**: The working group adheres to six principles: coordinate first and specify only when necessary; prioritize interoperability over innovation; ensure systems are observable by default; move at the speed of the ecosystem; emphasize implementation and adoption over theoretical elegance; and maintain strict vendor and framework neutrality [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Core Problem Space**: The group addresses ecosystem fragmentation across proprietary trace formats, bridges the visibility gap between individual LLM call tracing and session-level agent workflow understanding, and tackles multi-modal lineage and grounding [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Founding Focus Area**: The group's primary technical mandate is established around the [../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) (ABTM) focus area to standardize behavioral execution traces and causal tool event correlation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

# Lifecycle History
The charter draft was updated on April 13, 2026, designating Pavan Sudheendra as primary contact and chair [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing open threat models, shared taxonomies, design patterns, best practices guides, and cross-working group review checklists.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing open threat models, taxonomies, security design patterns, and operational review mechanisms for autonomous systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151] Operating within the Linux Foundation framework, the working group addresses architectural vulnerabilities arising from autonomous tool execution, persistent agent memory, dynamic privilege escalation, and multi-agent coordination.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group governs five primary deliverables approved for its initial 3–6 month horizon:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]
- **Taxonomy**: A living reference document defining foundational security and privacy terms for incorporation into the broader AAIF taxonomy through ../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: A research-oriented deliverable assessing existing frameworks (such as OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, and NIST) across modern threat contexts—including lethal trifectas, shared memory stores, and plastic neural weights—to evaluate whether a new domain-specific threat model is warranted (see ../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: A builder-facing catalog codifying patterns for human-in-the-loop oversight, hook extensibility, logical and semantic constraint enforcement, and privacy-preserving execution.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]
- **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: Practical, operational guidance covering topics such as secrets management and secure tool invocation for builders (see ../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: A structured review instrument enabling other AAIF working groups to evaluate early security and privacy implications across their specifications (see ../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]

Beyond internal deliverables, the working group liaises with adjacent ecosystem initiatives, including Model Context Protocol (MCP) Interceptors for standardized security hooks across runtimes, MCP Apps for site identity verification and secure agent interaction surfaces, and Linux Foundation efforts including Project Glasswing.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]

# Lifecycle History
On 2026-04-14, the Security and Privacy Working Group unanimously approved its operational scope, its five initial 3–6 month deliverables, and its charter via formal vote, scheduling formal charter presentation and deliverable lead ratification with the ../governance/technical-committee.md.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive ecosystem market map and catalog backed by landscape.yml and CNCF Landscape2 tracking open-source agentic AI projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive ecosystem market map and catalog providing a comprehensive view of prominent open-source software and open standards across the agentic AI landscape, including Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) members and hosted projects.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1] Maintained in coordination with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the landscape visualizes active projects categorized by functional architecture and ecosystem role.

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape is generated using the open-source CNCF Landscape2 compilation engine.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1] Catalog data is maintained declaratively in `landscape.yml`, paired with vector artwork stored in SVG format under the `hosted_logos` directory.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1] Automated workflows rebuild the deployment daily, publishing merged pull requests to production within 24 hours.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]

## Inclusion and Submission Guidelines
Submissions to `landscape.yml` must comply with strict acceptance criteria:[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]
- **Open-source scope**: Projects must be open-source software or open standards maintaining at least 1,000 GitHub stars and clear architectural relevance to an established landscape category.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]
- **Exclusion of closed solutions**: Proprietary software, closed-source SaaS offerings, commercial versions of open-source projects, and closed products implementing open-source interfaces are excluded.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]
- **Single-category allocation**: Each organization's project is restricted to a single box representing its primary or best-known capability to avoid redundant listings across categories.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]
- **Entity governance**: Organization attribution is mapped to the legal entity or organization controlling the software and associated trademark.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]
- **Asset conventions**: Logos must be provided in SVG format with English typography, transparent or white backgrounds (non-reversed), and stacked orientations when variant layouts exist.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]

## Extended Attributes
Detailed project descriptions and organizational context are provided through an `extra` configuration block in `landscape.yml`, conforming to the CNCF Landscape2 data specification.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]

# Lifecycle History
The landscape repository was initialized under the `aaif/aaif-landscape` GitHub repository to serve as the central open catalog for agentic AI tooling and foundation members.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]

[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]: Repository file `README.md` in `aaif/aaif-landscape`.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Foundation Code of Conduct
proposed_concept.description: Community standards, expected behaviors, reporting workflows, and jurisdiction scopes governing all AAIF boards, committees, working groups, and official events.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) Code of Conduct establishes community behavioral standards, expected interpersonal norms, and enforcement procedures designed to foster an inclusive, safe, and harassment-free environment across all Foundation activities [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588]. The policy mandates professional conduct across all foundation interactions regardless of personal characteristics, identity, or level of experience [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Applicability
The Code of Conduct governs participation across [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588]:
- Governing Board meetings
- Technical Committee ([`../governance/technical-committee.md`](../governance/technical-committee.md)) meetings
- Working Group meetings (such as [`../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md`](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md))
- Outreach Committee meetings
- Any other committee meetings and general foundation activities not otherwise governed by an independent technical project code of conduct

### AAIF Event Operations
In-person and virtual events produced by the AAIF with professional events staff are governed by the Linux Foundation Events Code of Conduct in conjunction with this foundation policy [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

### Technical Project Code of Conduct Boundaries
Technical projects hosted under the AAIF umbrella are organized as separate projects, and each project maintains its own code of conduct applying to participants in those specific codebases [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

## Expected and Prohibited Conduct
Community participants are expected to use welcoming and inclusive language, respect differing viewpoints, accept constructive criticism gracefully, and prioritize outcomes that benefit the community [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588]. Prohibited behaviors include verbal, physical, or visual harassment; discrimination based on protected characteristics; sexual attention or sexualized imagery; intimidation and stalking; sustained disruption of talks or discussions; personal attacks; and publishing private information without consent [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

# Lifecycle History
The foundation Code of Conduct was formally ratified and committed to the `aaif/foundation` repository as the foundational community standard governing foundation bodies and communications [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

# References
- Linux Foundation Events Code of Conduct: https://events.linuxfoundation.org/about/code-of-conduct/

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an AAIF technical body focused on defining comprehensive threat models, secure architectural patterns, cross-working-group security reviews, and privacy guidelines across the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. The working group evaluates emerging protocols, establishes baseline security taxonomies, and coordinates defensive architectural baselines for agentic workflows [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Charter Status
The working group's charter was submitted to the AAIF Technical Committee ([`../governance/technical-committee.md`](../governance/technical-committee.md)) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. Although an initial vote encountered procedural quorum delays due to infrastructure outages, the working group operates as approved under consensus given that no substantive objections were raised [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

## Workstreams and Deliverables
The working group executes its mandate through self-organizing asynchronous workstreams and scheduled milestone reviews [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]:
- **Cross-WG Taxonomy Collaboration**: Providing the initial draft security and privacy vocabulary as the baseline for joint cross-working-group terminology alignment alongside [`../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md`](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Protocol Security Tracking (MCP Interceptors)**: Evaluating proposals that introduce protocol hooks into the Model Context Protocol to support runtime data privacy controls and redaction [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Client Boundary Security (MCP Apps)**: Analyzing threat vectors arising when UI elements break client and browser boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Security Best Practices**: Developing implementation guidelines including [`../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md`](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) and [`../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md`](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md).

## Operating Cadence
To accommodate distributed participants across Americas, EMEA, and APAC time zones, bi-weekly all-hands meetings function as concise coordination checkpoints, while working updates and technical authoring transition to asynchronous channels and workstream-specific sessions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Lifecycle History
In April 2026, the working group presented its charter to the Technical Committee and agreed across working group chairs to use its security taxonomy draft as the inaugural cross-working-group collaboration deliverable [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, delegation frameworks, and trust evaluation mechanisms for AI agents across organizational boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group (I&T) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body advancing vendor-neutral, interoperable approaches for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]. Its core mission is establishing frameworks that allow agents to be discovered across disparate platforms, prove their operational provenance and principals, declare granular permissions, and record verifiable human approvals across organizational boundaries [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

The working group operates under the leadership of Chair Grant Miller [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c] and coordinates with adjacent foundation efforts, including the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md).

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's charter defines explicit in-scope and out-of-scope functional boundaries [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]:

- **In-Scope Responsibilities**:
  - *Agent Identity, Authentication, and Provenance*: Specifications and patterns for identifying agents, validating authentication credentials, and recording context such as operator identity and originating software stack [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].
  - *Delegation and Authority Chains*: Mechanisms detailing how agents represent human, team, role, or process principals [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].
  - *Authorization and Consent Models*: Protocols expressing short-lived, fine-grained access policies, time bounds, and explicit human consent gates [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].
  - *Trust Evaluation*: Frameworks for cross-organizational verification and policy evaluation before executing requested actions [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].
  - *Discovery and Metadata*: Trust-relevant metadata schemas supporting interoperability and agent registries [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].
  - *Contextual Coverage*: Enterprise and consumer deployment patterns [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

- **Out-of-Scope Boundaries**:
  - Formal standards development organization (SDO) ratification; the group informs and recommends rather than ratifying standards [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].
  - Comprehensive agent execution sandboxing and security controls, which are deferred to the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].
  - Standalone ethical frameworks or public policy positions disconnected from technical identity and trust representations [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].
  - Operating production identity infrastructure or commercial certification programs [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

# Lifecycle History
The working group established its formal charter outlining operational cadence, leadership terms, and boundary agreements to provide vendor-neutral identity foundations across AAIF initiatives [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Submission Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Operational guidelines governing working group proposal intake, membership tier eligibility restrictions, issue template requirements, and Technical Committee review cadences.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Submission Guidelines define the formal intake process and structural requirements for proposing new working groups to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) within the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c]. Proposals must be submitted via the designated GitHub issue template in the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository and undergo formal committee review under the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md) [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].

# Architecture / Specification
Proposals submitted to the Technical Committee must adhere to standardized metadata validation and organizational eligibility criteria [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c]:

## Submitter Validation and Intake
- **Organizational Affiliation**: The primary submitter must belong to an active AAIF Member Organization [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].
- **Membership Tier**: Submissions capture whether the proposing entity holds Platinum or Gold AAIF membership status [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].
- **Contact Details**: Submissions mandate full name, email address, role or title, and organizational affiliation [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].
- **Template Routing**: New proposals are labeled `New` and automatically assigned to community governance leadership upon submission [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].

## Proposal Form Structure
The intake template separates technical context from collateral attachments:
- **Resources**: Captures existing initiatives, prior art, and related efforts under `existing_work` [^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-2].
- **Supporting Materials**: Separately captures supplementary files and links under the distinct field `Supporting documents or attachments` (`supporting_documents`) [^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-2].

# Lifecycle History
The Technical Committee introduced an intake period notice stating that while working group proposals are actively accepted, formal committee reviews will not begin until June 1, 2026 [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c]. Template updates subsequently disambiguated field labels between existing art citations and supplementary attachments [^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-2].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Proposal Process establishes the governance procedure and technical criteria for onboarding open-source projects into the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]. Proposals are submitted through GitHub issue templates in the `aaif/project-proposals` repository for review by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) under the governing [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

# Architecture / Specification
The proposal intake process validates repository governance, community engagement, and licensing compliance while avoiding unnecessary barriers for early-stage candidate projects [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]:

## Submission Requirements
Candidate projects must provide core organizational metadata, architectural overviews, and intellectual property alignment:
- **Mandatory Disclosures**: Project scope, problem statement, current adoption metrics, contributor diversity, open-source license verification, and primary maintainer contacts [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].
- **Optional Supporting Elements**: In alignment with the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md), candidate projects are not required to provide a finalized public roadmap or an OpenSSF Best Practices badge at initial intake [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]. These fields are designated optional within the proposal form to ensure sandbox applicants are not prematurely blocked prior to formal admission [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

# Lifecycle History
In PR#23 of `aaif/project-proposals`, the project proposal template was corrected to mark the roadmap and OpenSSF badge fields as optional, eliminating a discrepancy where the template previously enforced mandatory checks contrary to the governing lifecycle policy [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, cross-boundary trace correlation, and agent behavior trace models.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body that convenes practitioners, vendors, and standards organizations to build a shared understanding of agent observability and telemetry conventions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d] Rather than creating a competing standards authority, the working group operates primarily as a coordination forum that aligns existing specifications—such as OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context—and directs technical efforts toward unresolved gaps.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]

# Architecture / Specification

## Mandate and Scope
The OT-WG addresses multi-turn, workflow-level agent visibility where raw LLM call tracing proves insufficient for auditing reasoning trajectories, tool invocations, and multi-modal transformations.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d] Core scope includes:
- Aligning and extending existing tracing specifications without introducing vendor-specific formats.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]
- Developing common conventions for agent session, workflow, and turn execution states, centered around the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]
- Tracing content lineage, fidelity, and grounding across tool and model boundaries, including [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) semantic convention integration.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]

## Guiding Principles
The group adheres to six core principles:
1. **Coordinate first, specify only when necessary**: Default to contributing upstream to established bodies.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]
2. **Interoperability over innovation**: Compose with existing ecosystem standards.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]
3. **Observable by default**: Ensure agent architectures instrument telemetry natively.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]
4. **Move at ecosystem speed**: Deliver iteratively on incremental deliverables.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]
5. **Adoption as key metric**: Value practical implementations over abstract designs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]
6. **Vendor and framework neutrality**: Guarantee equal architectural standing for all participants.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-04-15**: Working group ratified charter text.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]
- **2026-05-13**: Charter formally approved, led by primary contact Pavan Sudheendra.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]
- **2026-05-15**: Charter repository documentation updated.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing open threat models, shared taxonomies, design patterns, and cross-working group security review checklists.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security & Privacy Working Group (SPAA, Security & Privacy for Agentic AI) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across agent providers, consumers, and foundation working groups.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899] Chaired by Alex Frazer with Co-Chair Junjie Bu, the group develops open threat models, reusable containment patterns, and architectural review checklists to mitigate agent vulnerabilities such as prompt injection, confused deputy scenarios, tool invocation risks, and unauthorized memory access.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]

# Architecture / Specification

## Mandate and Scope
The working group treats security and privacy as a cross-cutting substrate intersecting all AAIF initiatives.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]

In-scope activity domains include:
- **Threat Modeling and Attack Analysis**: Documenting agentic failure modes and adversarial abuse cases.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]
- **Security Architecture and Design Patterns**: Establishing defensive runtime patterns including interceptors and hooks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]
- **Agent Control and Containment**: Defining execution boundaries, least-privilege tool access, and human-in-the-loop safeguards.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]
- **Data Protection and Privacy**: Addressing autonomous service traversal and sensitive data handling.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]
- **Cross-WG Collaboration**: Reviewing peer working group deliverables against a unified security baseline.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]

Explicitly out-of-scope areas include:
- Normative ethics, bias, and societal value judgments (deferred to Governance and Policy groups).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]
- Regulatory compliance interpretation or prescribing legal conformance.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]
- Formal certification programs for agentic systems or tools.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]

## Core Deliverable Roadmap
The group coordinates workstreams around several foundational artifacts:
1. **[Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md)**: Near-term gap analysis evaluating existing security frameworks against autonomous agents.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]
2. **[Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md)**: Practical review workflow socialized with other WG chairs to inspect emerging architectures.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Technical pattern catalog detailing concrete implementations such as protocol hooks and approval checkpoints.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]
4. **[Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)**: Advisory guide offering high-level architectural rules for system implementers.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]
5. **Taxonomy Contributions**: Initial security taxonomy work transitioned into the foundation-wide initiative under the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-04-29**: Working group charter draft finalized under pull request review.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]
- **2026-05-12**: Working group reconciled charter feedback and transitioned formal approval voting to the LFX platform.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]
- **2026-05-13**: Charter formal approval recorded.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Ecosystem Architecture Map is an interactive, CNCF Landscape2-powered market map that tracks and categorizes agent runtimes, protocols, security guardrails, observability frameworks, commerce rails, and regulatory environments across the agentic AI landscape[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]. Managed in collaboration with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the catalog provides a card-based interface for exploring open-source projects, foundation members, and external technologies[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape platform is governed by declarative YAML specifications and automated continuous integration pipelines deployed across foundation repositories:

- **Configuration and Display**: The presentation layer is governed by `settings.yml`, defining visual tokens (Slate 900 primary, Blue 500 secondary, Slate 800 navigation), card display options with logos and descriptions, and member tier categorization spanning Graduated, Incubating, Member, and External project tiers[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].
- **Dynamic Pull Request Preview**: Contribution workflows implement a pull request target automation using GitHub Script to generate ephemeral preview links via overlay parameters (`overlay-data`, `overlay-settings`, and `overlay-logos`) pointing to the fork and branch under evaluation[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00].
- **Schema Validation**: Automated GitHub Actions workflows invoke `cncf/landscape2-validate-action@v2` across both `landscape.yml` and `settings.yml` to enforce structural schema conformance on pull requests and merge groups prior to integration[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340].

# Lifecycle History
Originally seeded to catalog the evolving agentic AI ecosystem, configuration and deployment settings were standardized for Next.js static export on GitHub Pages under the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]. Continuous integration workflows were subsequently integrated into `aaif/aaif-landscape` to ensure automated validation and real-time pull request preview capabilities[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00][^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340].

# References
- [AAIF Taxonomy and Landscape Repository](https://github.com/aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape)
- [AAIF Landscape Repository](https://github.com/aaif/aaif-landscape)

# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an open-source interactive ecosystem map and directory cataloging open-source software, platforms, protocols, and foundational technologies across the agentic AI domain[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14]. Maintained by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the landscape visualizes project categories and tracks community momentum across foundation members and broader open-source initiatives.

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape taxonomy separates organizational membership from project classification through categorized grouping rules[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14]:

- **Agentic AI Project Watchlist**: Tracks leading open-source agentic AI repositories and emerging tools across the broader ecosystem, highlighting trending implementations and ecosystem adoption[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].
- **Decoupled Member and Project Groups**: Distinguishes member organizations from open-source projects via discrete grouping layers while maintaining bidirectional mapping and badges for Foundation member-backed projects[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].
- **Momentum Integration**: Supports automated telemetry and metric synchronization with the Agentic AI Momentum Dashboard hosted on LFX Insights to reflect commit cadence, contributors, and repository health[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].

# Lifecycle History
In PR #14, the landscape introduced the curated OSS project watchlist, decoupled Foundation members and technical projects into separate metadata groups, and established synchronization paths with LFX Insights[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Idea Submission Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Submission criteria and evaluation standards for Foundation members proposing new AAIF working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Idea Submission Guidelines govern how Agentic AI Foundation member organizations submit, structure, and advance proposals for new working groups[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]. Working groups represent structured, time-bound collaborations established to address technical challenges, develop specifications, and deliver actionable guidance critical to agentic AI systems.

# Architecture / Specification
Proposals submitted to the Foundation must conform to defined eligibility constraints and structured intake requirements[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]:

- **Submitter Eligibility**: Submissions are strictly restricted to Foundation member organizations in good standing across any active membership tier; submissions from outside Foundation membership are not reviewed[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
- **Core Proposal Requirements**: Submissions must document:
  1. *Submitter Information*: Affiliation, representative role, contact email, and leadership availability[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
  2. *Identity & Summary*: Concise name and a one-sentence non-jargon problem summary[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
  3. *Problem Statement & Purpose*: Clear articulation of the technical or operational gap and alignment with Foundation priorities[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
  4. *Scope & Deliverables*: Tangible target outputs including specifications, reference architectures, benchmarks, whitepapers, or tooling[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
  5. *Timeline & Cadence*: Charter duration, typically scoped between 12 and 24 months, with anticipated meeting cadences[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
  6. *Membership & Expertise*: Target stakeholder perspectives and committed participating organizations[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
  7. *Impact & Urgency*: Analysis of domain urgency and resource considerations[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
- **Review and Lifecycle Alignment**: Proposals are evaluated according to the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md) and governed by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

# Lifecycle History
Published in March 2026, the submission guidelines codified member eligibility rules, mandatory proposal sections, and 12–24 month charter timeframes[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]. In PR #4, external documentation links were verified and resolved to the primary foundation domain at aaif.io[^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-4].

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy defining entry requirements, stage progressions across Growth, Impact, and Emeritus, and annual review cycles for AAIF projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Lifecycle Policy defines the formal governance framework governing how open technical projects enter, advance through, and conclude their tenure within the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]. Governed by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the policy establishes objective entry criteria, progression expectations, and an annual review process to align open-source projects with the Foundation's technical mission.

# Architecture / Specification
Project progression is structured through explicit submission criteria and tiered maturity stages[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]:

- **Project Proposal Requirements**: Candidate projects must submit formal proposals via the project-proposals repository containing project origin, mission alignment, Technical Committee sponsor identification, OSI-approved permissive licensing, public repository links, automated release pipelines, open issue tracking, dependency licensing, core maintainer roster, and documented governance (`GOVERNANCE.md`)[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- **Maturity Stages**:
  - *Growth Stage*: Stage for early-stage or rapidly expanding projects demonstrating viable adoption, community growth, and technical utility under AAIF mentorship[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
  - *Impact Stage*: Stage for mature, production-grade projects demonstrating sustained multi-organizational governance, rigorous release cadences, and broad industry adoption[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
  - *Emeritus Stage*: Concluding stage for projects that have reached end-of-life, transitioned into archival maintenance, or ceased active community contributions[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171][^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].
- **Annual Review Process**: All accepted projects undergo periodic evaluations to assess governance health, active maintainership, community engagement, and suitability for stage advancement or graduation[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

# Lifecycle History
Effective March 18, 2026, the Project Lifecycle Policy established formal requirements for project onboarding, progression across Growth, Impact, and Emeritus tiers, and annual review checkpoints[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]. In PR #30, phrasing and typographical errors in the Emeritus Stage definitions and submission issue templates were corrected[^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol gap analyses, and reference architectures across agentic discovery, checkout, payments, and post-purchase lifecycles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group (AC WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body tasked with cataloging, aligning, and harmonizing open specifications, frameworks, and terminology for commerce workflows executed by AI agents on behalf of users, businesses, and software systems[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]. Chaired by Ilya Grigorik and Rahul Bansal, the group provides interoperability guidance and reference models across discovery, negotiation, checkout, payment orchestration, and post-purchase lifecycle interactions while remaining protocol-neutral and refraining from authoring competing commercial protocol specifications[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group focuses on interfaces, signals, and interoperability patterns between agentic systems and the broader commerce stack while treating underlying system implementations as out of scope[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]. Key functional areas within scope include:

- **Discovery & Negotiation**: Interfaces enabling agents and merchants to query offers, catalog availability, commercial terms, and fulfillment options[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Cart & Checkout**: Cart composition, price validation, and checkout handoff between agent and merchant infrastructure[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Identity & Delegated Authority**: Buyer identity verification, agent authority scoping, and consent conveyance, developed in collaboration with [Identity and Trust](identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Agentic Payments**: Interfaces between agents, digital wallets, and payment rails for intent, authorization, and settlement signals[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Fraud Signaling & Boundaries**: Risk posture exchange, human-in-the-loop escalation criteria, autonomy boundary representation, and post-purchase dispute signaling[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

Explicitly out of scope are payment rail operations, fraud detection engines, identity provider internals, UI/hardware design, and authoring competing commerce protocol standards[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Lifecycle History

The charter of the Agentic Commerce Working Group was formally approved on May 15, 2026[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# References

- [Identity and Trust Working Group](identity-and-trust.md)
- [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](workflows-and-process-integration.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing open threat models, shared taxonomies, design patterns, and cross-working group security review procedures for autonomous and agentic systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. The group coordinates vulnerability and boundary analyses across foundational model interactions, execution sandboxes, and multi-agent communications[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical deliverables across five primary workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]:

- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: Evaluates industry security frameworks and establishes agentic threat modeling methodologies, developed in close coordination with [Taxonomy and Landscape](taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: Practical implementation guidance covering sandboxing, credential isolation, and defense-in-depth patterns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Architectural and operational patterns addressing autonomy boundaries and containment controls[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Standardized review checklist applied to architectures and specifications from sibling working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Integration**: Alignment with Foundation-wide terminology and ecosystem mapping, co-chaired by Junjie Bu[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Lifecycle History

The working group charter was formally ratified in May 2026 under the leadership of Alex Frazer[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. Following charter approval, workstream lead self-selection was initiated and deliverable timelines were extended by approximately one month to accommodate initial governance setup[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# References

- [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md)
- [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md)

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure and governance gates governing project intake, Technical Committee voting thresholds, status tracking, and stage classification for AAIF-hosted projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Project Proposal Process defines the official intake, evaluation, and approval workflow for open-source software initiatives applying to become foundation-hosted projects under the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]. Administered via the public project proposals repository, the procedure establishes criteria for classification into Growth or Impact stages and specifies Technical Committee voting requirements[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

# Architecture / Specification

The proposal review pipeline enforces sequential governance stages and tracking conventions[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]:

- **Submission & Intake**: Candidates complete a standardized project proposal application form against requirements outlined in the project lifecycle documentation[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6][^evt-project-proposals-pr-35]. Submitted applications are placed in the backlog under the `New` label[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Triage & Presentation**: Applicants prepare a formal review presentation supported by AAIF staff and schedule a review session during a Technical Committee meeting[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]. Intermediate statuses include `Waiting on Comment` for clarifications and `Too Early` for projects requiring further maturity[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Review & Voting Gate**: The [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) reviews the project and classifies it as either a Growth or Impact project[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]. Acceptance requires an absolute majority vote (>50%) of all Technical Committee members, followed by referral to the Governing Board for final sign-off[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Reapplication Rules**: Applications assigned the `Declined` status may reapply after addressing reviewer feedback, with reapplication permitted as early as three months following the vote if tangible progress is demonstrated[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Membership Neutrality**: Project acceptance does not mandate foundation membership by the contributing organization, nor does project hosting confer membership tier status or Governing Board seats on contributors[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

# References

- [Project Lifecycle Policy](project-lifecycle-policy.md)
- [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation initiative responsible for harmonizing conceptual terminology across foundation working groups and curating the interactive ecosystem landscape map[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]. Operating via asynchronous, pull-request-driven contributions, the workstream coordinates domain taxonomies across runtimes, security, observability, commerce, and governance[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

# Architecture / Specification

The landscape architecture structures the agentic AI ecosystem into seven primary categories, each aligned with specific foundation working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]:

1. **Agent Runtimes, Frameworks & Workflow Orchestration**: Aligned with [Workflows and Process Integration](workflows-and-process-integration.md) and [Accuracy and Reliability](accuracy-and-reliability.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
2. **Protocols & Discovery Registries**: Aligned with [Identity and Trust](identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
3. **Security Guardrails & Firewalls**: Aligned with [Security and Privacy](security-and-privacy.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
4. **Observability & Tracing Telemetry**: Aligned with [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
5. **Agentic Commerce & Wallets**: Aligned with [Agentic Commerce](agentic-commerce.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
6. **Global Governance & Regulatory Regimes**: Aligned with [Governance, Risk and Regulatory Alignment](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
7. **Agent Evaluation & Benchmarking Harnesses**: Aligned with [Accuracy and Reliability](accuracy-and-reliability.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

# Lifecycle History

In May 2026, Junjie Bu was appointed co-chair of the Taxonomy workstream and chair of the Landscape workstream to formalize cross-group alignment and tooling surveys[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# References

- [Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md)
- [Security and Privacy Working Group](security-and-privacy.md)
- [Agentic Commerce Working Group](agentic-commerce.md)

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Submission Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Submission workflow, evaluation criteria, voting thresholds, and tracking statuses for proposing new AAIF working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Submission Guidelines define the formal intake, evaluation, and approval process for chartering new working groups under the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]. Any prospective working group must submit a structured application to ensure alignment with foundation goals, establish an initial leadership team, and undergo technical review.

# Architecture / Specification

## Submission and Intake Process
Proposals to form a new working group are submitted via GitHub issue forms in the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository using the standardized working group proposal template[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]. Submitted proposals are automatically ingested onto the public Working Group Proposals tracking board and placed in the backlog for triage[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

## Evaluation and Voting Governance
Working group proposals are reviewed and voted on by the Technical Committee ([governance/technical-committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)) during scheduled meetings[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]:
- **Review Scheduling**: Triage places submitted proposals onto the agenda for an upcoming TC meeting.
- **Voting Threshold**: Acceptance requires a simple majority vote of all members of the Technical Committee[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
- **Governing Board Ratification**: Acceptance by the Technical Committee is subject to final approval by the AAIF Governing Board[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

## Proposal Status Lifecycle
Proposal progression is tracked using standard repository issue labels[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]:
- `New`: The proposal is newly submitted and queued in the triage backlog.
- `Waiting on Comment`: Reviewers have posted inquiries requiring submitter clarification or additional detail.
- `Too Early`: The proposal is deemed premature; guidance is provided for potential reapplication.
- `Declined`: The proposal has been declined by the TC, with explanatory feedback recorded in issue comments.
- `Approved`: The proposal has met all intake criteria and achieved requisite approvals.

# References
- [Policies: Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md)
- [Governance: Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes vendor-neutral threat models, architectural security patterns, implementation baselines, and review frameworks for autonomous AI agents and harnesses[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]. Operating across specialized workstreams, the group addresses vulnerabilities unique to agentic execution including prompt injection, credential exposure, unsafe tool invocation, and attestation.

# Architecture / Specification

## Active Workstreams and Leadership
The working group executes its charter through distinct workstreams led by subject matter specialists[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]:
- **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, providing baseline checklists for evaluating cross-working group architectures and standards[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Matthew Khouzam and Fernando Lucktemberg, maintaining actionable deployment and sandboxing practices[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, benchmarking existing security frameworks against agentic requirements[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Sagar Dashora and Dan Kommatas, codifying architectural patterns for containment and control[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

## Cross-Working Group Coordination
The group actively delegates liaisons to cross-cutting foundation initiatives. Jay White and Katherine Druckman serve as the designated delegates representing Security and Privacy within the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]. In addition, the group maintains an asynchronous monthly progress cadence via GitHub pull requests to report to the Technical Committee ([governance/technical-committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)) without creating blocking approval bottlenecks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

# References
- [Guidelines: Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md)
- [Guidelines: Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, cross-boundary tracing, and reasoning observability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group establishes vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, distributed tracing conventions, and evaluation frameworks for autonomous agent architectures and multi-agent coordination[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]. The group addresses cross-boundary instrumentation across language models, harness runtimes, Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool servers, and direct subprocess execution.

# Architecture / Specification

## Focus Groups
Work within the group is organized into focused sub-groups addressing specific operational scopes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]:
- **Observability and Multi-Agentic Systems**: Led by Ty, conducting weekly sessions analyzing multi-agent trace propagation and distributed interaction topologies[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].
- **Observability and Protocols**: Led by Matthew, examining telemetry integration across agent protocol boundaries, including MCP and agent gateway mediation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].
- **Agentic Reasoning**: Organized by Pavan in coordination with Richard and Kevin, investigating trace primitives and observability frameworks for internal planning and reasoning loops[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

## Collaboration and Governance Operations
The working group conducts technical drafting and review asynchronously through GitHub issues and pull requests, transitioning from legacy shared documents to structured version-controlled artifacts[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]. It coordinates with the cross-cutting [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and reports monthly milestone progress to the Technical Committee ([governance/technical-committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)) using standardized update templates[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

# References
- [Resources: Cross-Boundary Observability Model](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md)
- [Resources: Agent MCP Server Boundary](../resources/agent-mcp-server-boundary.md)
- [Working Groups: Taxonomy and Landscape](taxonomy-and-landscape.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group is a cross-cutting foundational initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation charged with harmonizing terminology, resolving conceptual conflicts across working groups, and curating the open agentic ecosystem landscape[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

# Architecture / Specification

## Operating Model and Governance
Led by Junjie Bu, the workstream operates as a horizontal clearinghouse rather than an isolated vertical group[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]:
- **Delegate Representation**: Every AAIF working group designates official delegates to review terminology, surface conflicting definitions, and represent domain nuances[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]. For example, Jay White and Katherine Druckman serve as the confirmed delegates from the [Security and Privacy Working Group](security-and-privacy.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
- **Open Contribution via Git**: All definitions and landscape data are maintained as decoupled records that contributors modify directly through GitHub pull requests and issues, ensuring asynchronous resolution and traceable semantic history[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

## Coordination Functions
The workstream reconciles schema and vocabulary inconsistencies across AAIF projects, establishing shared ontology primitives that ground security threat models, observability telemetry schemas, and workflow patterns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
