proposed_concept.title: Working Group Reporting Template
proposed_concept.description: Standardized monthly reporting template and pull request workflow for Agentic AI Foundation working groups to provide asynchronous operational updates to the Technical Committee.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Working Group Reporting Template standardizes monthly operational reporting across all technical working groups and workstreams within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF). Designed to facilitate asynchronous governance, each group documents monthly achievements, impediments, and resource requests in a consistent markdown structure submitted for review by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].

Reports are tracked directly within each group's repository, establishing an auditable historical record of working group trajectory while minimizing administrative overhead for group chairs and foundation leadership[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-pr-4]. Automated synthesis tools such as [aaif-wg-monthly-report](../skills/aaif-wg-monthly-report.md) leverage this uniform format to compile status digests.

# Architecture / Specification

## Submission and Review Workflow

1. **File Location**: Working groups copy `reporting/TEMPLATE.md` to `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md` (for example, `reporting/2026-06-report.md`)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].
2. **Pull Request Protocol**: A pull request is created against the working group repository titled `[Report] <WG name> – <Month YYYY>`[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].
3. **Review Assignment**: The Technical Committee (or designated TC GitHub review team) is requested for review[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].
4. **Timelines and Deadlines**: Reports are due by the last business day of the reporting month. The formal TC review window remains open for 7 calendar days after submission[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].
5. **Merge Conditions**: The report PR is merged once the TC approves it or when the 7-day review window closes, whichever occurs sooner[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].

## Template Structure

Every report contains a standardized header and six operational sections[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]:

- **Header Metadata**: WG name, reporting period (`Month YYYY`), active chair(s), and submission date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
- **Summary**: Two to three concise sentences capturing the month's progress at a glance.
- **Progress Against Objectives**: Concrete accomplishments and deliverables shipped during the period, explicitly tied back to charter objectives.
- **Blockers and Risks**: Operational hurdles or risks requiring TC awareness (explicitly marked "None this month" when clear).
- **Decisions Needed from the TC**: Explicit, actionable requests requiring TC voting or governance intervention (marked "None" if not applicable).
- **Next Month's Focus**: The top two or three priorities targeted for the upcoming month.
- **Metrics / Links**: Hyperlinks to relevant PRs, issues, releases, meeting notes, and dashboards.

## Adoption Across Working Groups

The reporting standard is deployed across AAIF bodies and maintained by designated co-chairs:

- [WG Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md): Co-chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].
- [WG Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md): Co-chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a].
- [WS Taxonomy & Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md): Co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-9677055e316b-9ddc8f32].
- [WG Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md): Co-chaired by Grant Miller (IBM) and Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-9677055e316b-2e851e23].
- [WG Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md): Co-chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-9677055e316b-dc950981].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Monthly Reporting Template
proposed_concept.description: Standardized reporting template and pull request submission procedure governing asynchronous Technical Committee reviews across AAIF working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Monthly Reporting Template standardizes how Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) working groups report operational progress, blockers, risks, and resource requests to the Technical Committee.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-9677055e316b-188b9d10] Reports are submitted via pull requests directly to individual working group repositories and evaluated asynchronously by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f]

# Architecture / Specification

## Submission Workflow and Lifecycle
1. **File Placement**: Groups copy the canonical `reporting/TEMPLATE.md` to `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md` (e.g., `reporting/2026-06-report.md`).[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-9677055e316b-188b9d10]
2. **Pull Request Staging**: A pull request is opened against the working group repository titled `[Report] <WG name> – <Month YYYY>` with the Technical Committee team designated as reviewers.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f]
3. **Deadlines and Review Windows**: Reports are due by the final business day of the reporting month.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-9677055e316b-188b9d10] The formal review window spans seven calendar days following submission.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f]
4. **Approval and Merge**: Reports merge upon explicit Technical Committee sign-off or upon expiration of the seven-day review window, whichever occurs first.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-9677055e316b-188b9d10]

## Template Sections
Standardized reports contain the following mandatory sections:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f]
- **Metadata**: Working group name, reporting period, chairs, and submission date.
- **Summary**: High-level two- to three-sentence narrative capturing monthly progress.
- **Progress Against Objectives**: Concrete deliverables and milestones tied to charter goals.
- **Blockers and Risks**: Operational obstacles or governance impediments requiring awareness.
- **Decisions Needed from the TC**: Specific actionable decisions requested from the committee.
- **Next Month's Focus**: Top two to three forward-looking priorities.
- **Metrics / Links**: References to pull requests, issues, releases, and meeting notes.

# Lifecycle History

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body developing open threat models, shared taxonomies, design patterns, and governance checklists to secure agent runtimes, tool integrations, and multi-agent systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423] The working group operates structured repository workflows across charters, deliverables, and meeting records under strict review and publication gates.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]

# Architecture / Specification

## Repository Structure and Operational Conventions
The working group organizes documentation and workstreams within dedicated subdirectories governed by localized agent instruction files:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423]
- `charter/`: Contains foundational working group charter documents, retaining a `DRAFT.md` prefix until formally ratified by recorded group vote.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423]
- `deliverables/`: Houses formal threat taxonomies, reference architectures, and design pattern specifications.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]
- `meeting-notes/`: Chronological meeting records formatted as `YYYY-MM-DD.md` tracking agendas, decisions, action items, and recording links.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-eb9c68e792e7-3538ca31]

## Deliverable Lifecycle States
Deliverables within the working group transition through three explicit statuses:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]
- **Draft**: Work in progress prefixed with `DRAFT-` (e.g., `DRAFT-threat-model-framework.md`).
- **Final**: Approved deliverables stripped of the `DRAFT-` prefix. Promotion from Draft to Final strictly requires an explicit, recorded decision in a corresponding meeting notes file.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]
- **Moved**: Artifacts transferred to cross-working group workstreams or external repositories. The original file is retained as a redirect notice to preserve inbound hyperlinks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]

## Current Initiatives and Proposals
The group maintains active deliverables covering agentic threat taxonomies, hooks, checkpoints, prompt injection defense, and red teaming practices.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-6] External community proposals under review include cross-referencing OWASP Agentic Systems Incidents (ASI01-09) vectors against baseline threat terms, defining static analysis disciplines distinct from runtime red teaming, and formalizing human-in-the-loop preview and confirmation patterns across consumer messaging surfaces.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-6]

# Lifecycle History
Operating as an active technical working group within the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) framework, collaborating with cross-cutting workstreams including the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body tasked with establishing open threat models, security design patterns, actionable implementation guides, and security assessment checklists across the agentic ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]. Operating as an intersecting review and advisory layer across AAIF, the working group systematically evaluates agent identity delegation, behavioral telemetry, tool mediation, and commerce safety across peer working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical agenda into four active workstreams:
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling**: Evaluates existing frameworks (including CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF) for agentic-specific threats such as multi-agent persuasion, tool invocation vulnerabilities, delegated authorization boundaries, and supply-chain integrity [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]. Led by Alon Mazor (Ocean Security) and Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Curates reusable patterns and anti-patterns spanning hooks, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, privacy-preserving execution, blast radius containment, secure memory lifecycles, and runtime containment switches [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]. Led by Dan Kommatas (Circle) and Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Develops actionable guidance on secrets management, tool invocation guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and incident forensics [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]. Led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55].
- **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Defines an operational review workflow auditing peer group deliverables from [Identity and Trust](identity-and-trust.md), [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md), and [Agentic Commerce](agentic-commerce.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]. Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy (Global Payments) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].

# Lifecycle History
On 2026-06-22, the working group's standalone Taxonomy of Terms and Definitions workstream was formally merged into the cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) workstream chaired by Junjie Bu [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7]. Jay White (Microsoft) and Katherine Druckman (JetBrains) represent the SP WG as designated taxonomy delegates [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body established to identify unique security and privacy threats in agentic architectures, publish defensible design patterns, create actionable builder guides, and conduct cross-working group security reviews [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5].

The working group operates openly in public GitHub repositories as its primary system of record for mature deliverables, while coordinating cross-industry engagement with bodies including OWASP ASI, IETF, and MCP ACS [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical output across four active workstreams and one transitioned initiative [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]:

- **Threat Modeling**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, conducting comparative gap analysis of existing frameworks (CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, NIST AI RMF) against agentic risks such as memory poisoning, tool invocation, blast radius containment, excessive agency, and delegated authorization boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing prescriptive builder guidance and curated external operational references [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, curating reusable security and privacy patterns structured by problem, context, solution, and trade-offs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing lightweight security and privacy review criteria for evaluating deliverables produced by other AAIF working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Integration**: Original terminology definitions drafted within the group were contributed to and merged into the centralized cross-WG initiative led by Junjie Bu, with Jay White and Katherine Druckman serving as the group's designated delegates [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# Lifecycle History
The working group initially incubated taxonomy definitions before elevating the effort to the cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](./taxonomy-and-landscape.md) in May and June 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. In June 2026, the working group transitioned its repositories to public visibility, formalized its dedicated `workstreams/` directory structure, and established regular Technical Committee monthly reporting updates [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream harmonizing agentic AI terminology across vertical working groups and maintaining the foundation-wide taxonomy.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is an Agentic AI Foundation initiative led by Junjie Bu responsible for harmonizing agentic AI terminology, eliminating duplicate definitions, and curating an authoritative foundation-wide taxonomy across all working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

The workstream operates centrally through the `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` repository, synchronizing weekly and conducting primary harmonization work asynchronously across designated working group delegates [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

# Architecture / Specification
The taxonomy intake and harmonization model gathers 10 to 20 key terms from each vertical working group into a unified vocabulary, addressing domain-specific extensions and semantic alignment [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]:

- **Working Group Delegates**: Specific delegates represent vertical groups in harmonization discussions, such as Jay White and Katherine Druckman representing the [Security and Privacy Working Group](./security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **Agent Archetypes**: Capability-based classifications grouping agent types by operational characteristics, such as tool use, network access, and blast radius boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Cross-Group Harmonization Slices**: Vertical working groups align internal vocabularies against the taxonomy schema; for example, the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](./accuracy-and-reliability.md) reviews partitioned JSON topic slices covering system boundaries, reliability dimensions, grounding, failure modes, metrics, and evaluation ecosystems [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-4], while the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](./observability-and-traceability.md) coordinates plane models (orchestration, execution, protocol, reasoning) and OpenTelemetry alignment [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].

# Lifecycle History
Originally originating within the Security and Privacy Working Group, the taxonomy effort was elevated to an AAIF-wide initiative in May 2026, with Junjie Bu appointed as lead [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. In June 2026, working groups formalized delegate appointments and integrated cross-cutting topics, including agent archetypes and runtime failure classifications [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation framework capturing causal agent execution, tool invocations, approval states, and cross-boundary protocol spans.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and correlation specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to capture causal agent execution, decision chains, tool invocations, and environmental side effects across heterogeneous agent frameworks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12].

The model defines core dimensions spanning execution structure, reasoning and planning, and outcomes and effects, while maintaining strict alignment guardrails with upstream standards like OpenTelemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification crosswalks core observability planes with behavioral trace dimensions to guarantee comprehensive runtime visibility [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]:

## Observability Planes and Trace Dimensions
- **Taxonomy Planes**:
  - *Orchestration Plane*: Manages agent lifecycle, session continuity, subagent fan-out, and task decomposition [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].
  - *Execution Plane*: Tracks deterministic workflow execution, tool calls, subprocesses, and runtime resource operations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].
  - *Protocol Plane*: Monitors wire exchanges, transport sessions, and message delivery across interfaces such as MCP and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocols [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].
  - *Reasoning and Context Plane*: Instruments model context windows, prompt assembly, scratchpad tokens, and intermediate inference rationale [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].
- **Core Dimensions Crosswalk**: Maps these planes into three unified trace dimensions:
  1. *Execution Structure*: Directed causal graphs linking parent workflows, child agents, and tool invocations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].
  2. *Reasoning and Planning*: Intermediate rationale steps, plan mutations, and prompt context transitions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].
  3. *Outcomes and Effects*: Observed environmental state alterations, transaction commitments, and authorization checkpoint decisions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].

## Standardization Decision Framework
To prevent premature specification fragmentation, the working group governs the Agent Behavior Trace Model through a formal evaluation pathway [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12]:
- **Evaluation Pathway**: Systematic gap analysis determining whether to adopt an existing standard, extend an established specification (such as OpenTelemetry semantic conventions), or author a novel AAIF specification only when critical architectural gaps exist [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12].
- **Alignment Guardrails**: AAIF extensions are explicitly isolated as supplemental attributes rather than replacing core OpenTelemetry primitives [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing vendor-neutral telemetry standards, execution trace schemas, and cross-boundary visibility frameworks for agentic systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4] The group defines data models and capture conventions that trace multi-agent orchestration, context assembly, and tool interactions across infrastructure and protocol boundaries.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical investigations into four primary focus groups:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]
- **LLM Primitives**: Evaluates model-level interactions, prompt/response telemetry, white-box tracing methods, and foundational landscape surveys and gap analyses.
- **Agent State and Context**: Investigates runtime memory, context retention, and state synchronization across agent task cycles.
- **Orchestration and Coordination**: Analyzes multi-agent task delegation, scheduling, and protocol boundaries.
- **Agentic Reasoning**: Explores behavioral tracking, intermediate thought-step tracing, and decision-tree transparency.

The working group coordinates technical overlaps with cross-cutting AAIF specifications, including evaluating telemetry correlations with the [Agentic Resource Discovery Specification](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md), refining core terms with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), and standardizing deliverables such as [Agent Observability Prior Work](../resources/agent-observability-prior-work.md) and [Agent Observability Use Cases](../resources/agent-observability-use-cases.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-25**: The working group confirmed continued use of Discord for real-time collaboration, opened its public GitHub repository with Kanban project boards for focus group tracking, scheduled biweekly 5–15 minute community presentation slots, and targeted late-July completion for the LLM primitives landscape survey and gap analysis.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]

# Overview
AgentGateway is an open-source traffic mediation and policy enforcement proxy designed to manage Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent (A2A) communications.[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-17] Cataloged as an Agentic AI Foundation member project within the [Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md), it acts as an intermediary layer between agents, models, and external tools to govern data flow and enforce runtime boundaries.

# Architecture / Specification
AgentGateway provides protocol-aware routing, authentication, and policy enforcement across heterogeneous agent surfaces. It mediates client-to-agent and tool-to-agent interactions, enabling organizations to inspect, shape, and secure traffic without modifying agent runtime code or downstream endpoints.

# Lifecycle History

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing failure taxonomies, evaluation benchmarks, recovery specifications, and architectural patterns for dependable agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group (ARWG) advances the mission of the Agentic AI Foundation by establishing standards, evaluation benchmarks, and engineering patterns necessary for autonomous agents to operate reliably under real-world enterprise constraints [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. The working group addresses non-deterministic agentic behavior and the lack of visibility into system quality by classifying failure categories, defining resilience mechanisms, and formalizing intervention boundaries [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

ARWG operates under the leadership of co-chairs Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid), following formal charter approval on May 15, 2026 [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44] [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

# Architecture / Specification

### Scope Boundaries

The technical remit of the ARWG spans three primary domains [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]:
- **Accuracy & Reliability Frameworks**: Defining evaluation dimensions, failure modes, metrics, and quality thresholds for autonomous workloads.
- **Reliable Architecture Patterns**: Proactive structural requirements, verification loops, and grounding mechanisms tied to authoritative data sources.
- **Recovery and Corrective Actions**: Safe-state restoration, state rollback, automated compensation actions, and human intervention handoff triggers.

Explicitly excluded from scope are foundation model internals and pre-training, commercial platform tooling, domain-specific legal compliance, production orchestrator development, and trace log emission formats (which are formally delegated to the Observability and Traceability Working Group) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

### Deliverables and Cross-Group Coordination

The canonical work breakdown structure is organized into deliverables D1 through D6 alongside internal baseline I1 [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-6]:
- **D1 (Taxonomy & Architectural Frame)**: Structural framing for accuracy and reliability terminology, covering evaluation subjects, output quality, grounding, symptoms, root causes, and correction mechanisms [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]. ARWG coordinates directly with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) via dedicated liaisons [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].
- **D2 (Gap Analysis & Benchmark Survey)**: Applied evidence report led by enterprise personas (product managers, operations, evaluators, and data scientists) identifying tooling and interoperability gaps in production systems [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].
- **D6 (Evaluation Protocol)**: Downstream evaluation and testing specification informed directly by the D2 gap synthesis [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

ARWG maintains biweekly plenary meetings alternating with deliverable working sessions, collaborating closely with [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) on signal contracts [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy & Landscape Meeting Notes Operational Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Standardized instructions, file naming conventions, workflow steps, and communication style constraints for Taxonomy and Landscape meeting notes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

This guideline defines canonical agent instructions and operational procedures for generating and publishing meeting notes in the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream repository [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea]. It standardizes file naming, cross-linking in the primary index, section retention for empty content, and strict prose tone boundaries.

# Architecture / Specification

### File Naming and Structure

Notes must be saved under `YYYY-MM-DD.md` matching the meeting date [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea]. Content is generated by instantiating `TEMPLATE.md` with the following mandatory sections:
- **Resources**: Direct references to AI summaries, meeting transcripts, and recordings.
- **Topics Discussed**: High-level subjects formatted in concise 1-2 sentence bullet points.
- **Decisions**: Explicit policy or technical conclusions reached during the session.
- **Deliverables**: Tangible assets identified or assigned during the meeting.
- **Action Items**: Structured table specifying Task Owner, Description, and Due Date.

Sections lacking discussion or output must explicitly retain their heading and state `None.` rather than being omitted [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea].

### Indexing Workflow

Upon generating a meeting note, authors must update the repository `README.md` index table [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea]:
1. Insert a new row immediately below the table header to preserve reverse-chronological order.
2. Include the meeting date, a relative link titled `Full notes`, and a 1-2 sentence overview of the agenda.

### Communication Style Constraints

All notes, commits, pull request narratives, and automated agent interactions must respect explicit stylistic boundaries [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea]:
- Avoid contrastive language and partial clauses.
- Avoid line breaks using markdown horizontal rules.
- Maintain a direct, neutral voice that balances professional precision with approachable phrasing.
- Omit sycophantic or hollow praise.

References to unimplemented structures such as `recipes/`, `prompts/`, and `docs/` have been removed to align documentation with actual repository layout [^evt-public-agents-pr-2].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream harmonizing agentic AI terminology across vertical working groups and maintaining the foundation-wide ecosystem directory.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting body within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with establishing a shared vocabulary across all working groups and maintaining an ecosystem directory of member initiatives and external agentic technologies [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. By standardizing terminology and cataloging the ecosystem, the workstream eliminates siloed vocabularies, reconciles overlapping definitions, and prevents duplicated research across working groups such as [Accuracy and Reliability](accuracy-and-reliability.md), [Security and Privacy](security-and-privacy.md), and [Workflows and Process Integration](workflows-and-process-integration.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].

# Architecture / Specification

## Dual Metadata Schemas and Data Architecture
The workstream operates a decoupled data architecture that separates data storage from presentation web portals [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]:
- **Taxonomy Vocabulary**: Utilizes a SKOS-Lite (Simple Knowledge Organization System) metadata schema to capture concept definitions, cross-references, and notes [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. Each taxonomy entry incorporates both a concise summary for quick scanning and a comprehensive description field with scope notes to resolve ambiguity [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]. Schemas support citation tracking in notes to maintain definition provenance [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].
- **Ecosystem Landscape**: Utilizes CNCF-style metadata schemas to catalogue and display entities within the [Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md), explicitly differentiating between member-driven initiatives and external ecosystem projects [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985]. The directory integrates with the existing `landscape.aif.io` deployment while exploring a dedicated taxonomy domain [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].

## Governance and Contribution Workflow
Contributions follow an asynchronous, pull-request-driven lifecycle governed by working group delegates and domain editors [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]:
- **Working Group Representation**: Each vertical working group appoints one to two active delegates who constitute the core review team [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].
- **Conflict Resolution and Domain Editors**: Cross-cutting and conflicting terminology must be reviewed and approved by designated domain editors before merging [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].
- **Phased Intake and Alignment**: Term collection proceeds through collaborative offline whiteboards and spreadsheets before terms are submitted as individual pull requests [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]. Definitions must align with international standards such as ISO and NIST where applicable, documenting any deliberate deviations [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].
- **Style and AI Policies**: Terminology authoring follows a standardized style guide and an explicit AI usage policy requiring human curation and oversight [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].

## Reporting Procedures
The workstream submits monthly progress updates to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) by the final business day of each calendar month using the standardized reporting template [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b]. The Technical Committee has a seven-calendar-day asynchronous review window, after which reports are merged upon sign-off or window closure [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b].

# Lifecycle History
The workstream kicked off on May 21, 2026, establishing its initial weekly Monday meeting cadence and agreeing on a PR-driven contribution model using SKOS-Lite and CNCF schema baselines [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. On June 1, 2026, the team confirmed integration plans with `landscape.aif.io` and dual-level taxonomy definitions [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]. On June 8, 2026, charter updates incorporated conflict resolution metrics, delegate appointments, and an agreement to treat high-level boundary definitions as iterative deliverables [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985]. On June 15, 2026, existing unreviewed definitions were reset to formal pull requests, and standard ISO/NIST alignment was mandated [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90]. On June 22, 2026, the workstream announced the formal merger and approval of its charter and initiated universal term identification and agent boundary definition reviews [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Reporting Template and Instructions
proposed_concept.description: Standardized reporting template, monthly review timeline, pull request workflow, and communication style rules governing working group reporting to the Technical Committee.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Reporting Template establishes the required format, monthly cadence, pull request workflow, and editorial style for periodic updates submitted by AAIF working groups and workstreams to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b]. The process enables asynchronous governance, tracks progress against annual charter milestones, and surfaces formal decision requests requiring committee action [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b].

# Architecture / Specification

## Cadence and Review Windows
- **Submission Deadline**: Working groups must submit one report per calendar month by the last business day of the reporting month [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b].
- **File Naming Convention**: Each report file is named `YYYY-MM-report.md` (e.g., `2026-06-report.md`) within the group's `reporting/` directory [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b].
- **Review Window**: The Technical Committee review window remains open for seven calendar days following pull request submission [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b].
- **Merge Condition**: Reports are merged when the Technical Committee formally signs off or when the seven-day review window closes, whichever occurs first [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b].

## Pull Request Submission Workflow
Agents or human contributors generating reports must follow a defined procedural pipeline [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b]:
1. Copy `TEMPLATE.md` to `YYYY-MM-report.md` and remove template instruction comment blocks.
2. Populate the header with reporting period (`Month YYYY`) and submission date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
3. Draft a 2–3 sentence executive summary capturing progress at a glance.
4. Document progress against approved charter objectives, active blockers or risks, explicit decisions requested from the Technical Committee, and priorities for the following month.
5. Compile reference links to relevant pull requests, issues, releases, and meeting notes.
6. Submit a pull request titled `[Report] <Group Name> – Month YYYY` assigning the Technical Committee GitHub review team.
7. Update the repository `README.md` reporting table with a top-inserted row containing the period, report link, and summary.

## Editorial and Communication Style Rules
All reporting documents, pull request descriptions, and commit messages must adhere to specific communication constraints [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b]:
- Content must remain short, scannable, and formatted as concise bullet points rather than dense paragraphs.
- Empty sections must retain their headings and display "None." or "None this month." to preserve structural consistency.
- Avoid contrastive phrasing, partial clauses, and sycophantic language.
- Use complete, naturally flowing sentences maintaining a professional yet approachable tone.
- Do not insert horizontal rules for visual line breaks.

# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive ecosystem directory and catalog tracking agentic AI projects, member initiatives, and open-source tools across the industry [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]. Maintained by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the landscape establishes standard categorization across frameworks, infrastructure layers, protocols, and developer tooling to eliminate terminology silos and prevent duplicated research [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0].

# Architecture / Specification

## Data Model and Schema Architecture
- **CNCF Landscape Tool Format**: The directory uses the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) landscape tool metadata format as its baseline schema [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].
- **Decoupled Data Architecture**: Metadata files are managed separately from presentation web portals, enabling an asynchronous, pull-request-driven intake and curation workflow [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].
- **Entity Classification**: The catalog explicitly distinguishes between member-driven foundation projects and external third-party entities [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].
- **Deployment Target**: The landscape directory is integrated with the `landscape.aif.io` infrastructure, aligning foundation mapping efforts into a unified portal [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].

## Contribution Lifecycle
New technology additions and metadata updates are submitted via pull requests following community review guidelines [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]. Working group delegates and designated domain editors review entries to verify project boundaries, validate metadata attributes, and prevent catalog duplication [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream harmonizing agentic AI terminology across vertical working groups and maintaining an interactive ecosystem landscape.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) initiative charged with establishing shared terminological clarity across all technical working groups and delivering an open landscape directory of the agentic AI software ecosystem [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]. Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream coordinates appointed delegates from across AAIF's vertical bodies [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance & Contribution Pipeline

The workstream operates on a structured asynchronous governance pipeline backed by formal data specifications [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]:
- **SKOS-Lite Schema**: A simplified Simple Knowledge Organization System JSON Schema defining terms, definitions, prefLabels, altLabels, semantic relations (`broader`, `narrower`, `related`), and source attributions [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].
- **CNCF-Style Landscape Configuration**: An ecosystem directory config format driving the automated deployment of the workstream's web portal [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].
- **Unified Terminology Review Sheet**: A centralized review document where initial term proposals across all vertical working groups (approximately 250 terms) are collected, cross-referenced against related groups, and reviewed with consensus-based status flags (`LGTM`, `cull`, `debate`) before submitting formal pull requests [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e]. Universal terms spanning multiple working groups are prioritized at the top of the review sheet [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].

## Operational Cadence

Following its official launch and charter approval across working groups in June 2026, the workstream expanded its weekly Monday synchronization meetings to one hour to support structured debates over foundational terms such as `identity`, agent definitions, and boundary classifications [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e, ^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05**: Initial workstream kickoff meeting; draft charter formulated [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].
- **2026-06**: Charter formally approved across participating AAIF working groups; local development portal and CI/CD pipelines launched; delegates onboarded from across foundation bodies; initial batches of 10–20 terms delivered per working group [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].
- **2026-07**: Implementation of consensus-based cull/debate tracking and transition to one-hour weekly review meetings [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].

# References

- [Data Schema Specifications](https://github.com/aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape/blob/main/docs/data-schemas.md)
- [Taxonomy and Landscape Portal](https://aaif.github.io/ws-taxonomy-landscape/)
- [Working Group Delegates Directory](https://github.com/aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group (WG GRR) establishes bridges between emerging international artificial intelligence policy frameworks and the concrete architectures, controls, and technical execution patterns of agentic systems [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]. Chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase), the group evaluates global regulatory baselines against operational agent behaviors [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].

# Architecture / Specification

## Deliverables & Analysis Scope

The working group focuses on mapping regulatory compliance requirements into actionable technical guidance for agent developers and platform harnesses:
- **Regulatory Policy Landscape Mapping**: Systematic inventory of international AI governance frameworks, standards, and policy directives touching autonomous and semi-autonomous systems [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].
- **Policy Comparative and Gap Analysis**: Structured comparative evaluation identifying missing technical capabilities, unaddressed failure modes, and governance gaps when aligning existing policy frameworks with agentic workflows [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06**: Completed 3-month milestone surveying existing agentic AI policy frameworks, guidance documents, and regulatory standards [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].
- **2026-07**: Launched a 3-month sprint focused on performing an agentic AI policy comparative gap analysis [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].

# References

- [AAIF Working Group Reporting](https://github.com/aaif/wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory/blob/main/reporting/)

# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group defines open, vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, causal tracing models, and boundary propagation standards for agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]. Led by co-chairs Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group ensures agent decisions, tool invocations, and multi-agent coordination flows remain observable across heterogeneous runtimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].

# Architecture / Specification

## Focus Groups

To execute its six-month charter deliverables, the working group operates five specialized focus groups led by designated area leads [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]:
- **LLM Primitives Observability**: Standardizing telemetry around foundation model prompts, completions, token consumption, latencies, and raw inference primitives [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].
- **Protocol Observability**: Tracing interaction boundaries across protocols, including Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].
- **Multi-Agentic Observability (Orchestration & Coordination)**: Capturing distributed state transitions, task delegation topologies, fan-out joins, and consensus workflows across subagent swarms [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].
- **Agentic State and Context**: Telemetry capturing dynamic working memory, context window eviction, retrieval-augmented grounding, and long-term state persistence [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].
- **Agentic Reasoning**: Observing internal cognitive loops, chain-of-thought progression, tool candidate ranking, and step evaluation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].

## Cross-Working Group Integration

The group coordinates directly with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to align telemetry terms and definitions, while advancing initial draft documents for real-world observability use cases and technology landscape gap analyses [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06**: Finalized six-month charter objectives, launched five dedicated focus groups, drafted initial use case and gap analysis documents, and transitioned issue tracking and asynchronous decisions to GitHub and GitHub Discussions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].

# References

- [Observability & Traceability WG Repository](https://github.com/aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (WG SecPriv) provides reference security baselines, threat modeling frameworks, and architectural containment patterns for autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]. Chaired by Alex Frazer, the group investigates agent vulnerabilities, kernel sandboxing, tool verification, and cross-foundation alignment [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Architecture / Specification

## Workstreams & Deliverables

The group coordinates multiple active workstreams producing normative guidance and runtime evaluation resources [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]:
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, evaluating baseline coverage across MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF across eight distinct agentic threat domains [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing actionable security architecture and operational practices [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, authoring structured architectural templates for isolation, attestation, and privilege containment [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing lightweight security verification criteria applied across AAIF specifications [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Taxonomy & Landscape Alignment**: Appointed delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman collaborate with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to review agent security vocabulary and surface contentious definitions on Discord [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

## External Alignment

The working group maintains liaison alignment with external standards bodies including OWASP, ETSI TC SAI (concerning agentic compliance in the European AI Act), and evaluates potential interface overlap with the Linux Foundation's FINOS AI governance framework [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06**: Completed June TC report and transitioned meeting scheduling to Linux Foundation LFX [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **2026-07**: Delivered first draft of Best Practices Guide and final threat modeling gap review deliverable; initiated catalog branch staging for design patterns [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# References

- [Security and Privacy WG Repository](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy)

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream curating a standardized SKOS-Lite agentic AI glossary and an interactive CNCF-style ecosystem architecture map.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) initiative chartered to curate, harmonize, and publish a foundation-wide glossary of agentic AI terms and an interactive ecosystem landscape map.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b] Operating across specialized technical working groups, the workstream prevents fragmented or conflicting terminology and eliminates redundant ecosystem landscape research across the foundation.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]

The workstream maintains horizontal curation responsibility, consolidating shared terms and structural maps, while vertical technical working groups such as [Security & Privacy](security-and-privacy.md) and [Observability & Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md) maintain ownership over domain-specific specifications and protocol designs.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]

# Architecture / Specification

### Taxonomy Schema & Glossary Consolidation
Terminology entries are standardized using a SKOS-Lite metadata schema designed for flexible semantic cross-referencing and validation:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]
- `prefLabel`: Canonical term name.
- `altLabel`: Synonyms or deprecated nomenclature.
- `broaderTerm`: Hierarchical parent concept.
- `scopeNote`: Contextual application boundary.
- `relatedTerms`: Non-hierarchical conceptual associations.
- `contrastsWith`: Explicit conceptual distinctions to avoid conflation.

All baseline vocabulary entries are reconciled into a single repository (`taxonomy-data.js`) with active delegate oversight.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]

### Ecosystem Landscape & Portal Publishing
The workstream curates an interactive ecosystem architecture map modeled after the CNCF Landscape (`landscape.yml`). Categorization partitions and landscape groupings evolve iteratively through delegate consensus.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b] An automated GitHub Actions continuous deployment pipeline packages the static portal assets, taxonomy explorer, and landscape definitions, deploying them to GitHub Pages with build timestamps.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea]

# Governance & Operating Model

- **Charter Approval:** Ratified on June 21, 2026.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]
- **Leadership:** Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Co-Chaired by Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security & Privacy Working Group develops foundational threat models, actionable engineering best practices, security design patterns, and cross-working-group review checklists to safeguard agentic AI architectures against runtime exploitation, data leakage, and supply-chain vulnerabilities.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]

The working group collaborates with the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) on terminology arbitration and with [Workflows and Process Integration](workflows-and-process-integration.md) on boundary enforcement patterns.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]

# Architecture & Deliverables

As of its June 2026 reporting period, the group transitioned from organizational formation into active execution across five structured workstreams with assigned leads and documentation repositories:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]

1. **Threat Modeling & Gap Analysis:** Produced initial drafted analysis assessing existing cybersecurity frameworks against agentic-specific threat surfaces.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]
2. **Best Practices Guide:** Authored initial guidance on kernel-level sandboxing, credential isolation, and defense-in-depth measures.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]
3. **Security Review Checklist:** Lightweight criteria for evaluating AAIF reference architectures and tooling plugins.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]
4. **Design Patterns:** Formalizing hardened execution boundaries and runtime controls.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]
5. **Taxonomy Alignment:** Transferred standalone glossary curation to the cross-working-group [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to ensure single-source foundation definitions.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]

# Governance & External Liaisons

The working group reports monthly to the AAIF Technical Committee.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7] In June 2026, the working group submitted a formal decision request to the Technical Committee to define the posture and protocol boundaries for external collaboration with OWASP, AARM, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) Access Control Specifications (ACS).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]

# References

[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]: AAIF Security & Privacy Working Group June 2026 Monthly TC Report (PR #7, `reporting/2026-06-report.md`).

# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (W&PI) establishes a shared workflow model and common terminology for agentic AI systems, extending open specifications and producing interoperability guidelines and design patterns across heterogeneous agent frameworks, tools, and execution environments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]. Approved on May 13, 2026 and updated on July 23, 2026, the group addresses portability, replayability, failure recovery, and external system coordination [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

# Architecture / Specification
The group's technical scope is organized into three primary operational areas [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]:
- **Agent Workflow Models and Semantics**: Defining canonical terminology and primitives (tasks, tool calls, branching, sub-agents, retries) and non-deterministic workflow execution representations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].
- **Long-Running and Stateful Agent Execution**: Formulating patterns for multi-hour and multi-day executions, workflow state persistence, partial resumption, idempotency, and workflow-level audit logs distinct from runtime telemetry handled by [Observability & Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].
- **Tool Invocation and External Coordination**: Developing standardized coordination patterns between agents and external systems, APIs, CLIs, and human operators [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

# Working Group Operations
Leadership contacts established in the charter [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]:
- **Chair**: Yaron Schneider (`yaron@diagrid.io`)
- **Co-Chair**: Adam Seligman (`adam@workato.com`)

Core outputs interface with foundation patterns including [bounded convergence loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md), [human approval gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md), and [parallel fan out and join](../patterns/parallel-fan-out-and-join.md).

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol gap analyses, and reference architectures across discovery, checkout, payment, and post-purchase lifecycles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body defining protocol-neutral interfaces, capability abstractions, and interoperability baselines for commerce transactions mediated or executed by autonomous AI agents [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]. Chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), the group addresses agent-mediated discovery, merchant negotiation, payment delegation, and transaction settlement across heterogeneous platforms without standardizing proprietary internal architectures [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

# Scope and Objectives

The working group focuses strictly on commerce-facing interfaces and interaction protocols rather than agent internal reasoning mechanisms [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]. Its charter spans six functional domains:

1. **Discovery**: Mapping product discovery across asynchronous catalog feeds and real-time merchant or marketplace retrieval, addressing feed freshness, source provenance, and catalog normalization [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
2. **Delegated Authority**: Standardizing authorization envelopes that bound agent spending discretion, user consent, and intent validation across client and merchant contexts [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
3. **Checkout and Negotiation**: Evaluating stateful, merchant-authoritative negotiation flows across protocols, human handoff checkpoints, and cart finalization [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
4. **Payment Execution**: Analyzing payment handler abstractions across dynamic instrument eligibility, delegated tokenization, and sensitive data boundaries [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
5. **Fraud and Trust Signals**: Preserving contextual trust signals across shoppers, agent platforms, merchants, payment networks, and risk systems while isolating agent identity risk from shopper identity risk [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
6. **Post-Purchase Operations**: Supporting automated order status tracking, fulfillment updates, modifications, and returns [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].

The group maintains explicit cross-working-group touchpoints with [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), and [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].

# Workstreams and Deliverables

The working group's charter centers on four primary deliverables [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]:

- **Agentic Commerce Capability Map**: The initial milestone document formalizing capability abstractions across [agentic checkout](../taxonomy/agentic-checkout.md), [delegated payment](../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md), discovery, and risk boundaries [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
- **Protocol Gap Analysis**: A comparative assessment of existing commerce protocols evaluating composition hurdles, transport bindings, and trust assumptions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
- **Best Practices and Guidance**: Implementation guidance detailing privacy-preserving telemetry, credential handling, and merchant risk evaluation [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
- **Reference Architecture**: An architectural blueprint demonstrating end-to-end [agent-initiated](../taxonomy/agent-initiated-transaction.md) and [agent-in-the-loop](../taxonomy/agent-in-the-loop-transaction.md) transactions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].

# Protocol and Architecture Analysis

The working group evaluates emerging and established commerce standards to establish vendor-neutral integration patterns:

- **Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP) & Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)**: Analyzed as stateful, merchant-authoritative negotiation patterns for cart assembly, extension points, transport bindings, and dynamic payment-method discovery [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
- **Machine Payments Protocol (MPP)**: Evaluated for its challenge–credential–receipt exchange as a specialized payment-handler composition pattern within broader checkout pipelines [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
- **Payment Handler Model**: Structured around three decomposed entities: *handler* (execution runtime), *instrument* (underlying account or method), and *credential* (proof or token presented during authorization) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

# Lifecycle History

- **April 2026**: Conducted landscape exploration on product discovery and checkout mechanics across ACP and UCP; established interface-versus-internals scoping principles and drafted charter [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
- **May 2026**: Working group charter approved; initiated deliverable work on the Agentic Commerce Capability Map and conducted technical deep-dives comparing payment-handler models across ACP, UCP, and MPP [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol gap analyses, and reference architectures across the agentic commerce lifecycle.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an AAIF technical body established to provide a vendor-neutral forum and architectural framework for commercial transactions executed or mediated by autonomous agents[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26]. Chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), the group coordinates multi-stakeholder research across consumers, agents, merchants, payment providers, networks, and compliance practitioners[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332].

Rather than authoring another competing commercial standard, the group evaluates existing industry initiatives—including UCP, ACP, AP2, and x402—to document capability overlaps, protocol fragmentation, merchant integration burdens, and missing handoffs across transaction lifecycles[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its technical analysis around a four-stage commerce lifecycle, intersected by horizontal governance requirements[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332]:

1. **Product Discovery**: Comparing feed-based ingestion and live-query protocols, catalog normalization, data freshness, and trust models[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332].
2. **Checkout and Negotiation**: Evaluating extensible schemas, transport bindings, and human handoff mechanisms during basket assembly and price negotiation[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332].
3. **Payment Execution**: Analyzing agent wallets, x402 HTTP-native payment responses, and AP2 intent mandates that constrain delegated payment boundaries[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].
4. **Post-Purchase Operations**: Addressing order observability, policy discovery, adjustment ledgers, and state mutations governing cancellations, returns, refunds, and dispute management[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

Cross-cutting focus areas include delegated identity, human oversight gates (such as [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)), and signal propagation for fraud and risk assessment across merchant and payment boundary systems[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe]. The group maintains explicit cross-workgroup dependencies with [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), and [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].

# Lifecycle History
- **February 2026**: Working group kickoff; completed initial capability and actor inventory across consumers, agents, merchants, wallets, and banks, identifying protocol fragmentation and merchant integration burdens as key risks[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26].
- **March 2026**: Formulated lifecycle-oriented methodology; prioritized product discovery as the first deep dive and prepared draft charter deliverables[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332].
- **June 2026**: Conducted fraud and trust signal analysis, separating signal interoperability from internal fraud models and delineating shopper risk from agent risk and delegation proofs[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].
- **July 2026**: Commenced post-purchase review using UCP models and initiated agent wallet integration analysis across AP2 mandates and x402 payment flows toward a September Capability Map target[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream curating a standardized SKOS-Lite agentic AI glossary and an interactive directory of ecosystem technologies.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative chartered to curate a shared SKOS-Lite conceptual vocabulary and maintain an interactive ecosystem directory mapping agentic AI technologies and initiatives[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]. Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream arbitrates terminology across all AAIF working groups to establish consensus definitions for foundational agent concepts[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream manages two primary public assets:
1. **Agentic AI Taxonomy**: A standardized, machine-readable vocabulary establishing universal terms and specialized domain glossaries (covering areas such as Identity & Trust, Workflows & Process Integration, and Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
2. **Taxonomy and Landscape Portal**: A public web directory publishing admitted terms and indexing community and industry agent implementations[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

The term admission pipeline operates through sequential review syncs and GitHub pull requests. Terms are processed through a phased methodology where conceptual admission occurs prior to finalizing formal `definition`, `category`, and `broaderTerm` fields[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]. External proposals are held until contributors participate in review syncs to preserve review consistency[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

# Lifecycle History
- **July 2026**: Shifted from term collection to formal arbitration, extending review syncs to one hour. Reviewed 46 terms across universal and Identity & Trust categories; admitted 13 terms (published in PR #33), culled 11, and held 21 for debate[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
- **August 2026**: Reached 67 total reviewed terms out of the 128-term backlog. Admitted 8 additional terms from Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment via PR #35 (raising total live entries to 21), while managing an unresolved debate backlog of 25 contested concepts including `Agent`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

proposed_concept.title: Human Approval Gate
proposed_concept.description: Workflow governance pattern requiring explicit, authenticated authorization from a uniquely identified human before executing a protected agent action.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Human Approval Gate pattern mandates that an authenticated, uniquely identified human principal reviews and explicitly decides whether an immutable proposal may execute a protected effect.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428] Designed for workflows where actions carry high risk, legal exposure, or audit obligations, this pattern parks execution safely in a durable wait state until an explicit authorization decision binds to the exact version of the reviewed proposal.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428]

The pattern is composed within reference architectures such as [Single-Agent Process with Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md) and directly coordinates with the [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) and [Durable Wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md) patterns.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428]

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Flow
```text
immutable proposal ──► present to authorized human ──► explicit decision
                              │                           │
                              └── durable wait ─────────┘
                                          │
                          decision record: who · what · when
```

An execution engine surfaces an immutable action proposal across a human interaction surface to an authorized approver. While awaiting input, the workflow engine transitions into a durable wait state. When the human approves or rejects, an immutable decision record capturing the who, what, and when is persisted to the audit log under the same workflow run identity.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428]

## Required Capabilities
Implementations of this pattern require four foundational system capabilities:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428]
- **Execution engine**: Capable of halting and resuming execution safely based on external asynchronous events.
- **Human interaction surface**: Renders the complete, immutable proposal payload for inspection.
- **State/context store**: Persists workflow execution state, timers, and proposal versions during extended pauses.
- **Audit log**: Captures tamper-evident records of approval credentials, timestamps, and decision outcomes.

## Invariants
Any conformant implementation must satisfy the following invariants:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428]
- The approver must be a uniquely identified human principal authorized for the decision class; shared approval accounts or generic tokens do not qualify.
- The interaction surface must display the exact, immutable proposal version to which the subsequent decision will bind.
- Approval and rejection must be explicit decisions; silence, timeouts, delivery failures, or system errors must never evaluate to implicit approval.
- The decision record must atomically capture the proposal version, approver identity, explicit decision, and timestamp under the same run identity.
- Any modification or supersession of a pending proposal invalidates previous reviews and mandates a new approval decision.
- Pending approval requests must define an explicit deadline with deterministic expiration or escalation paths.
- Duplicate, late, or conflicting decision events must not cause duplicate resumption or multiple executions of the protected action.

## Failure Modes
Violating pattern invariants introduces distinct operational and security failures:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428]
- **Shared Approver Accounts**: Masks individual attribution, preventing non-repudiation in audit trails.
- **Mutable Proposals**: Allows an action to change between human review and backend execution, creating time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) vulnerabilities.
- **Implicit Approval on Timeout**: Degrades security boundaries by treating communication outages or human inaction as authorization.
- **Race Conditions on Late Delivery**: Allows duplicate execution of sensitive side-effects if approval messages arrive concurrently with timeout handlers.

# References
- Workflows and Process Integration WG: [Human Approval Gate Pattern Specification](https://github.com/aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration/blob/3b4d645499620b10b313297e7f365148fa6d0ee1/workstreams/reference-architectures/patterns/human-approval-gate.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428]
