proposed_concept.title: Job-Oriented Architecture Model
proposed_concept.description: Architectural framework structuring agent workflow reference architectures around recognizable practitioner jobs rather than structural agent counts.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Job-Oriented Architecture Model is an architectural decision adopted by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group to organize reference architectures around recognizable practitioner tasks and guarantees rather than structural topology such as single-agent or multi-agent counts.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62] In this framework, reference architectures represent complete compositions of reusable patterns, capabilities, boundaries, and exit states designed to achieve a named operational job.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]

By separating independently adoptable workflow patterns—such as the [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) or [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)—from full reference architectures like [Single-Agent Process with Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md), this model ensures that operational guarantees and failure modes are explicitly specified without redundant definitions across implementations.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]

# Architecture / Specification

## Decision Principles
The model establishes four foundational organizing principles for workflow engineering:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]
- **Job-First Classification**: Reference architectures are categorized by the operational job a practitioner aims to accomplish (e.g., human-approved execution, bounded remediation, coordinated research), ensuring that risk, attribution, and lifecycle guarantees match real-world requirements.
- **Pattern Independence**: A pattern is an independently adoptable solution addressing a single recurring workflow problem. Architectures compose multiple patterns, while patterns maintain their own invariants, failure modes, and implementation examples.
- **Structural Properties as Secondary Attributes**: Topology metrics such as agent count (single-agent versus multi-agent) are internal design characteristics rather than top-level architectural categories.
- **Scenario-Driven Validation**: Concrete practitioner use cases and scenarios validate architectures. A misfit scenario indicates a missing variant, an unmapped pattern, or a distinct operational job requiring a separate reference architecture.

## Consequences and Workflow Impact
Adopting this model imposes concrete constraints on working group deliverables:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]
- Generic structural scaffolds (e.g., generic single-agent or multi-agent templates) are replaced by job-specific reference architectures.
- Multi-agent architectures are drafted only after identifying a concrete, named practitioner job.
- Architecture proposals must define explicit guarantees, required capabilities, boundary interfaces, and a composition of reusable patterns.
- Pattern proposals are evaluated for independence from specific products, platforms, or single architectures.

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-07-20**: Proposed in ADR `job-oriented-architecture-model.md` for working group review to supersede generic agent-count taxonomies with practitioner job frameworks.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]

# References
- Workflows and Process Integration WG: [Architecture Decision Record: Organize Reference Architectures Around Practitioner Jobs](https://github.com/aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration/blob/3b4d645499620b10b313297e7f365148fa6d0ee1/workstreams/reference-architectures/decisions/job-oriented-architecture-model.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body chartered to define open telemetry formats, causal trace models, and cross-boundary correlation standards for AI agent systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7] Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group establishes vendor-neutral telemetry pipelines, bridges agent execution layers with upstream standard bodies such as OpenTelemetry and the IETF, and standardizes verifiable execution artifacts.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]

The working group coordinates technical outputs across taxonomy alignment with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), runtime observation frameworks such as [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md), and behavioral specifications including the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]

# Architecture / Specification

## Active Focus Tracks
To optimize contributor velocity and address overlapping scopes, the working group consolidated its initial five focus groups into three active tracks in July 2026:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]
- **LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability** (Lead: Zayne Turner): Merges core model invocation telemetry with protocol-level tracing. Key deliverables include observability for Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD), modeling skills as first-class observable entities, and cross-boundary gap analyses.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]
- **Multi-Agentic Observability - Orchestration & Coordination** (Lead: Ty Smith): Develops modular observability maps, multi-agent dialog tracing, and runtime intelligence graph prototypes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]
- **Agentic State & Context** (Lead: Govindaraj): Combines agentic reasoning telemetry with context store observability, producing comparative landscape surveys and gap analysis specifications.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]

## Emerging Technical Workstreams
In late 2026, the group initiated joint technical work bridging distributed peer-to-peer networking and agent telemetry:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: A dedicated recommendation workstream defining standardized causal execution representations and runtime schemas.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]
- **Composable Trust Blueprint**: Integration of Verifiable Telemetry Objects (VTO) with Agent Action Capsules (AAC), separating telemetry semantics from cryptography using CBOR42 encodings and collaborating with LibP2P and IETF/IRTF measurement efforts.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-07-31**: Monthly report submitted to the Technical Committee detailing the consolidation from five focus groups to three active tracks and establishing deliverables for cross-boundary observability.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]
- **2026-08-05**: Working group meeting advances P2P GossipSub observability demonstrations, VTO/AAC telemetry proposals, and scheduling of the Agent Behavior Trace Model pull request.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]

# References
- Observability & Traceability WG: [July 2026 Monthly Report](https://github.com/aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability/blob/ecdd24bcbb59140ce89b608a8ddf815a38140a2b/reporting/2026-07-report.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]
- Observability & Traceability WG: [Meeting Minutes 2026-08-05](https://github.com/aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability/blob/ecdd24bcbb59140ce89b608a8ddf815a38140a2b/meeting-minutes/2026-08-05.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body tasked with establishing a shared workflow model and standard terminology for agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]. The working group extends open specifications and projects while producing interoperability guidelines and design patterns that allow multi-agent workflows to operate across heterogeneous frameworks, tools, and execution environments[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87].

# Operational Structure
The working group is led by appointed leadership serving a defined governance term[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]:
- **Chair**: Yaron Schneider (Diagrid)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]
- **Co-Chair**: Adam Seligman (Workato)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]

Chairs are appointed by Platinum and Gold members of the working group, with the term running from March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87].

Working group meetings are held biweekly on Thursdays at 8:00 AM Pacific Time via the Linux Foundation LFX platform[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]. Public communication channels include the dedicated mailing list (`wg-workflows-process-integration@lists.aaif.io`) and community Discord channels[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87].

# Workstreams and Deliverables
The working group organizes technical activities across three primary workstreams:
1. **Taxonomy**: Curates a shared vocabulary, including foundational [`../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md`](../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md), to minimize ambiguity across WG specifications and architecture documents[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a].
2. **Reference Architectures**: Defines standard execution topologies and pattern implementations aligned with [`../guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md`](../guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a].
3. **Critical Use Cases**: Analyzes real-world deployment topologies to benchmark workflow requirements across heterogeneous enterprise environments[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Actionable security implementation guide detailing threat models, secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide is a practitioner-focused implementation guide produced by the Security and Privacy Working Group as Deliverable 4 of 5[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]. It establishes operational patterns and control implementations to harden autonomous agent architectures across secrets management, tool invocation pipelines, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

# Architecture / Specification
The guideline organizes technical defenses across five operational domains using a structured failure-pattern, control, and decision-framework format[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]:

1. **Secrets Management**: Controls and isolation techniques preventing credential leakage in conversational context, memory graphs, and execution logs.
2. **Secure Tool Invocation**: Defenses addressing Model Context Protocol (MCP) boundaries, tool supply-chain risks, and verified schemas aligned with [`../standards/toolsurface.md`](../standards/toolsurface.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].
3. **Guardrails**: Implementation of model-level validation, behavioral constraints, and policy interception checkpoints such as [`../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md`](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].
4. **Evaluation Frameworks**: Pre-deployment safety benchmarking, red-teaming methodologies, and regression testing suites.
5. **Post-Incident Forensics**: Invariant logging, causal event correlation, and tamper-resistant audit trails for investigating security anomalies[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

The guide also incorporates a curated tool reference ledger detailing technology maturity, cost implications, and integration notes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

## Boundary and Scope
Identity issuance and delegated authorization architectures—including SPIFFE/SVID credentials and OAuth token exchange (RFC 8693)—are explicitly excluded from this guideline and are governed by the [`../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md`](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) Working Group[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing threat models, security design patterns, best practice guides, and review checklists for secure agentic AI deployments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (WG Security & Privacy / SPAA) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body dedicated to addressing the expanded threat landscape, privacy boundaries, and attack vectors introduced by autonomous AI agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]. Chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), the group formulates actionable defense guidance, cataloged design patterns, threat modeling comparisons, and cross-working group security review frameworks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Operating Procedures

The working group operates under public-by-default transparency principles, maintaining open Discord channels, public repositories, and openly accessible meeting records [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]. Deliverables follow a decentralized review and merge process: the working group reviews and merges pull requests directly once group consensus is reached, without requiring individual approval from the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) provided the work falls within its approved charter [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]. Monthly reports submitted to the TC provide post-merge governance visibility [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

## Active Workstreams

1. **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, evaluating comparative industry frameworks (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, NIST AI RMF) alongside STRIDE and PASTA methodologies [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
2. **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing defensive architectures, tool-boundary isolation, and accountability structures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, defining standardized architectural security patterns and submission templates [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
4. **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, aligning baseline security requirements across sister working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
5. **Taxonomy and Landscape Coordination**: Represented by delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman, reconciling security and privacy terms within the centralized AAIF glossary [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

## Cross-Working Group Integration

The working group actively delegates domain-specific ownership to adjacent bodies, coordinating with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) for identity delegation and authentication mechanisms while synchronizing definitions with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06**: Stood up initial workstreams, transferred taxonomy responsibilities to the cross-WG effort, and began drafting threat modeling and best practices deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3].
- **2026-07**: Published initial drafts of the Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Best Practices Guide as GitHub pull requests; completed the Design Patterns Catalog framework [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10].
- **2026-08**: Formally confirmed PR merge authority within charter scope and established default public transparency for meetings and recordings [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group (WG Observability & Traceability) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body dedicated to creating standard semantic conventions, cross-boundary tracing protocols, and runtime telemetry models for autonomous agent workflows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]. The group develops specifications such as the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) while maintaining rigorous operational working methods to ensure open, asynchronous collaboration [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff].

# Architecture / Specification

## Operational Methods and Source of Truth

The working group designates GitHub as its single source of truth for durable artifacts and progress tracking [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]:

- **Issues**: Durable tracking units for workstreams, external coordination threads, and architectural decisions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff].
- **Pull Requests**: Authoritative mechanism for repository changes and formal peer review [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff].
- **Early Drafting**: Shared documents (e.g., Google Docs) may be utilized for early ideation, but completed artifacts must be transitioned into the repository before review or publication [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff].
- **External Channels**: Communications on Slack or Discord remain secondary and cannot serve as the sole record of project state [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff].

## Work Item Lifecycle

Deliverables and coordination tasks utilize a standardized work-item structure tracking outcomes, workstream classification, owner, concrete next steps, required decisions, and acceptance criteria [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b44b5d93b435-bb190e50]. Work items must reflect one of six defined operational statuses [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b44b5d93b435-bb190e50] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]:

- `needs owner`: Valid task awaiting an active driver.
- `scoping`: Boundaries, required inputs, and expected outcomes are being determined.
- `in progress`: Active research, drafting, or coordination is underway.
- `ready for review`: Artifact or decision is staged for stakeholder evaluation.
- `blocked`: Execution is halted by an explicit external dependency or unresolved decision.
- `done`: The deliverable is merged, intentionally closed, or relocated to downstream tracking.

## Operating Cadence

The group operates on a lightweight synchronization cadence tied to working group meetings and [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) monthly reports [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]. Pre-meeting reviews identify blocked tasks, meeting notes record action items linked to corresponding issues or PRs, and post-meeting updates reconcile task statuses for asynchronous participants [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design
proposed_concept.description: Comparative gap analysis evaluating OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF across eight agentic threat categories, augmented by STRIDE and PASTA alignment.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis is an ongoing research deliverable produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]. Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, the analysis systematically benchmarks existing cybersecurity and AI risk frameworks—specifically MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, CSA MAESTRO, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF)—against eight threat areas unique to autonomous agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

# Architecture / Specification

## Comparative Coverage

The initial gap review examines how traditional and AI-specific threat methodologies handle autonomous agent capabilities, including dynamic tool execution, memory persistence, multi-agent delegation, and human-in-the-loop bypasses [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]. The deliverable synthesizes findings from external industry sources such as OWASP's State of Agentic AI Security and Governance report [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

## Extended Methodological Scope

Subsequent revisions incorporate broader threat modeling methodologies and emerging protocol developments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]:

- **Classical Modeling Mapping**: Aligning agentic threat categories with established STRIDE (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, Elevation of Privilege) and PASTA (Process for Attack Simulation and Threat Analysis) structures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Interface Boundaries**: Analyzing UI and Human-User Agent (HUA) interaction perimeters where prompt injections and user deception manifest [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Tool and Protocol Attestation**: Addressing Model Context Protocol (MCP) updates, specifically evaluating stateless operation and cryptographic tool signing to mitigate tool rug-pull attacks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07**: Fernando Lucktemberg completed the eight-area initial gap review and opened a formal pull request on the working group repository [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **2026-08**: Workstream commenced bi-weekly meetings and began integrating STRIDE/PASTA mapping, UI/HUA risk considerations, and stateless MCP attestation dynamics [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Actionable security implementation guide detailing threat models, secrets management, secure tool integration, human accountability, and cross-boundary containment.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide is an implementation reference authored within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]. Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, the guide outlines defense-in-depth engineering practices for designing, deploying, and governing autonomous AI agent systems across enterprise environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

# Architecture / Specification

## Foundational Principles and Core Topics

The guide outlines engineering defenses against systemic agent vulnerabilities [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]:

- **Accountability Model**: Establishes that while autonomous agents perform execution actions, legal and operational accountability remains strictly with human operators and principals [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]. Human attribution must persist across service accounts, tool invocations, and autonomous tasks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Tool and Runtime Sandboxing**: Enforcing least-privilege tool execution, credential isolation, and memory-boundary containment.
- **Interface and HUA Protection**: Mitigating prompt injection, indirect instruction manipulation, and unauthorized delegation across Human-User Agent (HUA) surfaces [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

## Cross-Working Group Division of Scope

To prevent conflicting specifications across foundation projects, the guide partitions responsibilities:

- **Identity and Authorization**: Specific identity structures, delegation assertions, and trust token architectures are coordinated with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Threat Modeling Foundations**: Baseline threat categories and risk scores are drawn from the companion [Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07**: Fernando Lucktemberg published the initial skeleton draft as a pull request on GitHub, and the workstream convened its inaugural meeting [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **2026-08**: The workstream initiated incorporation of HUA interaction guidance and coordinated with adjacent working groups to establish identity and attribution boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's (AAIF) mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared engineering and governance discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]. It develops open threat models, shared security taxonomies, and architectural design patterns that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to implement shared responsibility for trustworthy agentic AI[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group repository is structured into three dedicated functional areas[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]:
- `charter/`: Governance charters and foundational operating rules.
- `deliverables/`: Published specifications, reference threat models, and architectural patterns.
- `meeting-notes/`: Agendas, running notes, summaries, and LFX meeting indices.

Collaborative artifacts maintained by the group include the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) and the [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md).

# Lifecycle History
The working group operates under the technical governance of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md). Current chairs were appointed by Platinum and Gold working group members for a term spanning March 1, 2026, to January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]:
- Chair: Alex Frazer (Runlayer)
- Co-Chair: Junjie Bu (Google)

Meetings take place biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM Pacific Time via LFX Zoom, with community discussions coordinated over the `wg-security-privacy@lists.aaif.io` mailing list and public AAIF Discord channels[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Lifecycle Policy defines the formal governance framework and operational criteria through which open technical projects join, advance within, and retire from the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]. Effective March 18, 2026, the policy outlines project intake criteria, stage-by-stage progression expectations (Sandbox, Growth, Impact, and Emeritus), and annual evaluation processes administered by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

# Architecture / Specification
Prospective projects are submitted to the AAIF project proposals repository under the [Project Proposal Process](project-proposal-process.md)[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]. Submissions must supply explicit operational and governance metadata, including:
- Project name, description, mission alignment statement, and relationships to existing AAIF initiatives[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Production use cases, adoption evidence, and an optional Technical Committee mentor sponsor[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Licensing under an OSI-approved permissive open-source license, public repository URLs, public issue trackers, and external dependency disclosures[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Automated validation pipelines, release methodology, public specification contribution paths, and documented governance (`GOVERNANCE.md`)[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Core maintainer listings, official communication channels, financial sponsorships, and foundation infrastructure requests[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

Project progression across lifecycle stages is governed by acceptance and graduation criteria[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]:
- **Sandbox Stage**: Incubation entry point designed to foster experimental open-source tooling, protocols, and libraries under foundation mentorship.
- **Growth Stage**: Intermediate tier demonstrating cross-organization contributor diversity, sustained release cadences, and real-world deployment traction.
- **Impact Stage**: Production-grade maturity demonstrating broad industry-standard adoption, rigorous security practices, and mission-critical ecosystem stability.
- **Emeritus Stage**: Structured retirement tier for projects that have concluded active maintenance, merged into successor efforts, or wound down operations.

# Lifecycle History
The policy was adopted by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) with an effective date of March 18, 2026[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]. Project stage standing and adherence to operational criteria are evaluated annually via the Annual Review Process[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Skill
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skill standardizing first-pass GitHub issue triage, codebase grounding, prompt injection defenses, and precedent matching against historical review references.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Issue Analysis Skill (`issue-analysis`) is a modular operational skill utilized by automated triage agents, such as the [Submission Analyser](../resources/submission-analyser.md), to produce structured first-pass analyses of filed GitHub issues[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. It provides maintainers with rapid problem classification, severity scoring, root-cause hypotheses, and suggested next actions grounded in repository evidence and historical maintainer reviews[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill enforces four sequential execution phases[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]:
1. **Evidence Ingestion and Prompt Injection Defense**: Untrusted issue bodies are wrapped within nonce-delimited text blocks and treated strictly as data. If an issue attempts to issue commands, alter output schemas, or extract credentials, the agent marks `injectionSuspected: true`, records details in `injectionNotes`, and restricts its output to technical evaluation[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
2. **Read-Only Codebase Grounding**: The agent inspects checked-out repository source code to locate referenced components and assess the plausibility of reported behavior, anchoring claims to explicit file paths rather than generalized subsystem labels[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. Code modification, build execution, and outbound network actions are strictly prohibited[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
3. **Precedent Matching via Past Reviews**: The agent evaluates human-authored analyses in `references/` by scanning frontmatter metadata (`tags`, `issue-type`, `severity`)[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. It references 3 to 5 overlapping precedent analyses to ground severity judgments (such as duplicate message deliveries after consumer restarts or authorization header disclosures in debug logging) while explicitly disallowing synthetic benchmark examples from being cited as true project history[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690][^evt-submission-analyser-file-20fc496a9225-9e278b3d][^evt-submission-analyser-file-4754a1b8e47b-9ed9890b].
4. **Structured Report Drafting**: The final triage report captures summary findings, classification with severity rationale, affected components, confirmed or refuted root-cause hypotheses, suggested remedial actions, and open investigative questions[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690][^evt-submission-analyser-file-20fc496a9225-9e278b3d].

# Lifecycle History
The skill is released under the Apache-2.0 license within the `aaif/submission-analyser` repository to provide automated issue triage across AAIF foundation projects[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skill standardizing first-pass GitHub issue triage, classification, component path localization, and maintainer action recommendations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Issue Analysis skill establishes a structured framework for automated, first-pass issue triage across GitHub repositories.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef] Operating within agent runtimes such as [Submission Analyser](../resources/submission-analyser.md), it digests untrusted issue reports and produces standardized diagnostic assessments that help maintainers quickly evaluate bug reports, feature requests, and operational questions.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]

# Architecture / Specification

## Output Structure and Schema

The skill mandates a seven-part analysis schema structured to isolate factual claims, concrete component paths, and actionable follow-ups:[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]

- **Summary:** A single-paragraph restatement of the reported issue or feature request in maintainer-oriented terminology without requiring prior review of the full issue thread.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]
- **Classification:** Controlled categorization covering:
  - *Type:* `bug`, `feature-request`, `documentation`, `question`, `security`, or `ambiguous`.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]
  - *Severity:* `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, or `informational`, supported by a brief rationale evaluating user impact, existing workarounds, and historical precedent.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]
  - *Reproducibility:* `reproducible`, `not-reproducible`, `insufficient-information`, or `not-applicable`.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]
- **Affected Components:** Concrete file paths or module identifiers (e.g., `src/config/loader.ts`) rather than abstract subsystem labels.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef][^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22]
- **Root-Cause Hypotheses:** Proposed technical mechanisms for defects or architectural design constraints explaining feature request behaviors, accompanied by explicit confirmation or refutation criteria.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef][^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22]
- **Suggested Actions:** Prioritized diagnostics, files to inspect, or targeted information requests rather than unverified patches.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]
- **Open Questions:** Specific clarifying inquiries directed to the original reporter before further investigation proceeds.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]
- **Related Past Reviews:** Citations to relevant past analysis files in `references/` that informed the assessment.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]

## Reference Corpus

The skill relies on historical and synthetic review documents located in `references/` to calibrate analysis depth and formatting conventions.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22] These examples guide the agent in recognizing design constraints—such as separating reloadable operational parameters from static import-time configuration—and recommending sensible scoping boundaries for maintainers.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22]

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless triage agent executing in GitHub Actions that analyses repository issues and tests robustness against untrusted prompt injections.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Submission Analyser is a headless triage agent operating within GitHub Actions workflows to perform automated assessment of inbound repository issues.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6] Utilizing the [Issue Analysis](../skills/issue-analysis.md) skill, the tool ingests untrusted user-submitted issue bodies while enforcing prompt boundary defenses against indirect injection and context contamination.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6]

# Architecture / Specification

## Injection Test Harness and Fixtures

Because inbound issues constitute untrusted external text, the project maintains an adversarial evaluation suite in `tests/fixtures/injections/` to benchmark agent robustness against common injection vectors:[^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6]

- **Direct Instruction Overrides:** Payloads attempting to clear system instructions, reassign agent personas, or force unauthorized disclosure of system prompts and tool definitions.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6]
- **Simulated Tool and Function Calls:** Injected XML elements (`<function_calls>`) or JSON code blocks (`tool_call`) designed to trick parsing layers into executing unauthorized actions, exfiltrating data, or subverting secondary security scans.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-2e092a0c54ea-4363d97f]
- **Obfuscation and Evasion:** Multi-format encoding attempts including Base64, ROT13, and Cyrillic homoglyph lookalikes designed to bypass keyword-based safety filters while directing the agent to reveal environment variables.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-0f27825af60d-1d3aca33]
- **Downstream Notification Flooding:** Mass-mention payloads (`@everyone`, `@here`, role and user IDs) crafted to coerce the agent into echoing verbatim notifications across integrated notification channels such as Discord.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-04ecd65ab81f-33714e60]

mutations.rationale: Incorporate adversarial prompt injection and security robustness test fixtures merged into the submission-analyser evaluation suite.

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless triage agent and adversarial evaluation suite testing issue analysis against prompt injection, privilege spoofing, and exfiltration vectors.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Submission Analyser is an automated triage utility and evaluation harness running in headless environments such as GitHub Actions to classify incoming issue submissions, extract diagnostic metadata, and evaluate agent resilience against hostile inputs.

To ensure triage pipelines do not execute untrusted directives embedded within user-submitted markdown, the repository maintains an adversarial fixture suite (`tests/fixtures/injections/`) that benchmarks agent robustness against common indirect prompt injection and privilege escalation patterns.

# Architecture / Specification

The evaluation harness subjects the triage analyzer to specialized adversarial fixtures designed to test specific threat boundaries:

- **Environment Variable and Secret Exfiltration**: Test payloads attempt to trick the triage engine into dumping its runtime environment or encoding secret tokens (such as `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, or API keys) into structured summary outputs or metadata lists [^evt-submission-analyser-file-c385a440d3d1-196a4a61].
- **Hidden Markup and Instruction Overrides**: Payloads conceal instructions inside HTML comments (`<!-- ... -->`) instructing the parsing agent to clear injection warning flags, elevate severity to critical, and falsely append security approvals [^evt-submission-analyser-file-305b7ba8fb0c-d60ec9fe].
- **Untrusted Remote Retrieval**: Payloads attempt to weaponize tool calling by commanding the agent to fetch unverified third-party patch files or URLs and embed arbitrary instructions into triage action lists [^evt-submission-analyser-file-7cf6ee468c96-f0fe2bdd].
- **Invisible Characters and Persona Hijacking**: Payloads utilize Unicode bidirectional controls or zero-width formatting paired with jailbreak framing (such as "DevMode" or maintainer role-play) to override default triage instructions and force verbatim system prompt reflection [^evt-submission-analyser-file-7385a2d6a676-148647ca].
- **Nested DOM Elements and Script Tags**: Vectors embed system overrides within collapsed markup (`<details>`, `<summary>`) or broken image tags containing cross-site scripting constructs to verify that HTML rendering does not leak agent credentials [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a072a88a60fa-f5eaa4ea].
- **Authority Impersonation and Urgency Coercion**: Social engineering fixtures simulate high-priority directives from governing bodies (such as "The Linux Foundation security team") to coerce prompt hierarchy inversion, disable injection detection heuristics, and exfiltrate configurations [^evt-submission-analyser-file-e761e6213598-a8166ad6].

These test cases support the implementation of defense-in-depth principles outlined in [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) and establish regression baselines for skills such as [Issue Analysis](../skills/issue-analysis.md) through [Deterministic Acceptance Gates](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md).

# Lifecycle History

- Added adversarial test fixture catalog covering environment exfiltration, hidden comment injection, external link dereferencing, persona hijacking, DOM evasion, and authority impersonation vectors.

proposed_concept.title: OpenTelemetry Agent Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry framework standardizing trace, metric, and log collection across agent harnesses, LLM gateways, and MCP servers using OTLP and gen_ai conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

OpenTelemetry (OTel) provides a vendor-neutral observability substrate standardizing how traces, metrics, and logs are instrumented, collected, and exported across AI agent infrastructures [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a]. Developed as a cloud-native standard, OTel functions as the plumbing layer connecting agent runtimes, language model proxies, and external tool endpoints with downstream telemetry backends without imposing vendor lock-in.

Within the scope of the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), OpenTelemetry acts as the primary transport and semantic baseline for propagating causal context across protocol boundaries, complementing standardized schemas like the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md).

# Architecture / Specification

The OTel agent reference architecture spans three distinct functional tiers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a]:

- **Instrumentation Layer:** Ingests execution events directly from agent harnesses, LLM gateways, and Model Context Protocol ([agent-mcp-server-boundary](agent-mcp-server-boundary.md)) servers via language SDKs (Python, Java, Go). Instrumentation adheres to OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions v1.27.0 (`gen_ai.*`), capturing prompt tokens, completion tokens, model configurations, and tool invocation parameters.
- **Wire Protocol (OTLP 1.3.0):** Standardizes telemetry delivery over gRPC (port 4317) or HTTP/protobuf and HTTP/JSON (port 4318) with consistent context propagation headers.
- **OTel Collector Pipeline (v0.104.0):** Decouples application components from telemetry sinks. Receivers ingest OTLP, Prometheus, and external signals; processors perform batching, PII redaction, and memory-limiting; and exporters push structured telemetry to target storage systems or analytical platforms.

# References

- OpenTelemetry Specification: stable signals for traces, metrics, and logs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a]
- OpenTelemetry Collector v0.104.0 architecture and pipeline specification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a]

mutations.rationale: Updates the PostHog agent telemetry reference architecture with Goose integration patterns, Capture API specifications, and client-side PII sanitization controls.

proposed_concept.title: PostHog Agent Telemetry Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Product analytics and session telemetry backend mapping agent behavioral events through direct HTTPS Capture API ingestion and client-side PII sanitization.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

PostHog functions as an external agent telemetry sink providing product analytics, adoption metrics, cohort segmentation, and behavioral event collection for AI agent frameworks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75]. Rather than capturing fine-grained distributed execution spans, it focuses on high-level lifecycle events, user onboarding funnels, error telemetry, and aggregate feature usage across desktop and CLI runtimes.

The reference architecture assesses PostHog's role within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), specifically evaluating privacy preservation boundaries during product event ingestion as exemplified by the [Goose](goose.md) agent runtime.

# Architecture / Specification

The integration pattern relies on an out-of-band HTTPS telemetry client without requiring heavy dependency SDKs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75]:

- **Client Ingestion Module:** The agent runtime embeds an HTTP telemetry module that writes directly to PostHog's Capture API (`/capture/`). Payloads consist of structured `CaptureEvent` records containing an API project key (`phc_*`), event identifier, pseudonymous `distinct_id` (persisted on disk as a UUID v4), timestamp, and key-value properties.
- **PII Sanitizer:** Before dispatch, client-side regex filters strip sensitive material including file system paths, authentication keys, email addresses, bearer tokens, and internal UUIDs from event payloads.
- **Storage Pipeline:** Events ingested by PostHog are buffered via Apache Kafka and persisted into ClickHouse for aggregate query evaluation and user profile correlation.

# References

- PostHog Capture API Reference and Ingestion Architecture [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75]
- Goose 1.39.0 Telemetry Implementation (`posthog.rs`) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75]

mutations.rationale: Incorporates reference architecture details covering Linux driver tracing primitives, dynamic debug callsites, hardware counter observation, and devcoredump facilities.

proposed_concept.title: Linux Driver Tracing Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Layered kernel observability framework capturing device driver hardware interactions, I/O requests, and error states via dynamic debug, TRACE_EVENT, and devcoredump.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Linux driver tracing comprises a layered collection of kernel-integrated debugging, logging, and performance instrumentation mechanisms dedicated to observing device driver behavior and hardware interactions without reallocating or recompiling driver code [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]. It provides low-overhead visibility into communication flows across PCIe, USB, NVMe, and GPU subsystem boundaries.

Within the broader hardware analysis landscape documented by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), driver tracing links operating system scheduling and containerized agent execution with underlying device controller states.

# Architecture / Specification

The driver observation model distinguishes between discrete hardware events and persistent subsystem states [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]:

- **Structured Device Logging:** Primitives such as `dev_dbg()`, `dev_info()`, and `dev_err()` bind log output directly to kernel `struct device` identifiers and sysfs topology.
- **Dynamic Debug (`dyndbg`):** Controlled via `debugfs` (`/sys/kernel/debug/dynamic_debug/control`), allowing administrators to toggle debug callsites at runtime on a per-file, per-function, or per-line basis without performance penalties when disabled.
- **Static Tracepoints (`TRACE_EVENT`):** Subsystem instrumentation exposed through `tracefs` (`/sys/kernel/tracing/`) consumed by tools such as `perf`, `trace-cmd`, or [bpftrace](bpftrace.md).
- **Specialized Subsystem Tracers:** Dedicated facilities including `usbmon` for raw USB packet sniffing and `blktrace` for block layer request lifecycles.
- **Crash and Snapshot Facilities:** `devcoredump` captures ephemeral hardware register snapshots and firmware state upon device failure for post-mortem extraction.

# References

- Linux Kernel Driver Tracing Documentation (Linux 6.x) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]
- Subsystem Tracing APIs: `blktrace`, `usbmon`, and `devcoredump` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser Triage Agent and Security Suite
proposed_concept.description: Headless issue triage agent and adversarial evaluation suite assessing prompt injection resistance, egress controls, and cross-repository trust boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Submission Analyser is an automated GitHub issue triage agent and security test suite designed to evaluate LLM-assisted issue analysis against adversarial prompt injections and untrusted inputs [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6]. It operates under the foundational threat assumption that attacker-controlled text from public issue submissions is directly processed by a model equipped with checkout inspection tools.

Managed in conjunction with guidelines from the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the system models secure execution boundaries such as the [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) by isolating analysis generation from publication channels.

# Architecture / Specification

The security architecture is defined by strict asset partitioning and trust boundaries [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6]:

- **Asset Isolation:** The agent protects model access credentials (`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`), publishing secrets (`GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON`, `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL`), repository workflows, and historical analysis corpora. The agent writes strictly to external human-reviewed sinks (a restricted Google Drive folder and Discord channel) and never commits back to source repositories.
- **Cross-Repository Boundary:** Runs are triggered across repositories using `workflow_dispatch` parameterized strictly by numeric issue numbers and `owner/repo` patterns. The dispatch token (`ANALYST_DISPATCH_TOKEN`) holds restricted `Actions: write` scope, preventing target repository compromise from escalating into workflow modifications in the analyst repository.
- **Adversarial Test Suite:** The system validates defense mechanisms against real-world prompt injection vectors, including delimiter forging (escaping untrusted issue wrappers via fake system nonces) [^evt-submission-analyser-file-f4ad28ba849d-48065e61] and fake authority spoofing (claims of repository owner or safety team override) [^evt-submission-analyser-file-fdb9d913d85d-8ad69d31].

# References

- Submission Analyser Threat Model Specification [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6]
- Delimiter Forging and Authority Override Test Fixtures [^evt-submission-analyser-file-f4ad28ba849d-48065e61] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-fdb9d913d85d-8ad69d31]

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless CI issue analysis agent built on Flue 2.0 that evaluates external GitHub submissions and publishes structured findings to Google Docs and Discord under strict zero-write repository permissions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Submission Analyser (`aaif/submission-analyser`) is an open-source, headless issue analysis agent operating in GitHub Actions to evaluate project intake submissions and issues filed across Agentic AI Foundation repositories[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec]. Built on the Flue 2.0 runtime with Pi model bindings (`@earendil-works/pi-ai`), the agent reviews target issues against repository context and historical reviews using the [Issue Analysis Skill](../skills/issue-analysis.md), generating structured reports published to Google Docs and announced via Discord webhooks[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec][^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].

# Architecture / Specification

## Trigger and Execution Model
The agent executes in a dedicated tooling repository and targets issues filed in external repositories (such as `aaif/project-proposals`) without requiring deployed HTTP listeners[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec]. Orchestration operates across two decoupled GitHub Actions workflows:
- **Target Repository Dispatcher:** External repositories deploy `.github/workflows/request-issue-analysis.yml`, triggered when issues are created (`opened`) or labeled by maintainers (`needs-analysis`)[^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660]. It triggers the analyst workflow via `github.rest.actions.createWorkflowDispatch` using `ANALYST_DISPATCH_TOKEN`[^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660].
- **Analyst Execution Workflow:** `.github/workflows/issue-analyst.yml` runs exclusively on `workflow_dispatch` to enforce an identical code path for both automated dispatches and manual invocations[^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f]. Concurrency groups prevent parallel runs on the same repository and issue number[^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f].

## Principle of Least Privilege and Token Isolation
The architecture strictly enforces least-privilege token boundaries to eliminate common prompt injection compromise paths[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec][^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f]:
- **Zero Repository Write Access:** The agent workflow requests only `contents: read` and `copilot-requests: write`[^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f]. The original design of commenting back on target issues was dropped to avoid requesting `issues: write`, preventing untrusted issue content from manipulating the model into committing malicious changes to workflow files or repository code[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec][^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f].
- **Dispatch Scoping:** The dispatch token is restricted strictly to `Actions: read and write` on the analyst repository[^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660]. Standard `repository_dispatch` was rejected because it requires `Contents: write`, which would allow code rewrites and secret exfiltration[^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660].
- **Tool-Level Credential Encapsulation:** Integration credentials (`GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON`, `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL`) are isolated inside tool integration code and are never exposed to the agent context or environment variables[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901][^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].

## Model Access and Fallback Strategy
Inference relies on GitHub Copilot enterprise entitlements using Pi's built-in `github-copilot` provider, authorized directly via `copilot-requests: write` on the workflow's native `GITHUB_TOKEN` without external model API keys[^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f][^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4][^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].
- **Primary Model:** Configured via repository variable `PRIMARY_MODEL`, defaulting to `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.7`[^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].
- **Fallback Model:** Multi-vendor model fallback is handled at workflow level via `FALLBACK_MODEL` (`github-copilot/gpt-5.4`), ensuring operational continuity across different model laboratories while maintaining a unified credential boundary[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4][^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].

## Adversarial Defense and Triage Semantics
Operational constraints defined in `AGENTS.md` mandate that issue titles, bodies, and comments are treated strictly as data and never as execution instructions[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901]. The agent is barred from creating, modifying, or deleting local files and executing network commands[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901]. When an injection attempt is detected, the agent is instructed to record `injectionSuspected: true` and detail the attempt in `injectionNotes` while completing its technical evaluation of legitimate claims, ensuring security events are recorded for maintainers rather than swallowed[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901][^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4].

mutations.rationale: Update issue-analysis skill specification detailing progressive disclosure mechanics, adversarial injection detection schema, and single-tool publishing orchestration under Flue 2.0.

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Skill
proposed_concept.description: Progressively disclosed Flue 2.0 agent skill structuring GitHub issue evaluation, reference comparison, output schema enforcement, and prompt injection detection.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Issue Analysis Skill (`src/skills/issue-analysis`) is a modular, progressively disclosed agent capability within [Submission Analyser](../resources/submission-analyser.md) designed to perform first-pass technical assessments of GitHub issues[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec][^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]. Mounted explicitly in the Flue 2.0 runtime via `useSkill()`, the skill provides evaluation instructions, standardized report templates, and synthetic reference benchmarks while minimizing prompt token overhead[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec][^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4].

# Architecture / Specification

## Progressive Disclosure Mechanics
The skill conforms to the progressive disclosure model of Flue 2.0 and [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md)[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec]:
- **System Prompt Footprint:** Each mounted skill introduces only a single catalog entry line in the initial system prompt[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec].
- **Deferred Loading:** Comprehensive guidance contained in `SKILL.md` is loaded into context only when the language model invokes `activate_skill`[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec]. Supporting files—including output templates (`template.md`) and historical reference reviews (`references/`)—remain unloaded until explicitly requested, avoiding token consumption for unconsulted materials[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec][^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4].

## Schema and Injection Reporting
The skill defines an explicit output schema for issue evaluations that includes explicit fields for adversarial manipulation detection[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901][^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]:
- **`injectionSuspected`:** Boolean flag toggled when prompt injection, persona hijacking, or unauthorized instruction overrides are detected in untrusted issue text[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901][^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4].
- **`injectionNotes`:** Explanatory field documenting the nature, vector, and content of detected manipulation attempts, transforming security events into actionable maintainer telemetry[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901][^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4].
- **Substantive Triage Output:** Structured fields evaluating repository component boundaries, technical merit, dependencies, and alignment with working group standards[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901][^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4].

## Orchestration Tooling
The skill is paired with the `analyze_and_publish` harness tool in `src/tools/analyze-and-publish.ts`[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901][^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec]. When invoked by the agent, this single tool executes the end-to-end integration sequence: fetching issue metadata, evaluating bot authorship (`isBot`), rendering formatted markdown, uploading the Google Doc via Google Drive API multipart uploads, and dispatching announcements to Discord[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901][^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, cross-boundary tracing, and full-stack observability architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical working group tasked with establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry specifications, cross-boundary tracing standards, and full-stack observability frameworks for agentic systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2] Operating under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group standardizes execution telemetry, semantic conventions, and audit trails across language model harnesses, protocol boundaries, runtime environments, and hardware layers.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group structures its core technical investigation and deliverables across specialized focus groups and layered architectural domains:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]

- **Focus Groups**: Technical work is partitioned into open focus groups, including *Protocols and Primitives* and *State, Context, and Reasoning*, coordinating specifications for agent wire protocols, session state, and cognitive context.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]
- **Five-Layer Observability Stack**: The group models agent observability across a five-layer stack spanning hardware accelerators and CPUs, network architecture, operating system runtimes, protocol mediation boundaries, and application-level agent harnesses.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512] A primary focus of the group's gap analysis is addressing limitations in conventional tracing frameworks like [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md), which predominantly capture application-level (Layer 5) spans but lack native cross-layer correlation, session-level replay, and lower-level network and accelerator visibility.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]
- **Behavior Trace Model**: The working group leads development of the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md), defining core semantic conventions and resolving semantic gaps across heterogeneous agent frameworks.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Collaborates with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to define and standardize core observability terms and runtime primitives.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-04-15**: Working group charter approved internally and submitted for Technical Committee review on 2026-04-21.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2]
- **2026-06**: Completed and merged monthly operational report for June 2026.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-14] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-15]
- **2026-07**: Completed and merged monthly operational report for July 2026.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-24]
- **2026-08-19**: Group advanced five-layer observability gap analysis, accepted initial taxonomy terms, and established open focus groups on protocols and primitives as well as state, context, and reasoning.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation framework capturing causal agent execution, tool invocations, approval states, and semantic conventions across execution layers.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and correlation specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to standardize structured observation of causal agent execution, tool invocations, cognitive state changes, and human approval checkpoints.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512] The model establishes vendor-neutral semantic conventions to bridge observability gaps across diverse agent frameworks and multi-layer runtimes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]

# Architecture / Specification

The trace model addresses structural and semantic deficiencies in conventional distributed tracing implementations:

- **Semantic Conventions**: Standardizes formal attribute namespaces and event schemas for agent prompt construction, reasoning phases, context window consumption, tool calls, and state transitions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]
- **Framework Gap Resolution**: Identifies and reconciles semantic gaps across heterogeneous agent frameworks where standard application-level tracing fails to capture agent lifecycle events, multi-turn session tracking, and deterministic replay needs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]
- **Full-Stack Correlation**: Designed to integrate with the [Cross-Boundary Observability Model](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md) and extend beyond application-layer [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) spans, enabling correlation downward into protocol boundaries and runtime layers.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-08-19**: The Observability and Traceability Working Group prioritized populating work items for semantic conventions and identifying semantic gaps in agent frameworks as part of its core trace model specification work.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Six-step operating procedure and governance gates governing project intake, Technical Committee evaluation, and onboarding within the Agentic AI Foundation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Proposal Process defines the operational workflow through which external projects are proposed, evaluated, approved, and onboarded into the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. While the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) serves as the governing authority for lifecycle stages and graduation criteria, this procedure defines the tactical review pipeline, committee engagement requirements, and voting gates managed by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and Governing Board[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

The process defaults to asynchronous, offline execution using GitHub, email, and LFX voting tools to accommodate a globally distributed Technical Committee[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. A foundational principle of the intake procedure is the mandatory engagement bar: a minimum number of Technical Committee members must actively review and comment on a submission before it can advance to a vote, prioritizing broad committee participation over single-champion sponsorship[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

# Architecture / Specification
The proposal workflow encompasses six sequential steps, one parallel contributor agreement gate, and one conditional on-demand presentation sub-step[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]:

1. **Step 1 - Initial Intake**: The CTO conducts initial screening for completeness and charter fit, assisted by an automated intake agent[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. The intake agent executes a public technical compliance check as a comment on the submission ticket and provides a private advisory review to the Technical Committee[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
2. **Step 2 - TC Q&A Window**: An asynchronous review period conducted directly on the GitHub ticket[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. Advancement requires satisfying the engagement bar. If insufficient TC members engage, TC chairs seek an on-demand TC supporter to champion the proposal; if no supporter is identified, the submission is rejected[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
- **Optional Presentation (On Demand)**: A live presentation is scheduled only if explicitly requested by a Technical Committee member[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
- **Contributor Paperwork (Parallel Step)**: Project submitters coordinate with the Linux Foundation PMO to prepare contributor agreements and licensing documentation prior to voting[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
3. **Step 3 - TC Vote**: The Technical Committee votes on project admission and initial lifecycle stage assignment using LFX Vote[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
4. **Step 4 - GB Approval**: The Governing Board confirms organizational readiness, resource allocation, and formal admission via LFX Vote[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
5. **Step 5 - LF Legal Formation**: Linux Foundation Legal and AAIF staff finalize contribution agreements, technical charters, trademark transfers, and asset documentation via DocuSign[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
6. **Step 6 - Technical Onboarding**: Project maintainers and LF IT execute technical infrastructure transfers, repository ownership handover, and CI/CD onboarding[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

# References
- [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md)
- [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agent Observability Use Cases
proposed_concept.description: Catalog defining multi-category agent observability use cases, cross-cutting telemetry requirements, and tamper-evident audit capabilities.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Observability Use Cases catalog defines core functional, operational, and regulatory telemetry requirements across agent execution surfaces, curated by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30]. The document categorizes use cases into diagnostic profiling, interaction tracing, cost monitoring, and regulatory compliance[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].

These requirements inform telemetry specifications such as the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) by establishing concrete technical criteria for verifiable execution across heterogeneous agent frameworks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].

# Architecture / Specification
The safety and compliance cluster addresses auditability, non-repudiation, and judicial defensibility of agent actions:

- **Use Case E4 - Tamper-Evident Evidence for Audit and Dispute Resolution**: Enables regulated entities to furnish mathematically verifiable proof of what an agent actually executed when audited or disputed[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30]. Architectural prerequisites include:
  - Merkle-chained, cryptographically signed event records ensuring sequence integrity[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
  - Write Once, Read Many (WORM) storage targets paired with RFC 3161 trusted timestamps[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
  - Cryptographic linkage binding human [approval checkpoints](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) directly to resulting tool invocation payloads[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
  - Reconciliation mechanisms validating declared agent intents against observed [action records](../taxonomy/action-record.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
  - Adoption of evidence-grade ladders spanning from basic self-declared assertions (E0) to hardware-anchored, third-party attested evidence (E4)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].

# References
- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)
- [Action Record](../taxonomy/action-record.md)
- [Evidence Record Specification](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Inventory documents verified production implementations across enterprise and industrial environments, maintained by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32]. It serves as an empirical reference for evaluating autonomy boundaries, multi-agent coordination models, and external system integrations[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32].

To align workflow modeling with the broader AAIF taxonomy, execution sequences are formally defined as activities rather than steps, harmonizing with standardized [workflow primitives](../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32].

# Architecture / Specification
The catalog organizes verified use cases according to standardized descriptive structures:

- **Domain and Scenario Classification**: Categorization based on organizational function, industry vertical, and operational risk tiers[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32].
- **Activity Sequences**: Structured decomposition of agentic workflows into atomic, inspectable activities representing discrete tool invocations, reasoning phases, or coordination actions[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32].
- **Governance Boundaries**: Explicit demarcation of policy enforcement points, including [human approval gates](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) and automated acceptance gates[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32].

# References
- [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy defining entry requirements and progression stages across Sandbox, Growth, and Impact for hosted AAIF projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Lifecycle Policy governs the entry requirements, maturity progression, and periodic evaluation of technical initiatives hosted within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-technical-committee-pr-9]. Enacted by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the policy establishes objective criteria for evaluating project health, open governance adoption, and ecosystem utility[^evt-technical-committee-pr-9].

Day-to-day intake execution and committee review procedures for prospective projects are specified in the [Project Proposal Process](../policies/project-proposal-process.md)[^evt-technical-committee-pr-9].

# Architecture / Specification
The lifecycle model delineates progressive maturity tiers:

- **Sandbox**: Entry stage for exploratory, experimental, or newly formed open-source initiatives seeking foundational alignment with AAIF technical scope and open governance standards[^evt-technical-committee-pr-9].
- **Growth**: Stage for projects demonstrating measurable production adoption, diverse multi-organizational contribution, active release velocity, and adherence to security guidelines[^evt-technical-committee-pr-9].
- **Impact**: Highest maturity tier for mission-critical, widely deployed industry standards with broad institutional backing and self-sustaining governance.
- **Emeritus**: Terminal phase for completed or superseded projects transitioned into archival maintenance.

# References
- [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)
- [Project Proposal Process](../policies/project-proposal-process.md)
