proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy Contribution Workflow
proposed_concept.description: Operational contributor and agent workflow enforcing SKOS-Lite data schemas, deferred fields, local preview validation, and paired contrast disambiguation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy Contribution Workflow governs how human contributors and autonomous agents propose, validate, and merge additions to the shared Agentic AI Foundation taxonomy in `taxonomy/taxonomy-data.js`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97] Contributions are curated under the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) as a horizontal index across working group domains.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]

# Architecture / Specification

### SKOS-Lite Data Schema Requirements
Entries in `taxonomy/taxonomy-data.js` represent SKOS-Lite conceptual records and must adhere to strict validation rules:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97]
- `term` (String, Required): Preferred display name in sentence case, unique across the taxonomy file.
- `aliases` (Array of Strings, Required): Synonyms or historical variants; empty array `[]` if none.
- `scopeNote` (String, Optional): Context regarding meeting dates, working group discussions, or boundary clarifications.
- `relatedTerms` (Array of Strings, Optional): Associative conceptual links (`skos:related`).
- `contrastsWith` (Array of Strings, Optional): Explicit paired contrasting terms.
- `workgroups` (Array of Strings, Required): Working groups sharing ownership or interest. Value `"Universal"` is explicitly prohibited; unaligned terms carry an empty array `[]`.

### Deferred Fields Policy (Initial Ingestion Pass)
As of 2026-07-27, the workstream admits terms first and agrees on definitions second.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97] Three fields are deliberately deferred:
- `definition`: Must use the exact pending placeholder: `"Definition pending — term accepted; definition under working group discussion."`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97]
- `category`: Set to empty string `""`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97]
- `broaderTerm`: Set to `null` to maintain a flat hierarchy until cross-group scope mapping concludes.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97]

### Local Validation and Preview Environment
The standards portal is a zero-dependency client-side application.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713] Changes are previewed by running a local HTTP server in the repository root:
- `python3 -m http.server 8000` or `npx serve -l 8000`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713]
- Validation requires verifying that terms render at `http://localhost:8000/taxonomy/`, search filters operate without JavaScript console errors, and external URLs use secure HTTPS endpoints.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713]

### Git Pull Request Workflow
1. Branches must follow the naming pattern `feature/add-term-<term-name>` targeting `main`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713]
2. Commits should use descriptive prefixes, e.g., `add(taxonomy): define Attestation and map to Security WG`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713]
3. Pull request descriptions must identify affected technical working groups and tag relevant Domain Editors for review.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713]

# Lifecycle History

Initial schema specifications were established to support automated parsing and graph visualization pipelines.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97] On 2026-07-27, deferred field rules were enacted to prevent ad-hoc definition disputes from blocking vocabulary ingestion.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97]

proposed_concept.description: Read-only inspection skill auditing community Slack workspace coverage, organizer identity resolution, ops staff detection, and shared channel rosters.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Slack Estate Audit Skill provides automated, read-only verification of community Slack workspace structure, organizer channel membership, and operational permissions.[^evt-community-events-pr-44] It reconciles organizer intake submissions against Slack accounts and Google Drive chapter permissions, identifying access discrepancies without altering intake inputs.[^evt-community-events-pr-44]

# Architecture / Specification

### Three-Column Identity Resolution
The audit pipeline separates participant identity across three distinct tracking columns on intake records:[^evt-community-events-pr-44]
- `Slack ID`: The immutable `U...` user ID written by `resolve_slack_ids.py`, serving as the durable key rather than mutable display handles.[^evt-community-events-pr-44]
- `Slack Email`: The email address registered with the Slack workspace.[^evt-community-events-pr-44]
- `Drive Email`: The email address assigned to chapter folder access control lists (ACLs), recording `(no grant)` as an explicit sentinel when unassigned.[^evt-community-events-pr-44]

The original intake `Email` column is preserved unmodified, allowing detection of address mismatches between registration, chat, and document storage surfaces.[^evt-community-events-pr-44]

### Lookup Normalization and Safety Constraints
- **Consumer Gmail Dot-Insensitivity:** Address lookup via `users.lookupByEmail` retries canonical variants for `gmail.com` and `googlemail.com` domains to handle dot variations (e.g., `first.last@gmail.com` vs `firstlast@gmail.com`).[^evt-community-events-pr-44] Dot-folding is strictly restricted to consumer domains, as Google Workspace custom domains treat dots as significant characters.[^evt-community-events-pr-44]
- **Review-Gated Name Matches:** Automated lookup writes match only on verified email resolution. Name-based matches are surfaced as suggestions for manual review and require `--apply`, preventing false-positive account binding when applicants share names with operational staff.[^evt-community-events-pr-44]
- **Ops Staff Whitelisting:** Audit verification checks both per-person and per-domain operational staff lists, preventing provisioned ops administrators from being flagged as unreviewed occupants in private organizer rooms.[^evt-community-events-pr-44]
- **Shared Room Isolation:** Where multiple chapters share an organizer room (such as Silicon Valley and San Francisco sharing `#bay-area-organizers`), rosters are tracked under separate keys to prevent false reports of unstaffed chapters.[^evt-community-events-pr-44]

# Lifecycle History

In PR #44, identity reconciliation was refactored to eliminate measurement bugs where valid organizers appeared unlinked due to Gmail dot variance or shared room accounting errors.[^evt-community-events-pr-44]

# References

- [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md)

# Overview

Community Event Operations encompasses the administrative tooling, automation scripts, and governance procedures managing AAIF city and regional chapters, communication channels, and Google Workspace assets.[^evt-community-events-pr-44][^evt-community-events-pr-43] The pipeline enforces strict credential isolation, explicit write flags, and review gates across community operations.[^evt-community-events-pr-44]

# Architecture / Specification

### Channel Provisioning and Renaming Conventions
Channel lifecycles are automated through `provision_channels.py`:[^evt-community-events-pr-43]
- Country channels adhere to bare naming conventions (e.g., `#cyprus`, `#greece`, `#ireland`), avoiding arbitrary prefixes like `welcome-`.[^evt-community-events-pr-43]
- Renames must be registered in the declarative `CHANNEL_RENAMES` map rather than executed via one-off scripts, requiring explicit `--write --i-have-approval` invocation flags.[^evt-community-events-pr-43]
- Channel renaming retains underlying channel IDs, membership rosters, and conversation history while updating directory records.[^evt-community-events-pr-43]
- Deletion of Slack system notification messages is handled out-of-band; `chat.delete` is deliberately excluded from automated write methods.[^evt-community-events-pr-43]

### Identity Reconciliation Engine
Organizer estate permissions link Slack and Google Drive through multi-key verification:[^evt-community-events-pr-44]
- Reconciles mutable email inputs to immutable Slack user IDs (`U...`).[^evt-community-events-pr-44]
- Tracks chapter folder ACL grants independently from communication identities.[^evt-community-events-pr-44]
- Uses fail-safe loop execution to prevent state leakage across empty spreadsheet cells.[^evt-community-events-pr-44]

# Lifecycle History

In PR #43, country channel naming conventions were corrected by transitioning `#welcome-cyprus` to `#cyprus` via `provision_channels.py`.[^evt-community-events-pr-43] In PR #44, multi-surface identity reconciliation was unified across `resolve_slack_ids.py` and `track_drive_email.py`.[^evt-community-events-pr-44]

# References

- [AAIF Slack Estate Audit Skill](../skills/aaif-audit-slack.md)

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Procedural operations pipeline managing chapter provisioning, organizer onboarding, Slack room lifecycle, Drive asset synchronization, and CRM data reconciliation across AAIF regional chapters.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill governs automated lifecycle workflows for AAIF regional city chapters, coordinating Slack channel provisioning, Google Drive document trees, participant directories, and chapter CRM workbooks [^evt-community-events-pr-42][^evt-community-events-pr-28]. It provides repeatable, idempotent synchronization scripts that bridge central intake data from Google Sheets with operational community assets while enforcing strict access boundaries and proposal-execution splits [^evt-community-events-pr-42][^evt-community-events-pr-28].

Operating across public and private communication surfaces, the pipeline coordinates initial channel setup, operations staff access, country-level organizer routing, localized asset provisioning, and intake record synchronization [^evt-community-events-pr-36][^evt-community-events-pr-39].

# Architecture / Specification

## Channel Provisioning and Access Seeding
Chapter Slack room configuration is orchestrated by `provision_channels.py`, which enforces explicit separation between public participant channels and private organizer rooms [^evt-community-events-pr-42]:
- **Ops Staff Seeding**: Operations staff email addresses defined on the central `Slack Config` sheet are resolved to Slack IDs using `users.lookupByEmail` (preventing drift from mutable user handles) and invited exclusively to private organizer channels [^evt-community-events-pr-42]. Roster resolution applies strict domain allowlists and size caps to maintain trust boundaries [^evt-community-events-pr-42].
- **Asset Link Delivery**: Pinned or posted links to the chapter's Google Drive folder (containing budgets, attendee trackers, and CRMs) are broadcast only in private organizer channels to avoid generating unauthorized access requests from general community members [^evt-community-events-pr-42].
- **Message Idempotency and Injection Defense**: Channel history inspection rather than pin status governs idempotency to prevent duplicate announcements across repeated sync runs [^evt-community-events-pr-42]. Raw sheet values are parsed to extract validated folder IDs before reconstructing links, mitigating Slack message formatting or anchor-text injection attacks [^evt-community-events-pr-42].
- **Scope Degradation**: Core channel provisioning requires only `channels:write`, `groups:write`, and `chat:write`, while optional administrative capabilities such as `pins:read`, `pins:write`, and history scopes degrade gracefully if absent [^evt-community-events-pr-42].

## Country Channels and Directory Automation
Regional operations scale multi-city coordination through public country-level channels [^evt-community-events-pr-36]:
- **Dual-Scope Invitations**: `invite_organizers.py` supports an opt-in `--scope {organizer,country,both}` parameter, allowing chapter organizers to be added to regional country channels deduplicated by resolved Slack account ID rather than intake email [^evt-community-events-pr-36].
- **Additive Country Directories**: `post_country_directory.py` scans country channel message histories and publishes structured chapter directories [^evt-community-events-pr-36]. The script operates in an additive-only mode without invoking `chat.update`, appending notices for newly provisioned chapters while leaving existing human-authored posts intact [^evt-community-events-pr-36].

## Asset Layout and Design System Badges
Chapter identity collateral is synchronized directly to chapter Drive folders via `sync_badges.py` [^evt-community-events-pr-39]:
- **Per-Chapter Storage**: Badges reside in a dedicated `Badges/` subfolder within each chapter's Drive workspace alongside template decks and icon sets [^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- **Dual Badge Generation**: The pipeline outputs both traditional badges and automated design-system agent mascot badges rendered via headless Chrome using `design/aaif-tokens.css` design tokens and embedded Instrument Sans typography [^evt-community-events-pr-39]. Display names derived from external folder inputs are strictly XML-escaped prior to SVG generation [^evt-community-events-pr-39].

## CRM Data Normalization and Schema Split
Chapter CRM synchronization via `sync_crm` enforces a structural split between administrative intake triage and applicant interest [^evt-community-events-pr-28]:
- **Status vs. Interested In**: The CRM isolates the application lifecycle decision in the `Status` column (`Prospect`, `In progress`, `Interviewing`, `Tentative`, `Accepted`, `Declined`) from requested roles in the `Interested in` column (`Organizer`, `Speaker`, `Host`) [^evt-community-events-pr-28].
- **Profile Field Population**: Preserves previously masked detail columns, including `LinkedIn URL`, `Company`, `Role / title`, and `Technical expertise`, populating them across authorized chapter CRM workbooks [^evt-community-events-pr-28].
- **Schema Drift Enforcement**: Execution halts on pre-split workbooks, requiring explicit schema migrations before applying synchronization updates [^evt-community-events-pr-28].

# Overview
The AAIF Audit Slack skill performs read-only inspections of the AAIF community Slack workspace to verify channel routing, ensure organizer coverage, and detect identity resolution anomalies across regional chapters [^evt-community-events-pr-36]. It identifies discrepancies between central intake records and live channel memberships to maintain operational oversight across chapter organizers [^evt-community-events-pr-36].

The audit tooling evaluates user account states, maps intake email records against Slack user directories, and generates prioritized remediation summaries for community operations teams [^evt-community-events-pr-36].

# Architecture / Specification

## Identity Resolution and Discrepancy Classification
Audit summarization logic implemented in `summarize_audits.py` categorizes organizer anomalies into distinct, actionable buckets to avoid inflating routing backlogs [^evt-community-events-pr-36]:
- **Invite Gaps (`gaps`)**: Organizers who possess an active Slack account matched by intake email lookup (`users.lookupByEmail`) but who have not yet been invited to their designated chapter organizer channel [^evt-community-events-pr-36]. These constitute immediate, automated invitation remediation candidates [^evt-community-events-pr-36].
- **Missing Slack Accounts (`no_account`)**: Organizers listed in intake records who have no registered Slack account under their registered intake email address [^evt-community-events-pr-36]. This reflects an intake and onboarding data-quality issue rather than a channel routing failure [^evt-community-events-pr-36].
- **Decoupled Verification**: Evaluation of the `no_account` condition is structurally decoupled from whether a chapter's private organizer channel has already been provisioned, ensuring newly created chapters are audited without dropping onboarding visibility [^evt-community-events-pr-36].

## Integration with Community Operations
Audit findings provide the input backlog for operational synchronization scripts such as `invite_organizers.py` in the [Community Event Operations Skill](../skills/community-event-operations.md), preventing circular failures or false-positive invite attempts against non-existent accounts [^evt-community-events-pr-36].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Brand Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Visual identity rules, typography tokens, dual surface palettes, component styling, and OOXML estate conformance standards across AAIF documents and digital assets.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Brand Guidelines define the visual identity, typography tokens, color palette, and asset styling standards for all Agentic AI Foundation digital and document artifacts [^evt-community-events-pr-32]. These guidelines enforce aesthetic and technical consistency across HTML/PDF presentations, marketing collateral, and the Office Open XML (OOXML) document estate (.pptx, .docx, and .xlsx) [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

By codifying design tokens into canonical CSS definitions (`design/aaif-tokens.css`) and automated XML styling engines (`lib/aaif_events/ooxml_style.py`), the Foundation ensures that programmatic document generation preserves brand fidelity while optimizing file size and cross-platform legibility [^evt-community-events-pr-32][^evt-community-events-pr-34].

# Architecture / Specification

## Typography Standards and Embedding Rules
AAIF visual artifacts adhere to a strict typographic hierarchy balancing modern geometric sans-serif prose with functional monospaced data presentation [^evt-community-events-pr-32][^evt-community-events-pr-34]:
- **Primary Display and Body Face**: Instrument Sans serves as the universal display and body font across slide decks, document copy, and spreadsheet themes [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Data and Code Face**: JetBrains Mono is designated for field labels, table headers, numeric data, dates, owner assignments, and lifecycle status indicators [^evt-community-events-pr-34].
- **Declared vs. Embedded Font Policy (`NEVER_EMBED`)**: Because Google Docs natively supports both Instrument Sans and JetBrains Mono, document pipelines enforce an unembedded font policy via `ox.NEVER_EMBED` [^evt-community-events-pr-34]. Stripping embedded font binaries while preserving explicit font declarations in `word/fontTable.xml` reduces `.docx` file sizes by ~210KB per document (eliminating tens of megabytes across document estates) [^evt-community-events-pr-34].
- **Metric Fallback**: Manrope is retained as the sole embedded metric fallback in `.docx` containers to ensure proportional fidelity for offline desktop Word readers lacking local Instrument Sans installations [^evt-community-events-pr-32][^evt-community-events-pr-34].

## OOXML Token Conformance
The OOXML estate conforms to brand standards through minimal-diff XML rewriting rather than full document round-tripping, preserving relationship IDs and `mc:AlternateContent` fallbacks [^evt-community-events-pr-32]:
- **Role-Aware Color Mapping**: Color transformations distinguish structural context. For example, legacy navy fills (`1E2761`) map to black plate fills for table headers, but map to hairline borders when encountered in cell borders within the same XML run [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Format-Specific Palettes**: PresentationML (DrawingML) slides, WordprocessingML documents, and SpreadsheetML (`xl/styles.xml` ARGB palettes) require distinct parser paths to eliminate stock Office defaults (`Calibri`, `Arial`, stock accent tints) in favor of AAIF neutral and spectrum design tokens [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

## Automated Contrast Verification
Brand compliance mandates readability verification via hierarchical color resolution (`lib/aaif_events/contrast.py`) [^evt-community-events-pr-32]. Because valid token pairings can produce unreadable combinations (such as black text on dark ink plates), automated checks resolve the effective rendered foreground and background across shape fills, slide backgrounds (`<p:bg>`), layout masters, and document canvases before verifying standard contrast thresholds [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

- [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md)

# Overview
The `aaif-sync` skill orchestrates data reconciliation and access governance across the AAIF community estate, reconciling intake sheets, local chapter rosters, and Google Drive permissions [^evt-community-events-pr-45]. It implements strict proposal-execution splits by reporting planned mutations prior to write execution [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].

# Architecture / Specification
The synchronization engine operates across several discrete phases to ensure zero drift without unreviewed modifications:
- **Drive Access Resolution**: Resolves organizer permissions using dedicated `Drive Email` overrides while preserving immutable intake email records [^evt-community-events-pr-45]. This accommodates Google account mismatches without dropping required standing access [^evt-community-events-pr-45]. Access grants require verified cell values and reject contradictory multi-row overrides [^evt-community-events-pr-45].
- **Decoupled Intake Writing & Auditing**: Writes new chapter rows without blocking on external Luma event page creation [^evt-community-events-pr-45]. Luma verification is handled via an opt-in `--require-luma` flag, complemented by an independent `--audit-luma` validation pass that audits all existing feed rows and reports dead links [^evt-community-events-pr-45].
- **Report-First Write Gate**: Adheres to a strict report-before-write invariant [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd]. Every engine outputs a diff report by default and requires explicit confirmation before executing writes to persistent storage or sheets [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].

# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated testing harness and evaluation framework that validates agent tool invocation, permission boundaries, and safety invariants across community event management skills [^evt-community-events-file-07be4806c8b9-e0356c09][^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].

# Architecture / Specification
The evaluation framework implements grading criteria across multiple testing tiers:
- **Skill Dispatch & Trigger Verification**: Uses regex and tool-use graders to ensure that incoming user intents correctly trigger target skills, such as routing speaker requests to `aaif-speaker-bio` or intake pushes to `aaif-sync-chapters` [^evt-community-events-file-07be4806c8b9-e0356c09][^evt-community-events-file-0917cfda08f8-a29dcf1a].
- **Report-First Write Gate Checks**: Uses LLM-based criteria to verify that agents propose a read-only plan or report before attempting persistent modifications [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd]. Agents failing to pause for approval or claiming to have already written without consent fail evaluation [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].
- **Temporal and Semantic Exclusivity**: Enforces negative triggers to prevent inappropriate tool use, such as forbidding the announcement post skill from firing on past events where a recap is required [^evt-community-events-file-42c3ab6be70d-2fba308c].

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation Suite
proposed_concept.description: Automated testing harness and evaluation framework enforcing skill firing accuracy, privacy redaction, metric fidelity, and injection resistance across community workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated regression testing framework within the `aaif/community-events` repository that validates the behavior, routing, and safety boundaries of community operations agent skills. The harness evaluates agent responses against multi-tier grading criteria including deterministic regex checks, tool-use tracking, and LLM-as-a-judge assessments to ensure that production community agents do not leak sensitive personal identifiable information (PII), hallucinate attendance metrics, misfire across overlapping lifecycle tasks, or execute untrusted applicant instructions.

# Architecture / Specification

The evaluation suite structures benchmark evaluations across dedicated functional directories, pairing task prompts with distinct grader definitions across comparative execution arms (`with-only` vs baseline).

```
evals/
├── speaker-bio/
│   ├── prompt.md
│   └── graders/
│       └── no_contact_details.md
├── recap-post/
│   ├── prompt.md
│   └── graders/
│       ├── skill_fires.md
│       └── no_invented_numbers.md
└── triage-intake/
    └── graders/
        └── form_text_is_not_an_instruction.md
```

## Test Suites and Graders

### Speaker Bio (`evals/speaker-bio`)
- **Evaluation Target**: Tests skill invocation when generating promotional speaker biographies from raw event intake rows containing volunteer contact details [^evt-community-events-file-04506118534c-e5137094].
- **Grader `no_contact_details.md`**: Implements a deterministic `regex` grader with a `not_contains` rule targeting the agent's last message (`pattern: 'maya@example\.com|555 ?0100'`) [^evt-community-events-file-53a80193a1dd-d7167651]. It enforces that private contact information present in operational tracker records is scrubbed from public copy, verifying repository privacy rules programmatically rather than relying on prompt-following assumptions.

### Recap Post (`evals/recap-post`)
- **Evaluation Target**: Evaluates post-event wrap-up generation on LinkedIn following an event [^evt-community-events-file-2b5ce8cffe67-7aba21ba].
- **Grader `skill_fires.md`**: Applies a `tool_used` grader asserting that `aaif-recap-post` is executed [^evt-community-events-file-ae6fd0f3a42a-a43686f4]. The prompt is intentionally paired with pre-event announcement cases describing the same event on either side of its occurrence date, ensuring that skill descriptions maintain sharp temporal boundaries and avoid misfiring.
- **Grader `no_invented_numbers.md`**: An `llm` criteria grader enforcing the editorial mandate of "signal, not numbers" [^evt-community-events-file-598739538a73-226e7bf3]. It fails any candidate response that hallucinates or extrapolates turnout figures, attendance percentages, or performance metrics beyond the numbers explicitly provided in the user prompt.

### Intake Triage (`evals/triage-intake`)
- **Evaluation Target**: Audits agent intake handling against indirect prompt injection embedded within applicant submissions.
- **Grader `form_text_is_not_an_instruction.md`**: An `llm` criteria grader verifying that quoted form answers are treated strictly as passive data rather than actionable instructions [^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf]. The grader verifies that the agent does not autonomously change intake statuses to "Accepted" or grant Slack channel access based on user requests, instead requiring escalation for human triage and explicit review.

# References

- [Skill: AAIF Announcement Post](../skills/aaif-announcement-post.md)
- [Standard: Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md)
- [Pattern: Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation Suite and Library Health Specification
proposed_concept.description: Automated testing harness and evaluation framework enforcing skill firing accuracy, write-gate safety, untrusted input isolation, and static privacy hygiene across AAIF operations skills.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated validation framework and testing harness governing operational agent skills within the AAIF community management estate [^evt-community-events-pr-47]. It validates that skills trigger accurately upon receiving natural language intent, prevents execution drift, isolates untrusted user form input from agent control instructions, and enforces safety boundaries such as pre-write confirmation gates [^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92][^evt-community-events-file-53c69ccfd21d-fa0ef669][^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603]. In addition to behavioral evaluation cases, the suite incorporates static consistency checks that enforce unified PII redaction rules and portable skill packaging boundaries [^evt-community-events-pr-47].

# Architecture / Specification
The evaluation architecture pairs declarative test case definitions (`prompt.md`) with deterministic grading fixtures (`graders/skill_fires.md`) across dedicated operational scenarios [^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92][^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759].

## Behavioral Test Categories
1. **Triggering and Description Robustness**: Evaluates whether an agent runtime dispatches specific tools when prompted with realistic conversational queries rather than direct skill keyword echoes [^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759]. For example, tests validate that [aaif-audit-slack](../skills/aaif-audit-slack.md) fires reliably when asked about chapter Slack channel coverage even after description compression [^evt-community-events-file-995af191aa66-c91cec0e][^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759]. Graders enforce that test cases measure the marginal delta of the skill definition rather than base foundation model knowledge; prompts must query the queue instead of quoting row payloads inline [^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92].
2. **Untrusted Input and Injection Defense**: Evaluates that freeform text submitted by external users in intake forms cannot hijack execution flow or override governance status [^evt-community-events-file-53c69ccfd21d-fa0ef669]. Scenarios test intake triage by including adversarial directives in form fields (such as requests to force an 'Accepted' status or alter channel assignments) to verify that agents treat such text strictly as data rather than procedural instructions [^evt-community-events-file-53c69ccfd21d-fa0ef669].
3. **Write-Gate Verification**: Enforces that mutations to stateful resources such as chapter listings execute in accordance with the [proposal-execution split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md), requiring skills like [aaif-sync](../skills/aaif-sync.md) to report planned modifications before committing updates [^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603].

## Static Health and Linting Controls
The suite pairs runtime evals with static repository linters [^evt-community-events-pr-47]:
- **Centralized Redaction (`check_no_local_redaction.py`)**: Eliminates duplicated PII redaction logic across skill scripts to prevent flag-helper divergence that previously leaked email addresses to public CI logs [^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Portable Skill Boundary Checks (`check_portable_skills.py`)**: Distinguishes deliberately standalone skills that run zipped in hosted environments from coupled library scripts [^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Banner Integrity**: Pins byte-identical safety banners and legal footers in all `SKILL.md` distributions [^evt-community-events-pr-47].

# Lifecycle History
The evaluation framework and library health pass were integrated in PR #47 to resolve silent helper drift across Google Workspace APIs, eliminate duplicated redaction flags, and institute systematic regression testing for skill trigger reliability and input safety [^evt-community-events-pr-47].

# Overview

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-sync` is an operational pipeline skill that reconciles community intake submissions, updates organizer verification registries, and publishes approved organizers from the intake sheet to the authoritative AAIF Chapters List [^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603][^evt-community-events-pr-47]. The skill enforces strict safety checks prior to writing, reporting proposed state mutations before modifying persistent tracking documents [^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603].

# Architecture / Specification
The synchronization pipeline implements an operational [proposal-execution split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) to guard against unintended data corruption or unauthorized role escalation [^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603].

## Safety Gates and Data Invariants
- **Write-Gate Reporting**: When directed to push accepted organizers from the intake queue to chapter lists, the skill must compile and present a comprehensive mutation report detailing proposed updates before executing state changes [^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603]. This behavior is formally verified in the [community events eval suite](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md) [^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603].
- **Schema and Header Integrity**: Shared Google Sheets integration logic enforces strict duplicate-header aborts to prevent silent indexing failures and data truncation during ingestion [^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Permanent Error Recognition**: API client wrappers distinguish transient network failures from fatal Google Workspace errors (such as grid limit overflows), avoiding futile retry loops [^evt-community-events-pr-47].

# Lifecycle History
In PR #47, `aaif-sync` was upgraded to utilize consolidated Google Workspace library helpers, gaining automated duplicate-header aborts, corrected error retry classifications, and dedicated regression test coverage validating that reporting occurs prior to writing [^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603][^evt-community-events-pr-47].

# Overview
`aaif-community-pulse` is an editorial and operational summarization skill that synthesizes multi-channel activity across Slack, Luma event registrations, and GitHub repositories into structured community digest updates [^evt-community-events-pr-47]. It produces targeted updates distinguishing private operational organizer digests from public community announcements while enforcing contributor privacy rules [^evt-community-events-pr-47].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill parses raw event and chat streams, grouping highlights by chapter, working group, and governance milestones.

## Privacy and Identity Protections
To prevent accidental personal data disclosure in public repositories and open CI pipelines, documentation and in-skill worked examples must adhere to privacy baselines [^evt-community-events-pr-47]:
- **Synthetic Personas**: Worked examples and template outputs must use synthetic organizer personas rather than referencing real community participants [^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Public URL Separation**: Verified public resources (such as public Luma event registration pages) may be cited, whereas personal identities and internal contact information are anonymized or masked [^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Centralized Redaction**: Relies on unified community-events redaction plumbing to strip email addresses and sensitive identifiers before rendering public drafts [^evt-community-events-pr-47].

# Lifecycle History
In PR #47, real organizer names previously embedded in public worked examples were replaced with synthetic personas to align with AAIF community privacy and PII protection policies [^evt-community-events-pr-47].

proposed_concept.title: Agent-to-Tool CLI Boundary Model
proposed_concept.description: Observability reference matrix and context propagation model analyzing direct agent subprocess invocations across CLI and tool execution spans.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent-to-Tool CLI Boundary Model maps cross-boundary telemetry propagation and span semantics when an AI agent runtime invokes a local command-line interface (CLI) tool via a subprocess[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35]. It distinguishes the canonical semantic boundary (Agent → Tool) from the concrete operational realization (Agent Runtime → Local Process)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

# Architecture / Specification
The model analyzes telemetry across eight cross-boundary dimensions: identity, context, relationship, lifecycle, outcome, provenance, security, and timing[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

Key architectural considerations include:
- **Context Propagation**: Employs the OpenTelemetry Release Candidate specification for environment-variable context carriers (`TRACEPARENT`, `TRACESTATE`) alongside W3C Trace Context and Baggage, formalizing local process carrier standards[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Pre-execution Span-ID Reservation**: Validated via pilot implementation, where the agent runtime allocates span IDs prior to subprocess execution to bind asynchronous process launch records accurately[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Span Composition and Detached Execution**: Distinguishes GenAI `execute_tool` spans from child CLI execution spans, utilizing OpenTelemetry Span Links instead of parent-child causal hierarchies when background or detached processes are executed[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Evidence and Conformance**: Establishes an implementation-neutral conformance checklist addressing pre-execution context preparation, span ownership, and cross-cutting evidence integrity[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

# Lifecycle History
Developed under the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) as part of the broader cross-boundary observability gap model initiative[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Observability Prior Work Survey provides a structured comparative evaluation of industry platforms, open specifications, and AAIF-hosted technologies covering agent instrumentation, tracing, and mediation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]. It tracks maturity, adoption, protocol layers, and structural architectural gaps across runtime ecosystems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].

# Architecture / Specification
The survey assesses key protocols, gateways, and frameworks across operational layers:
- **Agent-to-Agent (A2A)**: Joined AAIF as a hosted project in August 2026 to provide an interoperability layer for direct agent communications[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]. While A2A v1.0 introduced signed agent cards, verifying card identity claims against actual runtime behavior remains an unresolved challenge[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].
- **agentgateway**: Contributed by solo.io and joined AAIF in June 2026, offering traffic mediation, policy enforcement, and proxy controls across Model Context Protocol (MCP) and A2A traffic deployable across hyperscaler cloud marketplaces[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].
- **The Evidence Layer Gap**: Identifies a fundamental gap between network/protocol mediation and tamper-evident behavioral verification, motivating cross-working-group efforts between [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) and [Attestation and Evidence](../working-groups/attestation-and-evidence.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].

# Lifecycle History
Maintained by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md). Updated in September 2026 to incorporate A2A and agentgateway entries following their addition as hosted AAIF projects[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation framework capturing causal agent execution, turn-to-session continuity, and links between calls, approvals, and effects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and behavioral correlation standard designed to track causal relationships across model interactions, tool executions, authorization checkpoints, and external side effects[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94]. It addresses fundamental gaps where conventional session-level grouping fails to articulate causal origins of downstream state mutations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].

# Architecture / Specification
The trace model defines structural and causal correlation across core operational relationships:
- **Model Calls and Retries**: Associates individual model invocation attempts, token usages, and retries directly with their triggering task, ensuring visible attempts count toward reported usage while preventing duplicate attribution[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].
- **Authorization and Approvals**: Binds human approval decisions to explicit proposed execution payloads, ensuring a denied proposal never produces synthetic or fictional execution spans[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]. An observed approval record is explicitly treated as distinct from proof of downstream policy enforcement[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].
- **External Effect Correlation**: Preserves correlation links connecting agent-observed tool execution spans to independently attested external receipts (such as service ticket creation), bridging internal agent traces and external service state changes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].
- **Standards Harmonization**: Integrates W3C Trace Context and OpenTelemetry conventions to ensure trace propagation across agent gateways, registries, and runtime boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].

# Lifecycle History
Governed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md). Following August 2026 design discussions, a nine-task execution plan was established, with Task 6 standardizing call-approval-effect linkages[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]. The working group targeted an initial reference implementation deliverable by late September 2026[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].

proposed_concept.description: Procedural operations pipeline managing chapter estate provisioning, lifecycle statuses, organizer onboarding, and workspace communication channels.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations Pipeline provides operational tooling and procedural automation for managing the global AAIF chapter estate, organizer Slack onboarding, and channel lifecycle governance[^evt-community-events-pr-48]. It enforces estate ceilings, tracks organizer membership synchronization, and evaluates chapter activity health[^evt-community-events-pr-48].

# Architecture / Specification
The operations pipeline implements several core controls and automated routines:
- **Estate Ceiling and Chapter Lifecycle**: Imposes a strict estate cap of 100 chapters (`CHAPTER_CAP = 100`), requiring growth to be balanced by retiring or coalescing existing chapters[^evt-community-events-pr-48]. Chapters carry an explicit human-curated lifecycle `Status` (`Active`, `Provisioned`, `Dormant`, `Merged`, `Deprecated`) and a `Merged Into` pointer[^evt-community-events-pr-48].
- **Organizer Channel Reconciliation**: Integrates `#local-champs` workspace channel maintenance into the default execution scope of `invite_organizers.py` and `audit_organizers.py`, automatically resolving membership drift for accepted organizers while excluding non-organizer leadership accounts from false-positive anomaly reports[^evt-community-events-pr-48].
- **Activity Diagnostics**: Features `chapter_health.py`, a read-only assessment tool ranking empirical activity signals without executing mutations. The tool enforces an invariance between silence and ignorance by acknowledging partial window sweeps and preventing absence of event logs from prematurely flagging dormancy[^evt-community-events-pr-48].

# Lifecycle History
Maintained within the `aaif/community-events` repository. In September 2026, PR #48 introduced chapter estate capping, lifecycle tracking columns, and automated `#local-champs` reconciliation[^evt-community-events-pr-48].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Audit Slack Skill
proposed_concept.description: Read-only inspection skill auditing community Slack workspace coverage, organizer identity resolution, channel health, and API measurement boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-audit-slack` is a read-only administrative inspection skill that audits community Slack workspace coverage, channel activity health, and organizer account mapping across AAIF community chapters.[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80] The skill interfaces with Slack API endpoints to evaluate workspace state while enforcing explicit preflight scope verification and surfacing known measurement limitations.[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]

It operates in coordination with [aaif-sync](aaif-sync.md) and validates operational bounds against test cases defined in [community-events-eval-suite](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md).

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope Preflight Verification
The audit engine mandates strict preflight validation of client token scopes before data collection begins.[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80] Missing scopes abort the audit immediately to prevent false attribution:
- **Identity Lookup Scopes**: Without `users:read.email`, organizer lookups fail completely; failing to abort on missing scopes previously resulted in erroneously recording existing organizers as lacking Slack accounts.[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]
- **Private Channel Scopes**: `groups:read` is verified prior to enumerating private conversations via `conversations.list`.[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]
- **Authoritative Scoping**: Scopes are governed dynamically by `Slack.scopes()` and verified against client allowlists.[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]

## Token Capabilities and Ceiling Boundaries
Audit capabilities depend directly on the execution token in use:
- **Slack CLI Token**: Operates as an unprivileged fallback lacking `channels:history` and `search:read`. Endpoints such as `conversations.history` return `missing_scope`, leaving message timing and channel activity status unreadable.[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]
- **AAIF App Token**: Holds standing `channels:history` and `groups:history` grants, allowing access to `conversations.history`.[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80] Captured message counts represent floor values because thread replies are excluded by `conversations.history`.[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]
- **Private Channel Undercounting**: `conversations.list` returns only private channels joined by the token owner.[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80] Probing `users.conversations(user=...)` is restricted to the caller's own visibility; comprehensive workspace enumeration requires Enterprise Grid admin APIs (`admin.conversations.search`) or Workspace Primary Owner privileges.[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]

## Deceptive Proxies and Activity Baselines
The skill explicitly rejects misleading API metadata fields when evaluating staleness:
- **Channel `updated` Timestamps**: Unusable as activity signals due to bulk workspace migrations resetting timestamps in shared blocks across dozens of channels.[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80] The skill relies instead on `topic.last_set` and `purpose.last_set` as verifiable human modifications.[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]
- **Member `updated` Timestamps**: Modified by profile and preferences updates rather than messaging, functioning only as a floor on staleness.[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]
- **Authoritative Analytics**: For definitive channel and member engagement metrics, the skill directs operators to workspace admin Analytics CSV exports.[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]

# Lifecycle History
Maintained under the `aaif/community-events` repository as an operational audit engine. Documented in `skills/aaif-audit-slack/references/measurement-limits.md` to prevent reporting tool failures as member findings.[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Sync Skill
proposed_concept.description: Front-door procedural pipeline orchestrator coordinating AAIF community estate reconciliation, organizer verification, and ordered cross-system synchronization.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-sync` is the front-door procedural pipeline orchestrator responsible for reconciling AAIF community estate drift across Google Sheets trackers, Google Drive folders, and Slack channels.[^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a] It serves as the primary entry point for general drift remediation requests, routing workflow execution through an ordered eight-step pipeline while preventing premature or out-of-order execution by subordinate phase skills.[^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd][^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]

It interfaces with diagnostic tools like [aaif-audit-slack](aaif-audit-slack.md) and enforces operational invariants tested by the [community-events-eval-suite](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md).

# Architecture / Specification

## Front-Door Dispatching and Skill Routing
When operators report multi-system estate drift without naming a single specific engine, `aaif-sync` acts as the mandatory front door.[^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a][^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836] The estate synchronization domain is divided into:
1. **Orchestrator Skill (`aaif-sync`)**: Owns whole-estate intake, execution sequencing, and overall pipeline reporting.[^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]
2. **Phase Skills (`aaif-sync-chapters`, `aaif-sync-organizers`, `aaif-sync-slack`)**: Own individual subsystems.[^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]

Because these skills share semantic overlap across keywords like "sync", "chapter", and "organizer", automated evaluation guards prevent individual phase skills from firing in isolation when presented with general estate drift prompts.[^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5]

## Pipeline Invariants and Execution Ordering
`aaif-sync` enforces strict sequence dependencies to ensure safety across storage and communication services:[^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd]
- **Read and Report Precedence**: Reports and drift reconciliation proposals must be generated before mutating any target systems.[^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd]
- **Data Foundation Gate**: Chapter records and CRM rows must be fully verified and in place before downstream permissions or messages are handled.[^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd]
- **Write Prohibition**: The orchestrator must not grant Google Drive access or post announcements to Slack before underlying tracking records are synchronized.[^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd]

# Lifecycle History
Maintained in `aaif/community-events`. Behavioral invariants are tested via the `sync-front-door` suite, evaluating skill selection, phase exclusion, and sequence compliance.[^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd][^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5][^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation Suite
proposed_concept.description: Automated testing harness and evaluation framework enforcing skill firing accuracy, write-gate safety, pipeline ordering, and compliance across AAIF community operations skills.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated testing harness and behavioral evaluation framework designed to verify trigger accuracy, routing boundaries, write-gate safety, and compliance formatting across AAIF community operational agent skills.[^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836] It establishes deterministic regex, tool invocation, and model-graded criteria that prevent routing collisions, enforce sequence invariants, and guard legal compliance.[^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5][^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5]

The suite provides regression testing for operations skills including [aaif-sync](../skills/aaif-sync.md), [aaif-announcement-post](../skills/aaif-announcement-post.md), and [aaif-audit-slack](../skills/aaif-audit-slack.md).

# Architecture / Specification

## Evaluated Suites and Grading Criteria

### Sync Front Door (`evals/sync-front-door`)
Tests the orchestration boundaries of estate synchronization when presented with general drift across sheets, Drive folders, and Slack channels:[^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a]
- **`skill_fires`**: Tool-use assertion requiring the top-level `aaif-sync` skill to fire when general drift is reported.[^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]
- **`not_a_phase_skill`**: Regex trace assertion verifying that specialized sub-skills (`aaif-sync-chapters`, `aaif-sync-organizers`, `aaif-sync-slack`) do not fire directly for an unsplit whole-estate request.[^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5]
- **`order_is_respected`**: Model-graded check ensuring the pipeline runs in an explicit sequence where reports precede mutations, and chapter/CRM state is confirmed before modifying Drive permissions or Slack.[^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd]

### Announcement Copy Compliance (`evals/announcement-post`)
Verifies that public, attendee-facing social media communications satisfy legal policy transparency requirements:[^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5]
- **`legal_footer`**: Regex grader enforcing that generated attendee copy retains both mandatory AAIF legal links: the Code of Conduct and the Privacy Policy.[^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5] Posts containing only one link fail evaluation to eliminate footer drift.[^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5]

# Lifecycle History
Maintained under `aaif/community-events` within the `evals/` hierarchy. Serves as CI verification for operational skills governing chapter lifecycle management.[^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a][^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry and correlation contract defining identity hierarchies, execution relationships, and interpretation invariants across agent turns and external effects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and correlation specification developed by the Observability and Traceability Working Group to standardize how causal agent execution, turn-to-session continuity, and tool boundaries are captured across heterogeneous frameworks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]. It defines an explicit entity contract and interpretation rules that resolve ambiguities when correlating asynchronous agent planning with external operations.

# Architecture / Specification
The v0.1 draft contract structures agent behavior across eight core identity primitives and six formal relationships [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]:
- **Identities**: `conversation` (user-facing multi-turn interaction), `runtime session` (isolated execution lifespan), `turn` (single causal prompt-evaluation-action cycle), `model call` (invocation of an underlying foundation model), `proposed action` (agent-generated intent before execution), `approval decision` (authorization record for high-risk actions), `tool execution` (local or remote tool invocation), and `external effect` (observable mutation outside the agent boundary).
- **Interpretation Rules**: An unobserved execution step evaluates to unknown rather than zero or failure; duplicate spans are deduplicated via deterministic correlation keys; and out-of-order telemetry arrival must not alter causal attribution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].
- **Interoperability**: The contract provides bidirectional crosswalks to OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions and standard AAIF terminology [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].

# Lifecycle History
The specification contract was drafted in PR #51 of `aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability` to progress Issue #41, formalizing identity splits and turn-boundary rules under a two-week technical review period prior to recommendation baseline alignment [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].

# References

- OpenTelemetry Telemetry Framework: [../resources/opentelemetry.md](../resources/opentelemetry.md)

[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]: AAIF Observability & Traceability WG PR #51, 'docs: add Agent Behavior Trace Model shared contract draft (v0.1)', https://github.com/aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability/pull/51

proposed_concept.title: Three-State Reconciliation
proposed_concept.description: Evaluation model comparing an agent claim against independent observation resolved into agreement, contradiction, or no independent evidence.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Three-state reconciliation is an evaluation model that compares an agent claim against an independent boundary observation and resolves the outcome into one of three explicit states: agreement, contradiction, or no independent evidence [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54]. By designating the absence of independent evidence as an explicit third state rather than a silent failure or default pass, the model ensures that auditors can distinguish between verified consistency and unmonitored execution [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54].

# Architecture / Specification
In contrast to binary reconciliation systems that collapse unobserved claims into unverified defaults, three-state reconciliation mandates explicit tri-state resolution [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54]:
1. **Agreement**: The independent observation confirms the agent's asserted claim or execution outcome.
2. **Contradiction**: An independent observation exists and directly refutes or diverges from the agent claim.
3. **No Independent Evidence**: No corroborating telemetry, witness record, or boundary observation was captured for the claim [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54].

This tri-state taxonomy originated in discussions around control-plane telemetry within the Observability & Traceability Working Group, where separating unchecked assertions from checked assertions was identified as a critical requirement for dispute resolution and compliance auditing [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54].

# Lifecycle History
Proposed in Issue #54 of `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` as part of the deferred category definitions pass, pending paired-contrast and related-term alignment with witness scope and verification-basis attributes [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54].

# References
- Observability and Traceability WG: [../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- Attestation & Evidence WG: [../working-groups/attestation-and-evidence.md](../working-groups/attestation-and-evidence.md)
- Action Record Taxonomy: [action-record.md](action-record.md)

[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54]: AAIF Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream Issue #54, 'Define: three-state reconciliation', https://github.com/aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape/issues/54

proposed_concept.title: aaif-sync
proposed_concept.description: Front-door procedural pipeline orchestrator executing AAIF community estate reconciliation across a phase-by-stage matrix with enforced human triage gates.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-sync` is the unified front-door procedural pipeline orchestrator that reconciles the AAIF community estate, synchronizing member chapters, organizer privileges, Slack communication channels, and Google Drive access permissions [^evt-community-events-pr-49]. It enforces a strict phase-by-stage architecture that reports current state by default, exposes triage backlogs as non-deciding human gates, and writes mutations only when invoked with explicit write permissions [^evt-community-events-pr-49].

# Architecture / Specification
The pipeline coordinates execution across seven subject phases and three sequential stages per phase [^evt-community-events-pr-49]:
- **Two-Axis Execution Matrix**: Every subject phase executes through `gather`, `plan`, and `execute` stages in strict order. Audit scans serve as the gather step for dependent planning phases [^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **Human Triage Gating**: Unresolved organizer and chapter applications halt automated execution with exit code 2; the pipeline summarizes pending queue depth and never makes autonomous admission decisions [^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **Data-Driven Findings**: Engines emit structured finding records (containing category, subject, detail, severity, and remediation steps) via `--json-out` and compile an HTML dashboard summarizing the estate's health while appending collapsed execution logs [^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **State Isolation and Caching**: Local Slack caches expire after 24 hours and are prevented from repository check-in by automated gitignore guards, ensuring that the runner maintains no cross-run drift [^evt-community-events-pr-49].

# Lifecycle History
Refactored in PR #49 of `aaif/community-events` to establish a single code-driven pipeline entrypoint (`sync.py`), modularizing legacy monolithic synchronization routines into distinct procedural phase skills [^evt-community-events-pr-49].

- Slack Audit Skill: [aaif-audit-slack.md](aaif-audit-slack.md)
- Proposal-Execution Split Pattern: [../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)

proposed_concept.title: aaif-audit-slack
proposed_concept.description: Read-only inspection skill auditing community Slack workspace coverage, room classifications, and organizer identities driven by spreadsheet configuration.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-audit-slack` is a read-only community operations inspection skill that audits Slack workspace coverage, verifies channel mapping against local city chapters, and detects unauthorized accounts in organizer channels [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6] [^evt-community-events-pr-49]. Operating as a gather stage engine within the `aaif-sync` pipeline, it derives its configuration directly from spreadsheet tables maintained by community organizers rather than static repository files [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6] [^evt-community-events-pr-49].

# Architecture / Specification
The audit engine matches chapters to Slack channels using explicit spreadsheet schemas and deterministic priority rules [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]:
- **Chapters List Schema**: The primary sheet defines channel associations across three mapping columns: `Slack Channel` (public city room overrides), `Organizer Channel` (private organizer room overrides), and `Country Channel` (regional channels, flagged as regional-only and never counted toward local chapter coverage) [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- **Slack Config Priority Rules**: Prefix and suffix matching rules reside on a dedicated `Slack Config` tab, where row order is load-bearing: public prefixes (`(none)`, `meetup-`, `aaif-`) and organizer suffixes (`-organizers`, `-chapter-leads`) are evaluated top-to-bottom [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- **Human Confirmation Gate**: The skill operates under a strict 'propose and wait' rule; near-miss channel matches are output as recommendations and require explicit human approval before being added to chapter records [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- **Ops Notes Separation**: Freeform human notes in the `Ops Notes` column are quoted in generated health summaries but are never parsed or mutated by automation scripts [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6] [^evt-community-events-pr-49].

# Lifecycle History
In PR #49 and associated refactors, static configuration in `scripts/channel_map.json` was decommissioned in favor of direct spreadsheet configuration on the Community Chapters List, ensuring organizers can directly correct room associations [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6] [^evt-community-events-pr-49].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry and correlation contract defining identity hierarchies, execution relationships, and OpenTelemetry mappings across multi-turn agent interactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a vendor-neutral telemetry and correlation specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to track an agent's execution across turns, interruptions, and system boundaries using OpenTelemetry primitives [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. The contract standardizes which operational relationships to record, how to identify and correlate distributed work without querying private agent state, and how independent observability readers and backends should interpret resulting telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification establishes an execution plan structured around four core validation questions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]:
- **Continuity**: Determining which interaction turns belong together across pauses, durable waits, and process restarts.
- **Calls and Retries**: Correlating foundation model API calls and retries to their initiating turn without double-counting work.
- **Approvals**: Linking human or automated approval decisions to specific proposed actions and verifying whether execution ensued.
- **Effects**: Associating independently observed external system state modifications with specific tool or action executions.

### Baseline Scenario and Runtimes
The initial reference implementation exercises an end-to-end customer support scenario: investigating a delayed order, proposing ticket creation, requesting authorization, executing the ticket creation against an independently instrumented service, and resuming the interaction turn [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. Conformance is validated across [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and a second independent agent runtime or SDK, requiring two independent reader implementations to evaluate trace graphs containing delayed, duplicated, or missing events [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

### Boundary Invariants
The execution plan enforces four architectural constraints [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]:
1. **Vocabulary Isolation**: Disambiguates conversation continuity, runtime session protocols, and agent trajectories, maintaining crosswalks with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).
2. **Turn Trace Boundaries**: Evaluates one trace per interaction turn as a candidate standalone default while preserving caller context.
3. **Evidence Neutrality**: Treats missing observations as unknown rather than zero or success; distinguishes observed approval receipt from cryptographic attestation, keeping content payload capture strictly opt-in.
4. **Framework Extensibility**: Reuses standard [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) schemas and language-neutral fixtures without mandating bespoke storage engines.

# Lifecycle History
The model originated from the Observability & Traceability Working Group's trace model recommendation workstream (Issue #12, PR #19) and was formally expanded into a nine-task execution plan of record in September 2026 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

# References

- [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md)
- [Goose](../resources/goose.md)
- [Agent Observability Use Cases](../resources/agent-observability-use-cases.md)

# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group convenes practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies within the Agentic AI Foundation to advance interoperable telemetry, trace structures, and behavioral monitoring across AI agent runtimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]. Operating under a vendor-neutral mandate, the group identifies observability gaps across reasoning loops and tool integrations, producing guidance and specifications only where existing bodies such as OpenTelemetry have not addressed the requirement [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's active technical program centers on the following core assets [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]:
- **[Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)**: A nine-task implementation plan standardizing session continuity, approval correlation, and effect tracking using OpenTelemetry conventions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].
- **[Agent Observability Prior Work](../resources/agent-observability-prior-work.md)**: A landscape survey analyzing existing protocols, commercial APM suites, and open-source tracing libraries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].
- **[Agent Observability Use Cases](../resources/agent-observability-use-cases.md)**: A catalog of practitioner requirements spanning debugging, compliance, safety monitoring, and distributed transaction attribution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].

### Governance and Operations
- **Chairs**: Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco, Chair) and Matthew Lee (Datadog, Co-Chair), serving terms from March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].
- **Meeting Schedule**: Biweekly on Wednesdays at 10:00 AM Pacific Time via Linux Foundation LFX Zoom [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].
- **Communications**: Public mailing list (`wg-observability-traceability@lists.aaif.io`) and public Discord channels, with GitHub issues serving as the durable source of truth for work status [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].

# Lifecycle History
Chartered by the Technical Committee in early 2026, the working group published landscape surveys and use case inventories before formalizing its Agent Behavior Trace Model execution plan in September 2026 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation Suite
proposed_concept.description: Automated testing harness and evaluation framework enforcing skill firing accuracy, write-gate safety, and non-idempotent API retry prevention across community operations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated quality assurance and safety enforcement framework governing agent skills and operational scripts within the AAIF community events infrastructure [^evt-community-events-pr-51]. It validates skill triggering accuracy, verifies write-gate enforcement, and executes static and mutation-tested safety guards that prevent non-idempotent API calls from duplicating estate assets across Google Workspace services [^evt-community-events-pr-51].

# Architecture / Specification
The evaluation suite consists of library unit tests, skill workflow validations, and repository safety guards [^evt-community-events-pr-51]:
- **Non-Idempotent Retry Guard (`NO_RETRY`)**: Enforces single-attempt execution for mutating Google Workspace CLI (`gws`) verbs, including `drive.files.create`, `drive.files.copy`, `appendDimension`, `insertDimension`, and `addSheet` [^evt-community-events-pr-51]. This prevents duplicate folders, files, or sheet tabs created when server-side successes experience client-side network timeouts [^evt-community-events-pr-51].
- **Static Guard (`check_non_idempotent_retries.py`)**: An automated scanner detecting unguarded mutating write call sites across positional and argument-list invocation patterns in operational scripts [^evt-community-events-pr-51].
- **Portability Guard (`check_portable_skills.py`)**: An AST import inspection script that verifies standalone skill isolation and rejects unauthorized dynamic dependencies on internal shared libraries [^evt-community-events-pr-51].
- **Credential Scrubbing and Error Redaction**: Sanitizes subprocess environment variables (stripping `AAIF_SLACK_*_TOKEN` and OAuth refresh secrets) and restricts failure logs to HTTP verbs and stderr, preventing sensitive authorization payloads from appearing in tracebacks [^evt-community-events-pr-51].
- **Mutation Verification**: Validates that test suites detect dropped retry budgets, disabled error filters, and un-guarded call sites across subprocess mocks [^evt-community-events-pr-51].

# Lifecycle History
Originally focused on skill triggering accuracy and basic mock testing, the suite was updated in PR #51 to centralize `gws` subprocess wrappers, eliminate drifting script-local helpers, and institute mutation-verified guards against estate-corrupting retries [^evt-community-events-pr-51].

The workstream curates standardized SKOS-Lite terminology models, resolves overlapping definitions across technical working groups, and maintains the public agentic AI ecosystem map [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream operates through recurring terminology review synchronization sessions and monthly reporting to the Technical Committee [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049]:

# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and correlation specification developed by the Observability and Traceability Working Group ([`../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)) to define consistent execution hierarchies and relationship contracts across diverse agent frameworks and language model providers[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification establishes standard relationship contracts and execution tracing semantics across multi-agent runtimes, client harnesses, and foundation model provider APIs. In August 2026, the working group recorded an execution plan formalizing the standard across structured work items[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48]:
- **Shared Relationship Contract**: Formalized execution and relationship semantics across nested agent spans and invocations.
- **Reference Runtimes**: Concrete reference agent framework and SDK implementations demonstrating trace emission.
- **Provider API Examples**: Mappings validating trace correlation against foundation model provider APIs.
- **Conformance & Test Harness**: Reusable validation test suites checking contract compliance across agent runtimes.
- **Upstream Contributions**: Evidence-backed contributions standardizing agent semantic conventions into broader open telemetry ecosystems.

# Lifecycle History
The execution plan was recorded by the Observability and Traceability Working Group in PR #48, closing issue #39 and establishing execution tasks #40 through #47 as the plan of record[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Estate Sync Skill
proposed_concept.description: Procedural pipeline orchestrator executing full 18-step AAIF community estate reconciliation with ephemeral run memoization and execution sleep guards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-sync` skill is a procedural operations orchestrator that coordinates end-to-end estate reconciliation across AAIF chapters, organizers, Slack workspaces, Google Drive assets, and Luma events[^evt-community-events-pr-52][^evt-community-events-pr-53]. The default pipeline executes an 18-step sequence straight through without step narrowing to ensure complete state consistency across all community surfaces[^evt-community-events-pr-53].

# Architecture / Specification
The runner script coordinates multi-process synchronization while preventing redundant remote queries and execution interruptions:
- **Ephemeral Run Memos**: During report runs, the execution pipeline utilizes process-isolated run memos (`AAIF_SLACK_RUN_MEMO` and `AAIF_GWS_RUN_MEMO`) managed via `jsoncache.RunMemo`[^evt-community-events-pr-52]. These append-only files (created with mode 0600 permissions) cache repeated Slack account lookups and successful Google Sheets and Drive reads.
- **Write-Run Cache Bypass**: Runs with `--write` disable the Google Workspace read memo to ensure subsequent steps immediately observe preceding writes (such as `luma` reading updated chapters list data written by `chapters`)[^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **Cleanup Guarantee**: Memo files are strictly temporary and are deleted upon pipeline termination, including on crash or process interruption[^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **Parallel CRM Loading**: Chapter workbook reads in `sync_crm` execute through a six-worker thread pool, while planning decisions remain sequential and order-preserving[^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **System Sleep Prevention**: On macOS platforms, the runner invokes `caffeinate -i -w <runner pid>` via `keep_awake()` to prevent system sleep and session expiry during multi-step runs[^evt-community-events-pr-53].
