# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group is an AAIF technical body focused on defining standardized execution models, workflow primitive taxonomies, and reference architectures for agent orchestration[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea]. The working group is chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical deliverables across three active workstreams[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea]:
- **Reference Architectures Workstream**: Scopes and evaluates standardized reference implementations for agentic workflows (such as [`../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md`](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md)).
- **Critical Use Cases Workstream**: Catalogs and prioritizes production agent use cases across enterprise automation and multi-agent coordination.
- **Taxonomy Workstream**: Defines core workflow primitives and structural terms in coordination with the broader Taxonomy and Landscaping workstream ([`../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md`](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md))[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

# Governance & Operations
In its June 2026 report to the Technical Committee ([`../governance/technical-committee.md`](../governance/technical-committee.md)), the working group highlighted cross-group coordination risks regarding overlapping vocabulary definitions across different working groups, recommending that the global taxonomy workstream be empowered to enforce shared terms across AAIF efforts[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group bridging global AI policy developments and technical agentic systems by evaluating regulatory regimes against standardized engineering baselines.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group (WG Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment) is an AAIF technical working group tasked with analyzing international AI policies, identifying gaps in existing frameworks, and establishing actionable engineering alignments for agentic AI deployments [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]. Chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase), the group bridges jurisdictional statutory requirements with concrete technical architectures and governance standards [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].

# Architecture / Specification

To conduct structured comparative and gap analyses across regional AI and agentic AI legal instruments, the working group established a baseline of 16 core governance and regulatory themes [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]:

1. **Governance & accountability**: Organizational ownership, formal approval workflows, RACI allocations, and explicit risk acceptance boundaries.
2. **Use-case classification & risk tiering**: Clear demarcations of permitted versus prohibited use cases, alongside tiered technical controls aligned with risk profile.
3. **Architecture**: Reference implementation patterns, formal trust boundaries, and strategic control placement across agent components.
4. **Agent identity & delegation**: Authentication and authorization models, on-behalf-of delegation chains, and decentralized or centralized agent registries [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].
5. **Guardrails & policy constraints**: Deterministic business rules, policy-as-code enforcement, and model-level constraints.
6. **Data protection & privacy**: Personally identifiable information (PII) handling, strict data minimization, retention limitations, and data residency controls.
7. **Security & access controls**: Principle of least privilege, secrets isolation, runtime segmentation, and granular tool permissions.
8. **Model/agent risk management**: Pre-deployment validation, behavioral robustness, distribution drift monitoring, and formal change control.
9. **Human oversight**: Human-in-the-loop (HITL) and human-on-the-loop (HOTL) workflows, operational escalation protocols, automated oversight mechanisms, and out-of-band kill switches [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].
10. **Action management**: Pre-execution validation gates, dual-control approval patterns, and action reversibility guarantees.
11. **Monitoring & logging**: Tamper-evident audit trails, prompt/tool invocation logs, and decision rationale recording.
12. **Testing & red teaming**: Systematic resilience testing against prompt injection, tool capability abuse, and unbounded autonomy failures.
13. **Third-party & supply chain**: Vendor due diligence, foundation model provenance, and tool supply-chain verification [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].
14. **Incident response**: Autonomous anomaly detection, containment workflows, and external incident reporting procedures.
15. **Transparency & user disclosure**: End-user notifications regarding artificial nature, decision explanations, and reasonable user expectation framing.
16. **Recordkeeping & auditability**: Verifiable retention schedules and deterministic replay/reproducibility capabilities.

To ensure uniform extraction across diverse regional policy instruments, the group developed a standardized "golden source" prompt methodology to extract authoritative baseline statements across jurisdictions [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].

# Lifecycle History

In August 2026, the working group finalized the 16-theme baseline and standardized extraction prompts, transitioning into phase two comparative gap analysis across target jurisdictions [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]. Work planned for autumn 2026 includes delivering an interim comparative report and synthesis recommendations to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Inventory
proposed_concept.description: Production workflow catalog categorizing real-world agent deployments, activity sequences, and coordination topologies across industry and SDLC domains.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Use Case Inventory is a curated catalog maintained by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) documenting empirical agent deployments, activity sequences, and boundary controls across production domains [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]. It classifies workflows along standardized structural dimensions including trigger mechanics, human oversight patterns, agent population, coordination topology, workflow execution pattern, and duration bounds [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].

# Architecture / Specification

Use cases are categorized across primary operational domains, including software development lifecycle (SDLC), commerce, infrastructure operations, and data analytics. Workflows are classified against standard AAIF architectural dimensions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]:

- **Trigger**: Activation source (e.g., event-driven webhook, interactive user invocation, scheduled cron).
- **HITL Pattern**: Human oversight mechanism (e.g., [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md), none, or external out-of-band review).
- **Agent Count**: Structural cardinality (e.g., single-agent sufficient, multi-agent swarm).
- **Coordination**: Orchestration topology (e.g., single-agent orchestrated, dynamic delegation).
- **Workflow Pattern**: Execution sequence model (e.g., sequential pipeline, parallel fan-out and join).
- **Duration**: Expected execution envelope (e.g., short interactive bounds versus long-running durable sessions).

## SDLC Domain Implementations

### Upstream SDK Release Impact Analysis

An automated maintenance workflow evaluating upstream dependency updates, derived from production CI infrastructure in the Model Context Protocol Inspector [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]:

- **Trigger**: Scheduled (nightly cron execution).
- **HITL Pattern**: None within the workflow envelope; output generates an informational report while adoption decisions remain an out-of-band human process [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].
- **Agent Count**: Single-agent sufficient.
- **Coordination**: Single-agent, orchestrated by deterministic pipeline scripts.
- **Workflow Pattern**: Sequential pipeline (sweep upstream repository, fetch release notes, execute agent analysis, scan artifacts, publish findings) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].
- **Duration**: Short (bounded by container timeout, typically under 20 minutes).
- **Security Boundary**: Implements the [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) via job-level permissions rather than a dynamic runtime gate. The agent runs in an isolated read-only job with restricted tool grants (`Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`) and no shell or network access, preventing tool-poisoning risks from untrusted upstream release notes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]. Output is credential-scanned before handoff to an isolated write-scoped job as a build artifact [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].

# Lifecycle History

In August 2026, the inventory was expanded via draft proposals to capture production agent patterns enforcing boundary isolation through static platform permission grants rather than dynamic human approval gates [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body developing security design patterns, threat modeling frameworks, baseline implementation guides, and cross-functional security review checklists for autonomous agent architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]. The group coordinates cross-cutting security invariants and defensive guardrails across foundation initiatives [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

# Active Deliverables
The working group manages several primary artifacts [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]:
- **[Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)**: Baseline guidance addressing threat vectors, secrets handling, sandboxing, and execution constraints, moving to initial release with standing issue-driven review windows [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Structured comparative analysis and threat modeling methodology evaluated in tandem with implementation guidelines [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **[Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md)**: A security evaluation checklist designed for cross-discipline coordination across foundation groups, including [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md), Identity and Trust, and Agentic Commerce [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Reusable architectural security patterns, including attested and isolated runtime specifications [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

# External Collaboration and Tooling
The group coordinates with external standardization bodies and adopts specialized repository tooling [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]:
- **ETSI TC SAI Liaison**: Exploring bidirectional information exchange with ETSI Technical Committee Securing Artificial Intelligence regarding AI agent cybersecurity requirements [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Taxonomy Browser Tooling**: Deploying automated contribution tooling that tracks LLM provenance and human edit distance for proposed terminology definitions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Governance Norms**: Implementing standing PR review windows in repository contributing guides and quiet-period objection rules to streamline review throughput [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Observability Use Cases
proposed_concept.description: Living catalog categorizing agent observability requirements across debugging, cost, attribution, evaluation, safety, multi-agent coordination, and identity.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Observability Use Cases catalog documents real-world operational and governance requirements for runtime visibility into autonomous AI agent behavior, curated by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]. It articulates practitioner requirements spanning root-cause debugging, cost management, code attribution, evaluation, multi-agent boundaries, and compliance verification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].

# Cross-Cutting Telemetry Requirements
The catalog establishes core telemetry expectations across all agent operational scenarios [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]:
- **Source and Trust**: Telemetry must identify producer vantage points (distinguishing agent self-reporting from framework, gateway, identity-provider, sandbox, operating system, or sensor records) and indicate tamper-evidence or signing mechanisms [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **Privacy and Governance**: Content and identity fields must include metadata supporting redaction, minimization, residency, and retention policies, strictly prohibiting capture of raw credentials [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **Completeness and Sampling**: Traces must record sampling decisions, dropped-event counters, and gaps, segregating audit-grade requirements from sampleable telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **Schema Evolution**: Telemetry must carry schema, semantic convention, model, tool, and harness versions to ensure long-term historical interpretability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **Correlation and Causality**: Systems must provide stable causal linkages across sessions, tasks, messages, delegations, and tools without relying solely on wall-clock time or basic span trees [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].

# Use Case Categories
The inventory organizes observability requirements across nine domains [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]:
- **A. Debugging and Root Cause Analysis**: Diagnosing unexpected decisions (A1), execution bottlenecks (A2), and behavioral reproducibility (A3) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **B. Cost Management and Optimization**: Reconstructing session costs (B1), outcome efficiency (B2), and token waste (B3) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **C. Code Attribution and Provenance**: Tracking AI-authored code (C1) and conducting security reviews on generated source (C2) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **D. Evaluation and Quality Assurance**: Evaluating task-level benchmark performance (D1), regression tracking (D2), and configuration comparisons (D3) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **E. Safety and Compliance**: Tracking external actions (E1), scope boundary violations (E2), regulated audit trails (E3), and tamper-evident evidence for disputes (E4) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53].
- **F. Multi-Agent Systems**: Tracing across boundary handoffs (F1) and understanding agent-to-agent protocol dialogues (F2) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **G. Operational Monitoring**: Monitoring agent fleet health (G1) and infrastructure capacity (G2) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **H. Research and Improvement**: Identifying emergent failure modes (H1), collecting fine-tuning corpora (H2), and cross-implementation benchmarking (H3) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **I. Identity and Ownership**: Resolving cross-surface identity (I1) across human principals, agent personas, and delegating credentials [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry and correlation contract defining identity hierarchies, execution relationships, and independent verification test suites.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a vendor-neutral telemetry and correlation specification curated by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to define standard identity hierarchies, task causality, and structural execution records across diverse agent harnesses [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]. It provides a formal model guaranteeing that agent execution graphs remain interpretable even when telemetry streams experience lost, duplicated, or reordered records [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification is developed along a nine-task execution plan focused on contract conformance, sample fixtures, and multi-runtime interoperability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

## Shared Test Kit and Contribution Templates
Task 4 establishes a reusable test harness and contribution template for evaluating relationship models in exported telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]:
- **Fault Invariant Verification**: Validates deterministic resolution when records are out of order or duplicated (e.g. repeated task creation receipts maintain single-record idempotency, whereas missing downstream receipts correctly report execution as unconfirmed rather than unattempted) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42].
- **OpenTelemetry Conformance Integration**: Adapts existing OpenTelemetry conformance tooling with specialized relationship assertions, synthetic data fixtures, and opt-in payload capture guidelines [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42].
- **Test Isolation**: Separates deterministic unit verification from live integration testing to facilitate contribution without imposing whole-workflow harness dependencies [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42].

## Independent Interpretation Verification
Task 7 mandates rigorous multi-consumer evaluation to ensure specification neutrality [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]:
- **Dual Query Verification**: Requires two independently implemented consumers or query engines to process exported traces from distinct agents without sharing private runtime context, hidden fixtures, or internal reconstruction logic [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- **Consensus on Ambiguous Traces**: Proves that independent consumers produce identical state reconstructions when processing reordered, incomplete, or conflicting evidence (such as distinguishing approved proposals from unconfirmed external side effects) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing shared workflow execution models, reference architectures, boundary patterns, and activity-based composition taxonomies.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (WG Workflows & Process Integration) develops vendor-neutral architectural patterns, execution primitives, and reference architectures for agentic workflows [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. Chaired by Yaron Schneider and Adam Seligman, the group standardizes how agentic systems structure activities, enforce execution boundaries, and coordinate human and automated actors across enterprise environments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical outputs across three primary workstreams [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]:
- **Reference Architectures**: Standardizes formal architectural blueprints, including [Single-Agent Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md) ("human-approved operation") and [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. Architectures are validated using a four-outcome classification model: validated, partial, candidate, or no fit [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].
- **Taxonomy**: Curates core execution vocabulary, establishing "activity" as an atomic unit and defining workflows as compositions of activities to eliminate circular definitions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. Evaluation and gate terminology are scoped out to security, observability, and reliability groups [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].
- **Critical Use Cases**: Evaluates production agent workflows and aligns real-world operational sequences with standardized primitives and taxonomy [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

The working group enforces a standing contribution policy capping pull requests at approximately ten files to preserve reviewability [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group delivered its Phase One Core Terms draft, becoming the first AAIF working group to ship an approved asset [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. During the same period, architecture principles and the first reference architecture were merged, and pull request size limits were instituted to manage complex topologies [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, cross-boundary trace correlation, and verification pipelines.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group (WG Observability & Traceability) establishes vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, correlation models, and evaluation frameworks for AI agents [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra and Matthew Lee, the working group standardizes causal telemetry across agents, execution harnesses, Model Context Protocol servers, and local tools [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

# Architecture / Specification
The group's technical initiatives span several core areas [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]:
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: A vendor-neutral telemetry model preserving causal relationships and execution context across heterogeneous platforms, complemented by reference libraries and synthetic test cases [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Cross-Boundary Observability**: Metadata mappings and context propagation rules for agent-to-skill, skill-to-tool, agent-to-agent, and agent-to-MCP boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Agent Resource Discovery (ARD) Trust Pipeline**: Instrumentation and tracing of discovery, identity verification, and skill execution workflows using [Agent Gateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) and dedicated span attributes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Taxonomy Integration**: Developing standardized definitions for observability terms, including reasoning, agent trajectories, context propagation, memory access, context assembly, retrieval, and traceability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group consolidated the Orchestration & Coordination focus group into the primary working group body and established the implementation scope for the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. Additionally, seven core observability terms were accepted into the foundation-wide taxonomy [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry and correlation contract defining identity hierarchies, execution relationships, and portable context across agent runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a vendor-neutral telemetry contract developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to preserve execution context and causal relationships across agent runtimes, SDKs, gateways, and telemetry backends [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. It uses portable telemetry context to link agent planning and decisions to concrete execution outcomes without requiring raw chain-of-thought capture [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification addresses cross-surface causal tracking through several key components [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]:
- **Portable Telemetry Context**: Encapsulates causal linkages and execution states across multi-agent handoffs and asynchronous invocations, designed to support behavioral tracking alongside OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions rather than replacing them [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Identity & Context Correlation**: Standardizes canonical identifiers and context reuse across long-running tasks, ensuring privacy boundaries and verifiable evidence collection [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Reference Library and Conformance Tests**: Provides executable test fixtures and synthetic examples to validate telemetry correlation across independently instrumented components and identify potential upstream OpenTelemetry GenAI contributions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

# Lifecycle History
The initial scope and implementation plan for the Agent Behavior Trace Model were agreed upon in August 2026, establishing reference library development, synthetic examples, and integration testing with reference architectures from the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Survey Instrument
proposed_concept.description: Platform-neutral 16-question survey instrument gathering empirical practitioner data on real-world AI agent accuracy, reliability, and deployment challenges.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy and Reliability Survey Instrument is a platform-neutral evaluation questionnaire developed by the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) to gather structured practitioner data on production agent accuracy, failure modes, and architectural priorities [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9]. Composed of 16 standardized questions, the survey defines deterministic response behaviors, screening paths, and input constraints to ensure consistent cross-platform analysis [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].

# Architecture / Specification
The survey is organized into five sequential question sections [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9]:
- **Eligibility (Q1)**: Identifies qualifying respondents and defines three screen-out branches routed to a dedicated early-exit page [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].
- **About the System (Q2–Q5)**: Captures agent system characteristics, including inline write-in requirements ("Something else" text input) and optional architectural details in Q5 [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].
- **Benefits and Challenges (Q6–Q8)**: Evaluates organizational value and operational blockers using five-point response choices that include explicit "Not sure" options [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].
- **Accuracy and Reliability (Q9–Q13)**: Probes failure rates, evaluation methods, and reliability constraints with five-point response matrices [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].
- **Future Priorities (Q14–Q16)**: Gathers development roadmaps and future reliability requirements, with Q16 configured as an optional open-ended field [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].

All questions except Q5 and Q16 are mandatory to ensure statistical completeness across response cohorts [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].

# Lifecycle History
The survey instrument was contributed and merged into the working group repository in August 2026 under pull request #9 alongside an operational Google Forms review prototype [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing threat models, security design patterns, best practice guides, and cross-working group security review checklists for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group develops foundational threat modeling frameworks, security design patterns, operational security guidelines, and architectural review checklists across the Agentic AI Foundation estate [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. It coordinates cross-functional review processes with other working groups and aligns defensive engineering guidance with evolving industry standards [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group maintains five primary workstreams and cross-cutting efforts [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]:

- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Evaluates existing frameworks (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF) alongside threat modeling methodologies such as STRIDE and PASTA, incorporating considerations for human-user agent interactions and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Develops baseline guidance covering identity, authorization delegation, runtime sandboxing, and operational safeguards [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Documents architectural security patterns and templates for pattern submission [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Operates an overlap and engagement checklist with technical leads across other working groups to evaluate emergent specifications [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Delegation**: Evaluates agent-specific security and privacy terminology in conjunction with [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group established public-by-default meeting recording publishing, progressed skeleton drafts for best practices and threat modeling, and initiated requests to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) to clarify remit boundaries concerning the Agent2Agent (A2A) donation and protocol security ownership [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, cross-boundary trace models, and execution evidence architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group defines vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, distributed tracing boundaries, and operational evidence architectures across agent harnesses, model interfaces, and tool execution boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38]. The group stewards standard trace models, formalizes observability use cases, and coordinates across standards bodies and AAIF technical initiatives [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-18].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical domain around several key operational artifacts:

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: A neutral telemetry model evaluated via a structured recommendation plan balancing adoption, extension, or new specification pathways against candidate schemas [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38].
- **Liaison and Cross-WG Integration**: Maintained through an intake and coordination register connecting external initiatives (including OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, W3C Trace Context, AGNTCY, and Agent Trace) with internal AAIF bodies [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-18].
- **Use Cases and Evidence Tiers**: Telemetry requirements cataloging evidence grades, protocol boundaries, and jurisdiction-aware integrity assertions distinguishing technical timestamping from legal evidentiary weight [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].

# Lifecycle History
In mid-2026, the working group instituted a formalized liaison tracker [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-18] and established the trace model recommendation plan [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19]. Its August 2026 report confirmed delivery milestones for taxonomy contributions, cross-boundary proposals, and trace model implementation scoping [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate distinctions between use case identifiers and evidence-grade ladder tiers, along with cross-cutting jurisdiction and legal weight requirements.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Observability Use Cases
proposed_concept.description: Living catalog categorizing agent observability requirements across debugging, cost, attribution, evidence tiers, and jurisdiction-aware telemetry.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Observability Use Cases register is a foundational working group catalog defining practitioner requirements for tracing, debugging, compliance, cost tracking, and execution attestation in agentic systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56]. It provides functional requirements and operational criteria used to evaluate candidate trace formats and telemetry standards [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].

# Architecture / Specification
The use cases catalog details several operational clusters, including execution tracing, cost and attribution monitoring, and high-assurance evidence collection [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56]:

- **Evidence-Grade Ladder**: Defines hierarchical rungs of execution attestation explicitly disambiguated from functional use case numbering [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].
- **Jurisdiction and Legal Weight Requirements**: Mandates that telemetry records intended for compliance or statutory reliance explicitly state the record holder's legal role and applicable jurisdiction [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].
- **Timestamp Integrity versus Legal Effect**: Clarifies that cryptographic and protocol mechanisms such as RFC 3161 timestamps establish technical time-binding properties, whereas legal evidentiary weight is determined by relying party regimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].

# Lifecycle History
Originally drafted to inform the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md), the document was refined in September 2026 to resolve naming collisions between Section E use cases and evidence-grade ladder tiers, and to introduce jurisdiction qualification requirements across cross-cutting telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a vendor-neutral specification establishing common telemetry primitives, identity hierarchies, execution trees, and causal relationship models across multi-agent workflows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38]. It defines standard schema representations for agent sessions, delegations, and boundary transitions across models and execution environments [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification development follows a structured recommendation plan governed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19]:

- **Candidate Model Evaluation**: Evaluates external and member telemetry standards against documented agent observability use cases, taxonomy terms, and gap analysis results [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].
- **Decision Pathways**: Employs an adopt, extend, or new-artifact decision framework to ensure interoperability before introducing distinct schema constructs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].
- **Cross-Boundary Compatibility**: Coordinates with [Cross-Boundary Observability Model](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md) to correlate agent-to-tool and agent-to-agent protocol interactions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38].

# Lifecycle History
In mid-2026, the working group initiated the Trace Model Recommendation Plan under issue #12 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19]. Scope finalization and September implementation milestones were formalized in the August 2026 working group report [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Comparative gap analysis evaluating OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF across eight agentic architectural vectors.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis evaluates established security and risk management frameworks—specifically OWASP Top 10 for LLMs/Agentic systems, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF—against the failure modes and threat vectors unique to autonomous and multi-agent systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Architecture / Specification
The gap analysis assesses architectural vectors across several operational dimensions:

- **Framework Comparison**: Identifies coverage boundaries across MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF for agent-specific delegation and boundary crossing [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Methodological Alignment**: Evaluates traditional threat modeling methodologies, including STRIDE and PASTA, examining their applicability and limitations in non-deterministic agent workflows [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Protocol and Interface Vectors**: Incorporates analysis of user interface and human-user agent (UI/HUA) attack surfaces, as well as protocol boundaries introduced by the Model Context Protocol (MCP) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Lifecycle History
Authored by workstream leads in the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), initial drafts were placed in active review via PR #8, with expanded reviews on STRIDE/PASTA alignment and protocol considerations occurring in August 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22].

mutations.rationale: Creates the Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog established as a foundational architectural deliverable by the Security and Privacy Working Group.

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral catalog of reusable architectural design patterns addressing runtime governance, agent containment, secure tool invocation, and memory lifecycle security.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog is a vendor-neutral architectural reference published by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) defining reusable design patterns for recurring security and privacy challenges in agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3bbe1dee7e1d-99b84ed8]. It provides implementation-independent guidance applicable across platforms, agent frameworks, deployment models, and execution runtimes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3bbe1dee7e1d-99b84ed8].

# Architecture / Specification

The catalog serves as the architectural foundation for the accompanying [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md), organizing patterns into an intentional two-tier hierarchy where the patterns catalog defines reusable architectural mechanisms ("what") while the best practices guide provides operational and implementation instructions ("how")[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3bbe1dee7e1d-99b84ed8].

## Scope and Domain Coverage

The catalog covers eight architectural domains[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3bbe1dee7e1d-99b84ed8]:
- **Runtime security and governance**: Policy enforcement points, boundary verification, and runtime mediation.
- **Agent control and containment**: Sandboxing, capability degradation, and emergency execution limits.
- **Secure tool invocation**: Input sanitization, credential handling, and privilege isolation during tool calls.
- **Agent memory protection and lifecycle management**: Access controls, retention decay, and context isolation for persistent memory.
- **Privacy-preserving execution**: Data redaction, differential privacy, and minimization during inference.
- **Secure multi-agent collaboration**: Cross-agent message validation, delegation limits, and trust boundary management.
- **Security monitoring and intervention**: Out-of-band behavioral auditing, anomalous tool sequence detection, and active interception.
- **Auditability and recovery**: Cryptographic execution logging, state snapshots, and rollback mechanisms.

Identity issuance, authentication, trust federation, and credential management are treated as external inputs defined by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3bbe1dee7e1d-99b84ed8].

# Lifecycle History

- Draft 0.1 established by the Security & Privacy Working Group as a foundational design pattern workstream[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3bbe1dee7e1d-99b84ed8].

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless CI issue analysis agent built on Flue 2.0 that evaluates external GitHub submissions and pull requests with dual-model canary verification.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Submission Analyser is a headless continuous integration (CI) agent implementation built on the Flue 2.0 framework that automatically evaluates external GitHub issues and pull requests submitted to AAIF repositories. It provides structured feedback, reference comparisons, and triage analysis against foundational working group guidelines without requiring interactive human dispatch.

# Architecture / Specification

The analyzer executes in GitHub Actions workflows with strict permission scoping and automated model access verification[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].

## Model Access and Canary Testing

Because external foundation model inference endpoints represent a fragile dependency subject to shifting header requirements and entitlement expirations, the project operates an automated daily model canary workflow[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10]:
- **Dry-Run Execution**: The canary executes the real agent over a fixed known issue with `DRY_RUN=1`. The agent analyses and renders output but halts before creating Google Docs, commenting on issues, or posting to external notification channels[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].
- **Dual-Leg Matrix**: The canary runs independent matrix legs for both a primary model (`github-copilot/claude-opus-4.7`) and a fallback model (`github-copilot/gpt-5.4`) with `fail-fast: false`[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10]. Independent execution ensures that a failure in the primary provider does not mask a broken fallback path[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].
- **Least-Privilege Security**: Canary jobs run with read-only repository permissions (`contents: read`, `issues: read`) and `copilot-requests: write`[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10]. Model inference relies directly on workflow-scoped tokens carrying organization Copilot entitlements rather than personal access tokens (PATs), and publishing secrets are excluded to limit credential exposure[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].

# Lifecycle History

- Implemented automated daily model canary workflow to detect endpoint drift and entitlement revocation across primary and fallback inference providers[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, cross-boundary tracing frameworks, and automated governance reporting.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an AAIF technical body developing vendor-neutral specifications, data models, and instrumentation frameworks for tracking AI agent behavior, execution lifecycles, and tool interactions. It establishes reference architectures and interoperability profiles that bridge low-level system tracing (e.g., kernel and userspace profilers) and high-level agentic communication protocols.

# Architecture / Specification

The working group standardizes telemetry propagation across protocol boundaries, maintaining foundational models such as the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) and analyzing telemetry across Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent boundaries.

## Governance and Operations

In accordance with [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) operational guidance, the working group maintains an automated monthly activity reporting pipeline[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-59]:
- **Scheduled Metric Aggregation**: A GitHub Actions workflow runs on the first day of each month using the `issue-metrics` action to calculate monthly issue and pull request activity, open/closed counts, time to first response, and resolution times[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9373ed8bd5e2-54fdeb4c][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-59].
- **Automated Issue Tracking**: Aggregated metric reports are published automatically as repository issues tagged with the `monthly-report` label, ensuring consistent, auditable metrics for Technical Committee reviews without manual compilation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9373ed8bd5e2-54fdeb4c][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-59].

# Lifecycle History

- Adopted automated CI metrics pipeline to fulfill Technical Committee monthly reporting requirements following feedback on report #38[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-59].

proposed_concept.title: Approval Checkpoint
proposed_concept.description: Runtime governance pattern binding policy or human approvals to exact action payloads and maintaining strict separation across decision, execution, and effect records.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Approval Checkpoint pattern binds an approved action to its exact runtime payload and target for a defined validity interval, preventing execution drift, replay attacks, or unverified claims of task completion.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5] Contributed to the [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md) as candidate pattern SP-XXX, it addresses common failure modes in autonomous workflows where approvals are recorded as detached flags, permitting modified actions, reused authorizations, or unconfirmed downstream state changes.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26]

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern structures runtime approval around cryptographic parameter binding and explicit tri-record accounting.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]

## Action Binding and Verification
- **Approval Record**: Specifies the allowed action or tool, target resource, exact arguments or canonical digests, constraints, approver identity, validity interval, and allowable use count.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]
- **Digest Canonicalization**: Where arguments contain sensitive values or variable elements (such as timestamps), the approval record defines canonical serializations and explicitly marks which fields may vary.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]
- **Execution-Point Check**: The enforcement point recomputes bindings from the in-flight execution payload rather than relying on agent-supplied match claims or proposal representations.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]
- **Validity and Clocks**: Validity is evaluated against the enforcement point's local clock with an explicit skew tolerance.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]
- **Distinct Failure Modes**: An integrity check failure on the record, a parameter mismatch, and an unavailable approval check are reported as three distinct error states.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]

## Separation of Decision, Execution, and Effect
The pattern mandates maintaining three distinct historical records:
1. **Decision Record**: The approval issued by an authorized human or policy engine.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]
2. **Execution Record**: The dispatched attempt assigned an execution identifier by the enforcement point against which the approval's usage count is decremented.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]
3. **Effect Record**: The confirmation receipt returned by the target service, correlated by the service's own identifier.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]

Missing service receipts are recorded as unconfirmed effects rather than assumed non-execution, and divergent receipts under a single execution identifier are preserved as conflicts.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]

## Inter-Pattern Relationships
Approval Checkpoint interfaces directly with [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) during cooling-off queue releases and compensating rollback processing, where execution and service identifiers are required to target revocations.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]

# Lifecycle History
- Merged into `aaif/wg-security-and-privacy` via PR #26 as an initial candidate draft within the design patterns workstream.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26]

[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]: https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/22c3f9a2cdac4fcf092502fa06154b08b4df09b8/workstreams/design-patterns/DRAFT-approval_checkpoint_pattern.md
[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26]: https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/26

proposed_concept.title: Kill Switch
proposed_concept.description: Architectural control plane pattern providing out-of-band execution termination, network isolation, credential revocation, and compensating rollback for autonomous agent workloads.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Kill Switch pattern establishes an independent, out-of-band runtime control plane capable of immediately halting an agent's execution, severing its external network communications, and invalidating its active credentials.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01] Integrated into the [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md), it mitigates fundamental agent containment failures where prompt-level stop instructions are evaded or where background zombie tasks outlive orchestrator processes.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26]

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern structures agent containment into an automated loop: **detect → halt → rollback**, enforced completely outside the model's memory, prompt context, and execution loops.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]

## Core Containment Mechanics
1. **Execution Halting**: Forcibly terminates orchestrators and background child processes or async threads, preventing task orphanage.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]
2. **Network and Tool Denial**: Server-side proxies or runtime egress firewalls drop in-flight API requests and block tool endpoints.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]
3. **Credential Invalidation**: Out-of-band identity provider integration revokes short-lived session tokens, signing keys, and tool permissions.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]
4. **Circuit Breakers**: Threshold-based tripwires monitor tool error rates, loop depth, and resource consumption, triggering containment when anomalous behavior is detected.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]
5. **Reversibility and Rollback**: Reads structured execution logs to execute compensating transactions for side effects committed prior to termination.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]

## Unsettled Discussions and Residual Risks
Working group review has highlighted potential failure modes when enforcement points execute inside the agent's workload (e.g., sidecars or in-process SDKs). If credential revocation causes policy verification calls to return HTTP 401 or 403, misconfigured fail-open or availability fallbacks could inadvertently reopen tool dispatch, underscoring the requirement that policy rejections be strictly treated as refusal.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-27]

## Inter-Pattern Relationships
- **[Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)**: Coordinates cooling-off queue releases and provides the dual execution-service identifier mapping needed for compensating rollbacks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]
- **[Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)**: Supplies an immutable, hardware-enforced boundary for credential release and policy appraisal.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]

# Lifecycle History
- Initial draft merged into `aaif/wg-security-and-privacy` via PR #26.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26]
- Issue #27 opened to analyze enforcement point credential revocation and fail-open availability fallback risks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-27]

[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]: https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/22c3f9a2cdac4fcf092502fa06154b08b4df09b8/workstreams/design-patterns/DRAFT-approval_checkpoint_pattern.md
[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]: https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/22c3f9a2cdac4fcf092502fa06154b08b4df09b8/workstreams/design-patterns/DRAFT-kill_switch_pattern.md
[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26]: https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/26
[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-27]: https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/issues/27

proposed_concept.title: Attested Isolated Runtime
proposed_concept.description: Architectural security pattern isolating policy evaluation, credential release, and evidence signing inside hardware-attested trusted execution environments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Attested Isolated Runtime pattern isolates policy enforcement, credential release, and audit log signing inside a hardware-rooted Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) separate from untrusted host infrastructure.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb] Merged as the inaugural pattern under the privacy-preserving execution domain in the [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md), it provides cryptographic verification for relying parties when the infrastructure operator lies within the threat model.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26]

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern formalizes a four-party stakeholder model comprising the data owner, agent operator, infrastructure operator, and relying party, structured across four foundational operational pillars:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]

1. **Isolate Enforcement and Exclude Agent Workloads**: The policy evaluation engine, signing keys, and credential managers execute inside the hardware enclave, while large language model reasoning and agent orchestration remain outside to minimize the Trusted Computing Base (TCB).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]
2. **Internal Key Generation**: Cryptographic signing and identity keys are generated strictly inside the enclave boundary and sealed to platform measurements, preventing host extractability.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]
3. **Policy Sealing and Data Release on Appraisal**: Decryption keys and policy rules are only released to the enclave after external verification of hardware attestation evidence against expected identity measurements.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]
4. **Per-Unit Verifiable Evidence**: The enclave produces signed evidence records for each atomic evaluation or tool invocation, which independent relying parties verify without inspecting underlying private prompt data.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]

## Inter-Pattern Relationships
- **[Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md)**: Relies on the attested enclave to safeguard credential revocation logic and prevent untrusted hosts from tampering with isolation policies.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]
- **[Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)**: Utilizes enclave-signed evidence to establish tamper-proof audit trails for policy decisions.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]

# Lifecycle History
- Submitted to the design patterns workstream and merged via PR #26 as candidate architectural guidance for privacy-preserving execution.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26]

[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]: https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/22c3f9a2cdac4fcf092502fa06154b08b4df09b8/workstreams/design-patterns/DRAFT-approval_checkpoint_pattern.md

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral catalog of reusable architectural design patterns addressing runtime governance, agent containment, and confidential execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog is a structured collection of reusable architectural design patterns curated by the AAIF [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50] Maintained under workstream leads Dan Kommatas (Circle) and Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase), the catalog defines concrete implementation models and normative templates for secure, privacy-preserving agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50]

# Architecture / Specification
The catalog organizes design patterns across standardized security and privacy topic areas, mandating adherence to a common pattern template covering intent, problem context, architectural solution, consequences, trade-offs, and validation test cases.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50]

## Initial Catalog Composition
Initial pattern drafts merged into the catalog include:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26]
- **[Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)** (`DRAFT-approval_checkpoint_pattern.md`): Binds policy and human approval records directly to execution payloads while maintaining separation across decision, execution, and confirmed effect receipts.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50]
- **[Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)** (`DRAFT-attested-isolated-runtime.md`): Establishes confidential, hardware-attested execution enclaves for policy evaluation and evidence generation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50]
- **[Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md)** (`DRAFT-kill_switch_pattern.md`): Establishes an independent, out-of-band control plane for immediate process termination, network severing, credential invalidation, and rollback.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50]

## Governance and Contribution
- **Workstream Leads**: Dan Kommatas (Circle), Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50]
- **Contributing Organizations**: IBM, TELUS, Global Payments, Huawei, Bluerock, Ericsson, and independent community experts.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50]

# Lifecycle History
- Initial baseline of candidate patterns and folder index merged via PR #26 in `aaif/wg-security-and-privacy`.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26]

[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50]: https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/22c3f9a2cdac4fcf092502fa06154b08b4df09b8/workstreams/design-patterns/README.md

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Implementation guide establishing architectural controls, protocol hardening, and operational requirements across secrets management, tool invocation, guardrails, evaluations, and forensics.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide consolidates implementable security guidance for builders deploying agentic AI systems, structured across five core domains: secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] Governed as Deliverable 4 of the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guide provides production failure patterns, architectural controls, and decision frameworks for selecting appropriate safeguards.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]

The guide explicitly scopes out foundational agent identity and delegated authorization architectures—such as SPIFFE/SVID workload attestation, RFC 8693 delegation-chain encoding, and UCAN capability tokens—which are maintained by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and cross-referenced via the [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]

# Architecture / Specification

### 1. Secrets Management
Static, long-lived credentials, API keys, and environment-variable secrets represent durable attack surfaces vulnerable to prompt-injection extraction and state serialization leaks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] The guide mandates shifting to ephemeral attestations scoped to single operations:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]

- **Workload Identity:** Primary baseline for containerized deployments (e.g., AWS IRSA, GCP Workload Identity, Azure Managed Identity) exchanging cluster OIDC attestations for short-lived credentials without environment secrets.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]
- **Dynamic Secrets:** On-demand credential generation for databases and external APIs via secret engines (e.g., HashiCorp Vault) configured with narrow time-to-live (TTL) and automated revocation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]
- **Network-Layer Injection:** Sidecar and proxy injection for legacy targets to prevent agent runtimes from inspecting credentials.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]
- **Confidential Computing:** Hardware-protected memory enclaves (Intel SGX/TDX, AMD SEV-SNP) with attested key release for regulated, multi-tenant, or untrusted-host threat models.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]
- **CI/CD Hygiene:** Mandatory automated scanning for secrets embedded in environment variables or container image layers.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]

### 2. Secure Tool Invocation (Model Context Protocol)
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) presents inherent attack vectors including [tool poisoning](../taxonomy/tool-poisoning.md), [rug pulls](../taxonomy/rug-pull.md), cross-server shadowing, and conversation hijacking.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] The guide establishes dual-layer controls across connection and content:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]

- **Pre-deployment Verification:** Mandatory source repository validation (active within 90 days), cross-referencing public vulnerability databases, and executing static and runtime security scanners prior to deployment.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]
- **Transport Enforcement:** Mandatory OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, TLS enforcement, and RFC 8707 token audience binding for HTTP transport; treating local `stdio` transport as untrusted binaries requiring sandbox containment.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]
- **Mediation Gateways:** Routing multi-server agent traffic through centralized policy enforcement gateways (e.g., Cloudflare MCP Portals, AAIF `agentgateway`) to capture full request/response payloads and enforce granular permissions.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]
- **Runtime Invariants:** Tool description hash tracking across sessions to block rug-pull schema alterations, out-of-scope data category filtering, and allowlist enforcement.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]

### 3. Supply Chain and Skill Verification
Third-party skills, MCP server packages, and A2A Agent Cards require multi-tiered intake analysis:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]

- **Tier 1 Automated Pre-scanning:** Static pattern matching and behavioral dataflow analysis blocking Critical/High vulnerabilities.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]
- **Tier 2 Manual Review:** Scrutiny of elevated permission requests (`allowed-tools` validation, detection of dynamic evaluation constructs or Base64-obfuscated payloads).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]

### 4. Operational Domains
The specification additionally defines requirements across guardrail deployment, evaluation frameworks, sandboxed execution, and post-incident forensics.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06-23 to 2026-08-04:** Workstream initiated under co-leads Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson). First skeleton drafted and shared for initial working group review.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066]
- **2026-09-01:** Workstream completed review freeze; work initiated to derive static-analysis rules from the guide.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b]
- **2026-09-29:** Deliverable v0.1 completed final review and merged via PR #9. The working group adopted the guide as a living document governed through issues and pull requests, designating Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam as mandatory reviewers.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066]

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing open threat models, security design patterns, best practice guides, and taxonomy terms across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (WG) advances the mission of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) by establishing security and privacy as shared operational disciplines across the agentic ecosystem.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56] Operating under the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group produces open threat models, a shared taxonomy, and security design patterns that agent developers, enterprise consumers, and peer working groups adopt to distribute responsibility for trustworthy AI agents.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]

# Architecture / Specification

### Leadership and Terms
The Working Group Chairs were appointed by the Platinum and Gold members of the working group for the term March 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]
- **Chair:** Alex Frazer (Runlayer)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]
- **Co-Chair:** Junjie Bu (Google)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]

### Meetings and Operations
- **Primary Cadence:** Biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM US Pacific Time (6:00 PM UTC) via Zoom/LFX.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]
- **APAC Meeting Trial:** In September 2026, the working group instituted an alternate-week meeting trial tentatively at 10:00 PM US Eastern Time (8:00–9:00 AM JST) to accommodate contributors in the Asia-Pacific region, with Chair Alex Frazer bridging notes across both sessions.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]
- **Communications:** Public mailing list (`wg-security-privacy@lists.aaif.io`) and dedicated channels on the AAIF Discord server.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]

### Repository and Pull Request Governance
The group operates on GitHub (`aaif/wg-security-and-privacy`) with defined folder ownership rules:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]
- **`deliverables/`:** Contains formal published deliverables; PR authors are strictly prohibited from merging their own PRs into this directory, requiring independent maintainer review.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]
- **`workstreams/`:** Dedicated workstream folders where leads maintain operational autonomy and direct review over exploratory assets.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]
- **AI Contributions:** In response to influxes of uncoordinated automated pull requests, maintainers enforce human engagement norms and triage through pre-PR meeting discussions or AI-assisted review tooling.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]

### Deliverables Portfolio
1. **Taxonomy and Landscape:** Security and privacy domain definitions aligned with the cross-WG SKOS-Lite taxonomy workstream.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b]
2. **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis:** Comparative threat analysis and framework design led by Fernando Lucktemberg.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b]
3. **Design Patterns Catalog:** Implementation patterns for runtime governance, kill switches, and isolation led by Sagar Dashora and Dan Kommatas.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b]
4. **[Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md):** Living operational guide and feature matrix led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b]
5. **[Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md):** Lightweight assessment rubric evaluating security baselines across peer AAIF working groups.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-02-17 to 2026-03-03:** Orientation and initial charter ideation; Alex Frazer confirmed as elected chair.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b]
- **2026-04-14:** Scope, five deliverables, and working group charter approved unanimously by vote.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b]
- **2026-05-26:** Charter officially ratified; Junjie Bu confirmed as co-chair and Taxonomy/Landscape lead.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b]
- **2026-06-23:** GitHub repository made public, establishing workstream folders and monthly Technical Committee updates.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b]
- **2026-09-29:** Version 1.0 of the Security Best Practices Guide merged into `deliverables/`; APAC meeting trial agreed upon; deliverables non-author merge policy formally adopted.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry and correlation specification standardizing identity hierarchies, causal execution graphs, and evidence collection across agent harnesses.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model defines a vendor-neutral telemetry contract standardizing how agent harnesses emit, correlate, and propagate execution state, causal relations, and identity hierarchies across system boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60] Developed by the Observability and Traceability Working Group ([`../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)), the specification establishes semantic conventions for telemetry capture across heterogeneous agent frameworks.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]

# Architecture / Specification
The specification defines correlation across three core charter dimensions: identity and delegation hierarchies, causal execution relations, and boundary transitions across models, tools, and inter-agent protocols.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]

Following empirical findings that OpenTelemetry support varies substantially among coding agents and agent SDKs despite claiming GenAI semantic conventions, the specification adopts an evidence-first roadmap organized into four consecutive phases:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]
- **Agree**: Establish initial scope boundaries and dimension coverage definitions for Milestone 1.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]
- **Evidence**: Collect baseline trace emissions from production reference implementations, beginning with AAIF's [Goose](`../resources/goose.md`) runtime before expanding to secondary agent harnesses.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]
- **Interpret**: Curate a shared gap register contrasting observed telemetry outputs against semantic model requirements.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]
- **Contribute**: Submit validated attribute proposals to upstream OpenTelemetry specifications and finalize normative profile releases.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]

# Lifecycle History
Drafted within the Observability and Traceability Working Group. PR #60 restructured the initial nine parallel tasks into a phased, evidence-first execution model anchored on Goose trace baselining and a central gap register.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]
