proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (WG Security & Privacy) develops threat models, security architectures, implementation guidance, and design patterns to secure autonomous AI agents across execution environments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1] The working group operates under the Technical Committee and collaborates with partner groups like the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) to define operational security boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

Chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), the group coordinates workstreams across security best practices, threat modeling, architectural design patterns, and cross-working group security reviews.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group manages four primary workstreams:
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Living implementation guidance defining protocol hardening, sandboxing, and execution controls, supported by a Security Best Practices Feature Matrix mapping practices to people, process, and technology controls.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: A comparative assessment benchmarking existing frameworks (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, NIST AI RMF) across eight agentic threat areas to identify unique agentic risk domains.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Reusable architectural blueprints for agent safety, including [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md), [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md), and [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **Cross-WG Security Review Checklist**: Cross-cutting review criteria evaluating security and privacy considerations across all AAIF working groups.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25]

# Lifecycle History
In September 2026, the working group merged its first official Draft deliverables into `deliverables/`, including the Best Practices Guide and the Threat Modeling Gap Analysis v0.1.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1] The group instituted merge governance rules preventing authors from merging their own changes into `deliverables/`, initiated trial alternate-week APAC meetings, and submitted a request to the Technical Committee to establish formal bidirectional information exchange with ETSI TC SAI.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide is a living implementation standard developed by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to define hardening controls, architectural boundaries, and operational mitigations for autonomous agent systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1] Maintained by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, it serves as the working group's foundational implementation deliverable.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

Identity and trust topics are explicitly scoped out of the initial deliverable and deferred to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) to maintain clear jurisdictional boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25]

# Architecture / Specification
The guide defines operational requirements and architectural controls across agent development and runtime environments:
- **Feature Matrix Mapping**: Supported by the Security Best Practices Feature Matrix, which maps each practice to people, process, and technology controls.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **Static Analysis Rules**: Best practices are actively formulated into machine-readable rules for automated static analysis tooling.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **SDK Benchmarking**: Guidance is systematically compared against major agent frameworks, starting with the Google Agent Development Kit (ADK).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **Boundary Controls**: Mandates runtime sandboxing, principle of least privilege, strict tool execution isolation, and out-of-band monitoring.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

# Lifecycle History
The guide merged to `main` on 2026-09-30 via PR #9 and is registered as a Draft deliverable at `deliverables/DRAFT-agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md`.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1] Substantial open feedback items—such as hybrid and multi-cloud workload identity—were split into dedicated tracking issues to facilitate iterative updates.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

# Overview
The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis is a technical deliverable produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) evaluating existing cybersecurity and AI safety frameworks against the specific risks posed by agentic AI.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1] Authored by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, it establishes the empirical justification for targeted threat modeling initiatives across the foundation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

# Architecture / Specification
The document evaluates four prominent frameworks—OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF)—across eight agentic threat categories:
- **Classification Baseline**: Recommends establishing existing industry frameworks as the WG's classification foundation rather than authoring redundant baselines.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **Targeted Gap Coverage**: Directs new analytical work toward gaps unique to agentic architectures, including goal manipulation, memory corruption, unconstrained recursive delegation, and runtime tool abuse.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **Session Operationalization**: Serves as the primary reference document for dedicated threat modeling sessions launched in October 2026, interleaved with the best practices track.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

# Lifecycle History
The gap analysis was finalized and merged on 2026-09-30 via PR #8 as Draft v0.1 at `deliverables/DRAFT-agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md`.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog is an architectural catalog maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) providing repeatable, verifiable design patterns for securing agentic systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1] Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, the workstream standardizes architectural controls across agent harnesses, tool runtimes, and external communication boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

# Architecture / Specification
The catalog requires each design pattern to follow a standardized specification template defining context, forces, structural invariants, and runtime trade-offs.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1] The foundational pattern set includes:
- [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md): Binds external authorization to action payloads prior to runtime side effects.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md): Provides out-of-band execution termination, token revocation, and state quarantine mechanisms.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md): Enforces isolated policy evaluation, cryptographic evidence generation, and credential release boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

Subsequent patterns in the workstream pipeline address memory boundaries, context poisoning prevention, and multi-agent interaction isolation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

# Lifecycle History
The catalog landing page, pattern template, and the first four pattern drafts merged via PR #26 on 2026-09-30 under `workstreams/design-patterns/`.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1] External PR #11 was superseded by and incorporated into PR #26, and follow-up PR #28 initiated subsequent revisions to the Approval Checkpoint pattern.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Implementation guide establishing architectural controls, protocol hardening, pre-execution hook authorization, and threat mitigation baselines across agentic workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide establishes architectural controls, runtime enforcement boundaries, and threat mitigation standards for deploying autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents. Developed within the Security and Privacy Working Group (see [Security and Privacy WG](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)), the guide specifies defense-in-depth measures against prompt injection, credential exfiltration, untrusted tool execution, and unconstrained action execution.

A central focus of the guide is the authorization framework governing tool invocation and external environmental interactions. Recent working group proposals advocate positioning authorization controls behind deterministic pre-execution hooks rather than treating human-in-the-loop review as the sole control tier [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].

# Architecture / Specification

## Pre-Execution Hook and Authorization Tiers
Under active discussion in the working group, runtime governance relies on intercepting every proposed tool execution prior to dispatch [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31]:
1. **Pre-Execution Interception**: Every tool call is routed through an out-of-band evaluation hook before running, returning decisions such as `allow`, `deny`, `modify`, or `ask` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].
2. **Context- and Argument-Aware Classification**: Tier assignments and authorization decisions cannot rely solely on static operation names (such as generic database queries); they must evaluate the full payload, including arguments, target endpoints, and session context [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].
3. **Layered Policy Evaluation**: Deterministic rule engines evaluate payloads first; secondary model-based judges handle ambiguous edge cases, and human reviewers are queried only when the hook issues an `ask` directive [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31]. This mitigates approval fatigue observed in human-only authorization gates [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].
4. **Architectural Separation**: The classifier and hook engine execute outside the agent's context window and cannot be bypassed or modified by model self-reporting [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].

## Architectural Controls
- **Boundary Controls**: Strict ingress and egress network allowlisting enforced at the platform boundary rather than within the agent environment.
- **Payload Verification**: Tight binding between approved intent and exact execution payloads, aligned with the [approval-checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) pattern.
- **Separation of Duties**: Structural decoupling between planning and execution as defined in the [proposal-execution-split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md).

# Lifecycle History
- **Draft Development**: The guide is maintained under active iteration within the Security and Privacy Working Group.
- **Hook-Based Governance Proposal**: In October 2024, working group members raised issue #31 to transition the four-tier human approval model into an automated pre-execution hook architecture backed by empirical data on human approval fatigue [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].

# References
- [Approval Checkpoint Pattern](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)
- [Proposal Execution Split Pattern](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)
- [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry and correlation specification standardizing OpenTelemetry semantic conventions, receipt verification, and evidence-grade audit trails for AI agent executions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and correlation specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md). It standardizes OpenTelemetry-compatible semantic conventions, span structures, and verifiable action receipts for autonomous agent executions, bridging high-level cognitive decision steps with underlying infrastructure calls.

The model ensures that agent actions, tool calls, and state transitions produce structured audit traces capable of post-execution verification, multi-tenant isolation, and evidence-grade correlation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].

# Architecture / Specification

## Trace Semantics and Evidence Receipts
The specification establishes standard semantic conventions for agent traces:
- **Execution Spans**: Structured representations of agent planning steps, model invocations, tool requests, and environment responses.
- **Action Records**: Verifiable execution tokens binding action identifiers, target parameters, and execution results, complementing the [action-record](../taxonomy/action-record.md) taxonomy.
- **Signature and Receipt Decoupling**: Cryptographic signature validation is explicitly separated from real-world target effect correlation; synthetic signatures validate format mechanics without asserting live tenant effects [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].

## Conformance Test Kit
The working group maintains an automated test kit validating reader implementations and telemetry pipeline compliance [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57]:
- **OTLP/JSON Test Vectors**: Six standardized fixtures exercising edge conditions across duplicate receipts, missing receipts, valid signature verification, and invalid signature rejection [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].
- **Tenant and Ticket Boundary Checks**: Explicit test cases covering altered ticket identifiers and cross-tenant reuse of action identifiers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].
- **Reader Query Context**: Conformance readers load basis query context prior to evaluating expected telemetry outputs, ensuring deterministic trace analysis [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].

# Lifecycle History
- **Specification Draft**: Initiated under the Observability and Traceability Working Group.
- **Conformance Test Suite**: In October 2024, PR #57 introduced the #42 test kit with six OTLP/JSON test cases, expected answer vectors, and CI verification gates for signature and effect correlation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].

- [Evidence Record Specification](evidence-record-spec.md)
- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, delegation frameworks, and authority verification models for AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body established to develop vendor-neutral identity standards, cryptographic trust architectures, and delegation frameworks for autonomous systems. The group's scope covers machine-verifiable agent identity, credential exchange, authority propagation, and consent verification across multi-agent and human-agent environments.

Recent work includes benchmarking authority-at-dispatch protocols, enforcing versioned contract identifiers on execution traces, and establishing freshness limits on delegated credentials [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Technical Focus Areas
1. **Agent Identity and Credentials**: Formats and lifecycle specifications for agent decentralized identifiers (DIDs), public key infrastructure, and verifiable credentials.
2. **Authority-at-Dispatch**: Mechanisms validating whether an agent possesses active, unrevoked authority at the exact moment of action dispatch [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17]:
   - **Versioned Contract Identifiers**: Execution traces require explicit, versioned contract identifiers to validate that dispatched tasks conform to agreed capability boundaries [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].
   - **Evidence Freshness Limits**: Authority assertions incorporate age tracking and deployed freshness thresholds to prevent replay of stale delegation tokens [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].
   - **Trace Observer Workflows**: Automated reader pipelines ingest reference cases from external runs (such as MintID, Proofable, and Alakris) to verify authority compliance [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].
3. **Delegation and Trust Chains**: Protocols enabling human principals and upstream orchestrators to delegate bounded authorities to subordinate agents.

# Lifecycle History
- **Charter Formation**: Formed as a core technical working group within the AAIF.
- **Authority-at-Dispatch Cataloging**: In October 2024, PR #17 proposed integrating an authority-at-dispatch comparison catalogue entry and trace verification workflow enforcing versioned contract IDs and freshness limits [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].

- [Evidence Record Specification](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md)
- [Taxonomy: Identity](../taxonomy/identity.md)

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation Suite
proposed_concept.description: Automated testing harness and evaluation framework enforcing skill firing accuracy, write-gate safety, and credential isolation across event operations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated evaluation harness designed to test AI agent skills against regression failures that static linting and deterministic unit tests cannot detect[^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]. While deterministic tools such as `pytest` and schema linter scripts prove syntax, tooling banners, and YAML validity, they cannot verify whether an LLM reading a skill definition triggers the correct skill or reliably complies with behavioral directives[^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].

The evaluation harness targets subtle behavioral shifts, such as prompt vocabulary drift causing neighboring skills to misfire, improper handling of untrusted inputs, inadvertent disclosure of personal data, or token ingestion in conversational context[^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].

# Architecture / Specification

### Dual-Arm Differential Evaluation

The framework executes test cases across two concurrent arms to isolate skill contribution from foundation model defaults[^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]:
1. **With Plugin / Skill**: The agent executes the scenario with candidate skill documentation (`SKILL.md`) in context.
2. **Without Plugin / Skill**: The agent executes the identical prompt in baseline configuration.

Graders that pass under both conditions evaluate base foundation model abilities rather than skill effectiveness; criteria evaluated only when a skill is present are classified as `arm: with-only` to quantify the document's direct performance delta (`Δ`)[^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].

### Evaluated Failure Modes and Cases

- **Skill Triggering Disambiguation**: Tests such as `announcement-post` versus `recap-post` verify that similar attendee-facing skills fire accurately based on contextual phase (e.g., RSVP opening versus post-event recap)[^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
- **Vocabulary-Agnostic Activation**: The `check-setup` test evaluates non-technical prompts (e.g., asking "is it all working?") to ensure operational tools activate without relying on verbatim trigger phrases[^evt-community-events-file-5a72ef6a708b-c7737da1][^evt-community-events-file-cd95e0a9e63d-5578e7ad].
- **Privacy and Credential Boundary Defense**: Ensures that agents explicitly reject sensitive credentials offered in chat (such as Slack tokens) and redirect users to secure credential stores (e.g., Keychain Access)[^evt-community-events-file-a6116ffcd592-e614afed], while preventing accidental leakage of speaker contact information (phone numbers, private addresses) into published outputs[^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
- **Adversarial and Untrusted Form Input**: Enforces defenses against prompt injection via intake form cells (e.g., users requesting automated approval)[^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
- **Write Gate Enforcement**: Verifies that skills follow the [proposal-execution-split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md), reporting and proposing changes by default and executing updates only upon explicit confirmation[^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].

### Execution and CI Policy

Evaluations are invoked via the CLI harness (e.g., `claude plugin eval . --no-publish --trust-plugin`)[^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]. The suite runs locally and outside of pull request CI jobs (`validate.yml`) because public fork builds operate without API credentials to protect against token exfiltration[^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].

# References

- [aaif-check-setup](../skills/aaif-check-setup.md)
- [aaif-clean-data](../skills/aaif-clean-data.md)
- [proposal-execution-split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Clean Data Skill
proposed_concept.description: Operational data normalization and intake hygiene skill enforcing proposal-execution splits, multi-tier city resolution, and strict API-driven document surgery.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-clean-data` skill is an operational data normalization and quality assurance agent skill targeting the AAIF Community Intake Operations spreadsheet[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7]. It parses and normalizes untrusted form submissions without silent alterations, canonicalizing LinkedIn profile URLs, fixing casing and whitespace in names and cities, extracting geographic locations from free-text answers, identifying duplicates, and applying conditional formatting flags for manual review[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].

# Architecture / Specification

### Tooling and Rendering Constraints

- **API-First Operation**: All reads, writes, and modifications across Google Drive assets must execute via the `gws` CLI tool driven by Python, interacting directly with native Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides APIs[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].
- **OOXML Surgery Restrictions**: Byte-level zip surgery on `.docx`, `.pptx`, and `.xlsx` files is restricted to true Office storage formats to preserve embedded fonts and unedited structures[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].
- **Prohibition of Desktop Converters**: Tools such as LibreOffice, `soffice`, `unoconv`, or standard desktop office suites are strictly prohibited for file editing, format conversion, or visual preview rendering[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7]. These tools substitute system fonts for brand typography and drop unrecognized OOXML tags, producing inaccurate representations[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7]. Visual previews must be generated via native API rendering pipelines[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].

### Governance and Security Controls

- **Proposal-Execution Split**: The skill defaults to read-only operation via `python3 <skill-root>/scripts/clean.py scan`, outputting proposed mutations and flags[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7]. Changes can only be committed via `apply`, `cities --write`, `install-flags`, or `install-colors` following explicit operator authorization[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].
- **Input Sanitization**: Sheet cell values and form submissions are treated as untrusted data; prompt-like text inside form responses cannot alter status fields, chapters, or access rights[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].
- **Cell Injection Protection**: Values must be written using Google Sheets API `RAW` input mode rather than `USER_ENTERED` to prevent formula execution, and computed columns (such as `Resolved City`) must never be overwritten directly[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].
- **Ephemeral Data Handling**: Intermediate diff files such as `changes.json` contain personally identifiable information (PII) and must be generated in secure temporary directories (`mktemp -d`), never committed to session folders, shared in transcripts, or retained post-execution[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].

# References

- [proposal-execution-split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)
- [community-event-operations](community-event-operations.md)
- [community-events-eval-suite](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md)

proposed_concept.description: Automated provisioning and maintenance engine managing chapter Google Drive assets, OOXML rebranding, design system styling sweeps, and asset isolation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-create-chapter` skill automates the lifecycle provisioning, folder restructuring, and visual conformance of regional AAIF community chapters[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]. In addition to provisioning chapter estates, it provides operational tooling to audit and conform existing estate templates, trackers, and CRM workbooks to the AAIF visual identity and design system[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].

# Architecture / Specification

### Design System Conformance (`restyle_design_system.py`)

Estate visual consistency is enforced through programmatic auditing and update sweeps governed by shared styling logic in `lib/aaif_events/ooxml_style.py` and `lib/aaif_events/agent_art.py`[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]:

- **Strict Template Allowlisting**: Sweeps apply exclusively to designated template definitions (`TEMPLATE_FILES` and chapter CRM workbooks `<City> CRM.xlsx`)[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]. Files outside the explicit allowlist (such as custom drafts or dated decks created by local organizers) are skipped and logged to prevent accidental overwrite of customized organizer collateral[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].
- **SpreadsheetML Format Isolation**: Workbook styling rewrites are strictly isolated to `xl/styles.xml` and workbook theme files[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]. Cell data stored in `xl/worksheets/` and `xl/sharedStrings.xml` is never opened or altered by restyling passes[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]. Formatting handles SpreadsheetML patterns (e.g., `<patternFill>`, ARGB color definitions) distinct from presentation DrawingML to avoid silent styling failures[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].
- **Non-Overwriting Pristine Archives**: The script operates read-only by default (`--check` mode)[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]. Prior to applying writes (`--write`), pre-modification files are archived to timestamped local directories (`backups/restyle-<UTC>/`)[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]. Existing archive records are immutable; a secondary sweep preserves the earliest recorded copy rather than overwriting it with partially modified files[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].
- **Contrast and Readability Repair**: Automated passes evaluate text runs against slide background plates according to WCAG AA legibility standards, repairing contrast failures caused by dark background plate transitions[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].
- **Asset Generation Sandboxing**: Visual assets (such as chapter agent artwork) are generated in private, non-predictable temporary directories prior to deployment, eliminating symlink and multi-user race hazards on shared hosts[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].

# References

- [brand-guidelines](../guidelines/brand-guidelines.md)
- [community-event-operations](community-event-operations.md)
- [aaif-clean-data](aaif-clean-data.md)

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Clean Data Skill
proposed_concept.description: Operational intake data hygiene and normalization skill executing read-only scanning, diff-based proposals, and gated writes across community estate spreadsheets.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-clean-data` is an automated data normalization and intake hygiene skill for the AAIF community events estate, functioning as Phase 1 of the broader `aaif-sync` pipeline to sanitize incoming chapter and organizer submissions before downstream processing[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112]. It operates under an explicit [proposal-execution split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) by running read-only issue detection, generating structured before-and-after diffs, and committing modifications only upon operator approval[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill interacts with the central community intake sheet through the `gws` command-line interface driven by Python scripts, adhering to native Google Workspace formats or atomic OOXML manipulation while banning desktop office suites like LibreOffice to prevent font degradation and XML schema stripping[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].

### Operational Modes
1. **Scan (`clean.py scan`)**: Default read-only mode detecting formatting anomalies, canonicalizing LinkedIn URLs, collapsing irregular whitespace, and flagging unresolved records such as `City="Other"`, duplicate emails, or missing names[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].
2. **Apply (`clean.py apply`)**: Gated execution mode consuming an approved `changes.json` payload, applying modifications directly to the source `Form Responses` tab by header name, and logging row-level audit trails in an `Autofixes` column[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].
3. **Chapter Flags (`clean.py chapter-flags`)**: Formats submitted `Other` city cells with red highlights across role tabs to visually surface rows requiring chapter triage without mutating values or granting automated permissions[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7].

### Estate Sync Dependency
Because downstream pipeline stages (such as CRM synchronization, Chapters List population, and Google Drive access provisioning) resolve chapters through extracted city records, unresolved cities become invisible omissions rather than explicit errors[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112]. `aaif-clean-data` serves as the intake gate guaranteeing all applicants are resolved into their respective roles (`Organizers`, `Hosts`, `Speakers`, `Collaborators`)[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112][^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7].

mutations.rationale: Updates the pre-flight setup diagnostic skill with non-technical operator reporting conventions, credential resolution precedence, and Google Workspace validation scopes.

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Check Setup Skill
proposed_concept.description: Read-only diagnostic skill evaluating environment readiness, credential resolution precedence, and third-party API connectivity across Google Workspace, Slack, and Luma.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-check-setup` is a read-only pre-flight diagnostic skill designed to audit the host runtime environment and verify all external credentials required to operate the AAIF Community Events Toolkit[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77]. Formatted specifically for non-technical community operators running agents in [Goose](../resources/goose.md) or Claude Desktop, it evaluates system readiness and outputs plain-language remediation instructions without exposing secret values[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77][^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7].

# Architecture / Specification
The diagnostic engine executes `scripts/check_setup.py` using Python standard libraries to allow standalone execution without external dependencies[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77].

### Diagnostic Scope
- **Google Workspace Access**: Validates `gws` authentication, token readability, and Drive/Sheets edit permissions over the community intake spreadsheet[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77].
- **Slack Connectivity**: Issues an `auth.test` call against the AAIF Slack workspace using resolved read or write tokens[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77].
- **Luma API Access**: Queries `calendars/get` to confirm calendar management authorization[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77].
- **Local Tooling**: Inspects the presence of Python 3 and Chrome/Chromium for headless PDF report rendering[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77].

### Credential Resolution Precedence
Credentials resolve through a fixed fallback chain: environment variables, repository `.env` configuration, and the macOS system keychain (`aaif-slack-read-token`, `aaif-slack-write-token`, and `luma-api-key`)[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7]. Writing and drafting tasks remain functional even when upstream credentials fail validation, relying on direct user paste inputs[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77].

mutations.rationale: Updates the event launch announcement skill with strict public-copy privacy redaction rules, field withholding semantics, and standardized compliance footers.

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Event Announcement Post Skill
proposed_concept.description: Copy generation skill drafting concise, practitioner-focused LinkedIn launch posts for AAIF events under strict privacy redaction and compliance footer rules.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-announcement-post` is an operational agent skill that drafts scannable, builder-focused LinkedIn announcement posts for AAIF chapter and online events when RSVPs open[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]. It enforces a strict public-copy governance rule that strips all non-public attendee personal data, speaker contact details, and venue access codes from output copy and conversational transcripts[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill consumes structured event metadata retrieved directly from chapter event trackers via `fetch_tracker.py`[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].

### Structural Constraints
- **Format**: Composed of a single-line hook, what/when/where logistics, speaker topic with one key takeaway, and an RSVP call-to-action linking to Luma or Gradual.AI[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].
- **Length & Style**: Approximately 120 words, at most one emoji, and a maximum of three hashtags, adhering to an authentic "share the practice, never sell the product" house voice[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].
- **Mandatory Compliance Footer**: Terminates with a standardized footer referencing the Linux Foundation Code of Conduct and Privacy Policy[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].

### Privacy & Data Protection Rules
All event intake records and tracker entries are treated as private data. Contact parameters—such as speaker email addresses, phone numbers, door access codes, and unverified intake names—are withheld by the ingestion utility[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]. The agent is explicitly prohibited from echoing withheld values or confirming omitted specifics in conversational responses, mandating that omitted categories be referenced only by field name[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].

mutations.rationale: Updates the Slack auditing skill with Phase 8 verification architecture, multi-engine cache composition, filesystem isolation, and prompt injection defense rules.

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Slack Audit Skill
proposed_concept.description: Read-only inspection skill auditing community Slack workspace coverage, organizer rosters, topic health, and member telemetry into a consolidated HTML report.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-audit-slack` is a read-only community inspection skill providing comprehensive operational audits of the AAIF Slack workspace, verifying channel coverage for local chapters, organizer access rosters, topic room health, and active member engagement[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]. Operating as Phase 8 of the estate synchronization pipeline (`aaif-sync`), it acts as an independent out-of-band verification layer ensuring that changes applied during earlier pipeline phases reflect accurately in community communication channels[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill aggregates data across three specialized reporting engines and a shared measurement layer into a single HTML deliverable (`slack-full-audit.html`)[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d][^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]:
1. **Organizers Engine (`audit_organizers.py`)**: Reconciles accepted organizers from the intake sheet against private chapter channels and verifies chapter channel provisioning[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].
2. **Topics Engine (`audit_topics.py`)**: Evaluates activity and newcomer discoverability across thematic discussion channels using the Intake Ops Topics configuration tab[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d][^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].
3. **Members Engine (`audit_members.py`)**: Assesses workspace health and newcomer experience from the perspective of standard community participants[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].
4. **Activity Measurement Layer (`audit_activity.py`)**: Collects channel recency metrics, human message volumes, and distinct poster counts to supply telemetry to topic and member analyses[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].

### Cache Integrity and Git Leakage Protection
Raw API pulls are serialized atomically to disk with explicit workspace stamps to prevent redundant API paging[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d]. Because audit outputs and cache files contain personal member names and email addresses, files are generated with `0600` permissions inside `0700` directories[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d]. Both audit engines enforce strict repository preflight checks, aborting immediately if cache or output paths would be captured by `git add -A`[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d].

### Untrusted Input Defense
Slack member profiles, channel topics, and message bodies are handled strictly as passive data rather than instructions. Directives embedded within channel metadata or sheet cells requesting administrative promotion or channel additions are treated as unverified text and flagged to operators without altering state[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].

mutations.rationale: Documents the AGENTS.md repository convention as an emerging AAIF standard and file format governing coding agent behavior and operational constraints.

proposed_concept.title: AGENTS.md Repository Convention
proposed_concept.description: Standardized repository configuration format providing operational constraints, runtime execution contexts, and security boundaries to coding agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `AGENTS.md` file convention is a standardized repository-level specification that instructs autonomous and interactive coding agents (such as Claude Code) on operational guidelines, security constraints, and execution boundaries[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]. Within the AAIF ecosystem, `AGENTS.md` is tracked under the Conventions & File Formats taxonomy as a member-maintained project convention distinct from wire protocols[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30].

Coding assistants frequently require clear environmental demarcation between human documentation (`README.md`), skill authoring (`CONTRIBUTING.md`), visual design systems (`DESIGN.md`), and engine maintenance routines (`MAINTAINING.md`)[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]. The convention establishes symlinks (such as `CLAUDE.md`) to maintain backwards compatibility while unifying behavioral policies in a single declarative root artifact[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].

# Architecture / Specification
An `AGENTS.md` configuration enforces several fundamental operational and architectural boundaries[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]:

- **Installed Plugin vs. Checkout Boundary**: Agents must distinguish between local Git checkouts and distributed plugin runtime environments (e.g., [Goose](../resources/goose.md) or Claude Desktop)[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]. Command invocations must target `<skill-root>` variables rather than repository-relative paths (`skills/<name>/...`), ensuring script portability[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].
- **Credential Resolution Precedence**: Operational secrets required by executing scripts follow strict resolution chains: process environment variables, repository-root `.env` files, and platform-native credential storage (such as the macOS Keychain), ensuring installed plugins without shell environments authenticate safely[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].
- **Working Directory and Scratch Data Isolation**: Agents are restricted from writing scratch or runtime outputs directly to the current working directory (`cwd`), which often maps to synced user folders[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]. Outputs must be directed through designated data directories (e.g., `aaif_events.datadir`) or ephemeral scratch spaces generated via `mktemp -d`[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].
- **Personally Identifiable Information (PII) Guardrails**: Because public commits and force-pushes cannot guarantee full eradication on upstream repository hosts, `AGENTS.md` mandates that all test fixtures, logs, and docstrings utilize synthetic data, supported by automated linting scripts like `check_no_real_pii.py`[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].

# Lifecycle History
The convention originated in operational AAIF repositories such as `community-events` to mitigate common agent execution failures, including broken path assumptions and accidental credential or PII disclosure[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]. In the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream, proposals were introduced to formally catalog `AGENTS.md` as an AAIF Member convention alongside runtime control planes and communication protocols[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30].

mutations.rationale: Updates the aaif-backup operational skill with the immutable snapshot schema, platform-specific Application Support datadir isolation, and manual restore procedures.

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Backup Skill
proposed_concept.description: Operational agent skill creating timestamped, immutable local and cloud snapshots of community Google Drive assets and local spreadsheets.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-backup` is an operational agent skill designed to generate immutable, timestamped local snapshots of Google Drive files and community operational spreadsheets, such as chapter intake and tracker sheets[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7]. The skill ensures data integrity and operational resilience by preventing in-place overwrites and segregating backup state from public repository trees[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].

The skill functions across both developer Git checkouts and installed agent harnesses, adapting storage targets according to runtime environment capabilities to ensure backups survive plugin updates[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7].

# Architecture / Specification
The backup execution pipeline adheres to strict directory structures and isolation policies[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7]:

- **Snapshot File Layout**: Backups are persisted chronologically using an immutable folder structure:
  ```
  backups/<slug>/<UTC-timestamp>.<ext>
  ```
  Every execution writes a new timestamped file (e.g., `backups/aaif-community-intake-ops/2026-07-03T142530Z.xlsx`), ensuring that a directory listing reflects a complete, unmodifiable version history[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7].
- **Environment Storage Routing**: In local development checkouts, snapshots are written to the local `backups/` directory, which is git-ignored to prevent inadvertent committing of organizer or attendee data[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]. In installed plugin environments (such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md) or Claude Desktop), files are written to system-level application storage (e.g., `~/Library/Application Support/AAIF/backups/` on macOS) to guarantee persistence across plugin updates[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7].
- **Invocation & CLI Interface**: The backup routine is invoked via Python scripts targeting either the default intake sheet, a specific Google Drive file ID, or a local file path:
  ```bash
  python3 <toolkit>/skills/aaif-backup/scripts/backup.py [target]
  ```
- **Manual Restoration Protocol**: Restoration is strictly manual and non-destructive. Operators copy specific row values or cell data back from snapshots into live sheets rather than overwriting target files, preserving complex formulas, role tabs, and conditional formatting[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7].

# Lifecycle History
Authored as part of the `aaif/community-events` operational tooling, `aaif-backup` implements library-independent data directory helpers to maintain compatibility with standalone zip distributions and pinned tests[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6][^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy Contributions Skill
proposed_concept.description: Operational contributor and agent workflow enforcing SKOS-Lite data schemas, deferred fields, local validations, and deduplicated Define issue routing.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-taxonomy-contributions` skill guides agents and contributors in routing, preparing, and validating submissions to the AAIF Common Taxonomy and Landscape workstream (`aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape`)[^evt-public-agents-pr-3]. The skill consolidates schema rules, submission routes, and pre-drafting validation checks that are otherwise distributed across schemas, contributing guides, and taxonomy source files[^evt-public-agents-pr-3].

By packaging routing logic into an agent skill, it prevents common contribution errors, such as opening pull requests for deferred fields where an issue or weekly sync review is required[^evt-public-agents-pr-3].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill equips autonomous agents with structured routines for taxonomy intake[^evt-public-agents-pr-3]:

- **Routing and Pre-Drafting Checks**: Agents search for existing in-flight issues and pull requests on the proposed term or landscape entry prior to generating contributions, preventing duplicate submissions[^evt-public-agents-pr-3].
- **Schema and Tone Conformance**: Enforces pre-competitive, objective definition standards. It strips marketing language and superlatives (e.g., "best open source platform") in accordance with schema rules, and verifies required fields including `name`, `homepage_url`, `description`, `project`, and `logo`[^evt-public-agents-pr-3].
- **Define Issue Formatting**: Outlines the standard template and evidentiary requirements for creating formal "Define" tracking issues in the workstream[^evt-public-agents-pr-3].
- **Dynamic Policy Fetching**: Instructs agents to dynamically fetch the latest guidelines from `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` documentation before drafting, ensuring graceful adaptation if the workstream updates its processes[^evt-public-agents-pr-3].
- **Empirical Efficiency**: In automated evaluation benchmarks, agents equipped with the skill completed contribution routing in 6 targeted tool calls compared to 15 exploratory calls required by baseline agents[^evt-public-agents-pr-3].

# Lifecycle History
The skill was submitted to `aaif/public-agents` in PR #3 to streamline contributor engagement with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-public-agents-pr-3].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive ecosystem directory and catalog tracking member initiatives, external projects, and category taxonomies across agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape (`landscape.yml` in `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape`) is an interactive directory and categorical index tracking foundation member projects, open-source initiatives, and external technologies across the agentic AI domain[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-31]. Maintained by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the catalog classifies tools and frameworks into structured categories governed by strict pre-competitive schema definitions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30].

The landscape serves as a vendor-neutral index helping practitioners identify established runtime frameworks, communication protocols, developer tools, and governance solutions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30].

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape catalog is defined declaratively in YAML and enforces specific structural invariants[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30]:

- **Metadata Schema**: Every entry requires four standard fields: `name`, `homepage_url`, `description`, and `project` (with values such as `member` or `external`), alongside asset markers such as `logo`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30]. Descriptions must adhere to neutral, pre-competitive language without superlatives[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30].
- **Taxonomic Subcategories**:
  - *Gateways & Control Planes*: Proposed under Agent Runtimes, Frameworks & Workflow Orchestration to classify traffic mediation and policy enforcement infrastructure like [AgentGateway](../resources/agentgateway.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30].
  - *Conventions & File Formats*: Proposed under Protocols & Discovery Registries to catalog repository-level agent configurations such as [AGENTS.md](../standards/agents-md.md), distinguishing them from network-level communication protocols like MCP and A2A[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30].
- **Link Integrity and Health Checks**: The catalog is periodically audited to resolve dead URLs, redirected project domains, and tracking status updates (such as A2A transitioning from external to TC Approved member status)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-31].

# Lifecycle History
Originally launched as a static catalog, maintenance of `landscape.yml` was transferred to the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream, where domain editors review additions and manage structural subcategories through pull requests[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-31].

mutations.rationale: Align reporting template requirements with Technical Committee PR title format and monthly-report label specifications.

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Reporting Template and Submission Workflow
proposed_concept.description: Standardized reporting template, monthly review timeline, pull request naming conventions, and automated discovery labels for AAIF working group reports.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Working Group Reporting Template standardizes the operational reporting process required for all Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) working groups and workstreams[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62]. Working groups compile monthly updates on milestones, charter deliverables, cross-group collaborations, and governance escalations to provide visibility to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and the broader community[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62].

# Specification

## Pull Request Workflow and Naming Rules

To allow automated indexing and report discovery across all AAIF repositories, monthly report pull requests must adhere to explicit naming and labeling rules[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62]:

- **PR Title**: Pull requests submitting monthly reports must follow the format `[Report] <YYYY-MM>` (e.g., `[Report] 2026-09`), deprecating previous free-form variations such as `[Report] <WG name> – <Month YYYY>`[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-52].
- **Labels**: Every report pull request must be tagged with the `monthly-report` label[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62].
- **File Naming**: Report Markdown files are subject to strict case-sensitive file naming conventions within repository directories[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62].

## Template Sections

Reports capture:
1. **Charter Status and Roadmaps**: Summary of progress against scheduled roadmap milestones.
2. **Artifact Deliverables**: Published patterns, reference architectures, standards, or taxonomy terms.
3. **Cross-WG Collaboration**: Alignment with related efforts such as [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) or [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).
4. **Decisions and Escalations**: Explicit notation of any required Technical Committee decisions (or statement confirming no TC decisions are required)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-13].

mutations.rationale: Add the newly defined Mandate concept established in the Agentic Commerce taxonomy.

proposed_concept.title: Mandate
proposed_concept.description: Agentic Commerce taxonomy term defining an explicit authorization and boundary agreement governing an agent's authority to act or transact on behalf of a principal.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

A Mandate is an Agentic Commerce taxonomy concept representing an explicit delegation of authority granted by a [principal](../taxonomy/principal.md) to an agent[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-77]. It defines the precise operational, financial, and contractual constraints within which an agent is legally and operationally permitted to execute tasks or financial commitments[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-77].

# Architecture / Specification

In agentic commerce architectures, a mandate functions as the authorization contract underpinning agent transactions, including [agent-in-the-loop transactions](../taxonomy/agent-in-the-loop-transaction.md) and [agent-initiated transactions](../taxonomy/agent-initiated-transaction.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-77]. 

A mandate typically articulates:
- **Scope of Representation**: Permitted counterparty domains, merchant registries, or catalog surfaces.
- **Transaction Boundaries**: Per-transaction or aggregate monetary thresholds and expiration timelines.
- **Execution Constraints**: Required checkpoints, such as invoking a [human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) or [delegated-payment](../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md) execution mechanism when transactions exceed authorized boundaries.

mutations.rationale: Incorporate Goose autonomous agent framework metadata and new CI validation constraints for landscape data files.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive ecosystem directory, catalog, and schema-validated metadata registry tracking member initiatives, external projects, and category mappings across the agentic AI domain.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive directory and schema-validated ecosystem map cataloging projects, frameworks, protocols, and control planes across the agentic AI domain[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28]. Maintained by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), it indexes AAIF-hosted member projects and external ecosystem tools into curated functional categories[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27].

# Architecture / Specification

## Project Classification and Hosted Frameworks

The landscape classifies entries by operational domains such as Autonomous Agent Frameworks, Gateways and Control Planes, and Specification Formats[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27]. Foundation-hosted projects include:
- [Goose](../resources/goose.md): Open-source general-purpose autonomous agent runtime (donated at launch and categorized under Autonomous Agent Frameworks with member project classification)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27].
- Model Context Protocol (MCP): Context and tool integration protocol.
- [AgentGateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) and [AGENTS.md](../standards/agents-md.md): Infrastructure mediation and repo configuration formats[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27].

## Validation and Security Controls

To ensure runtime reliability, browser parser parity, and denial-of-service resilience, entries in `landscape/landscape.yml` are validated via an automated test and CI enforcement pipeline (`validate-landscape.mjs`)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28]:
- **Parser Parity**: CI and the browser application parse using `FAILSAFE_SCHEMA` and fixed depth parameters to prevent type distortion (e.g., numeric scalar strings turning into numbers)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- **Resource and Graph Budgets**: A strict 512 KB file cap, limits of 500 items, and maximum graph budgets of 5,000 objects/arrays and 20,000 references prevent denial-of-service from YAML expansion[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- **Prohibited Structures**: Disallows YAML node reuse (aliases or cycles for collections), merge keys, control or format characters, and unescaped credentials[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- **Symlink Protection**: Automated checks prevent committed symlinks in deployable source artifacts to guard against runner file exposure[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Implementation guide establishing architectural controls, runtime hook enforcement, and network gateway checkpoints for agent environments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide outlines architectural controls, operational defenses, and governance boundaries required to secure autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents across enterprise deployments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]. The guidelines address supply-chain integrity, execution isolation, identity delegation, and boundary mediation across internal runtimes and remote protocol boundaries.

# Architecture / Specification

## Boundary Enforcement and Checkpoints

The guidance establishes a dual-layer architectural control pattern separating in-process lifecycle interception from network boundary traversal[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]:

- **Runtime Hook Enforcement**: Runtimes enforce pre-execution and lifecycle policy checks directly at hook points across the run lifecycle[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]. When an agent attempts an action, the runtime suspends execution and hands the pending action payload along with preceding contextual trace data to dedicated policy code before invocation proceeds[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38].
- **Gateway Checkpoint Mediation**: Network-level Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateways serve as network path control checkpoints rather than solitary runtime enforcers[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]. The gateway provides a unified mediation endpoint for remote MCP servers, authenticates sessions via OAuth, evaluates per-tool permission policies, and captures comprehensive audit event payloads[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38].

This division ensures that policy enforcement occurs inside the execution loop while protocol translation, authentication federation, and network payload capture are offloaded to proxy infrastructure such as [AgentGateway](../resources/agentgateway.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38].

# Lifecycle History

Proposed under PR#38 in the Security and Privacy Working Group to decouple network gateway capabilities from in-runtime hook evaluation in Section 3.1 and standardize vendor-neutral reference tooling[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an AAIF technical body tasked with standardizing protocol interoperability, transaction governance, identity mandates, and financial interaction boundaries for agent-led commerce[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-9]. Its scope spans agent-mediated checkout workflows, machine-to-machine payments, and verifiable consumer intent delegation.

# Architecture / Specification

The working group evaluates emerging protocols against agentic transaction lifecycles, identifying handoffs and capability boundaries across:

- **onX**: Specifications governing verifiable merchant interaction and transaction framing[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-9].
- **Machine Payments Protocol (MPP)**: Autonomous agent settlement and machine-to-machine financial transfer frameworks[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-9].
- **Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)**: Shared interoperability primitives standardizing catalog discovery, checkout handoffs, and consumer mandate verification[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-9].

Each protocol is analyzed along four dimensions: problem formulation, functional mechanics, governance status, and operational handoff boundaries to peer protocols[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-9].

# Lifecycle History

In September 2026, the working group delivered comparative evaluations of the onX, MPP, and UCP August releases, detailing protocol governance and cross-standard integration touchpoints[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-9].

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: Governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation overseeing technical vision, project lifecycles, working groups, and open agent standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Technical Committee (TC) is the technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation, operating under the AAIF Governing Board (GB) as part of The Linux Foundation [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04]. Adopted on March 3, 2026, the TC Charter establishes the committee's mandate to define technical vision, review and recommend technical projects, charter and archive working groups, and administer the foundation's project lifecycle policies [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].

# Architecture / Specification

## Purpose and Responsibilities

The TC assists the Governing Board with technical governance through several primary functions [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04]:

- **Project Evaluation and Recommendations:** Reviewing incoming project proposals and recommending qualifying initiatives to the Governing Board for acceptance as Technical Projects [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].
- **Lifecycle Administration:** Applying and maintaining the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md), governing transitions across stages (including Sandbox, Growth, and Impact), and defining the [Project Proposal Process](../policies/project-proposal-process.md) [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04] [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-8f2953e0].
- **Working Group Oversight:** Establishing, managing, and archiving technical Working Groups under the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md) and reviewing monthly working group reports [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04] [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-8f2953e0].
- **Technical Coordination:** Fostering cross-project collaboration, establishing architectural baselines, and advising the Governing Board on technical resource priorities [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].

## Composition and Leadership

Each Platinum Member of the AAIF is entitled to appoint one representative to the TC [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04]. Foundational voting members appointed by the Governing Board for the term spanning March 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026 include [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-8f2953e0]:

- David Soria Parra (Anthropic) – TC Chair
- Caitie McCaffrey (Microsoft) – TC Co-Chair
- Alan Blount (Google)
- Bradley Axen (Block)
- James Ward (Amazon Web Services)
- Nick Cooper (OpenAI)
- Sambhav Kothari (Bloomberg)
- Steve Faulkner (Cloudflare)

## Decision-Making and Voting Rules

While operating primarily on consensus, formal decisions follow defined procedural rules [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04]:

- **Voting Weight:** Each voting member possesses one vote [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].
- **Quorum:** At least 50% of voting members must be present during a meeting to conduct binding votes [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].
- **Lazy Consensus:** Routine proposals follow a 7-day silence-as-agreement model, automatically approving actions if no formal objection is registered within seven calendar days [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].
- **Electronic Voting:** If an objection arises against a lazy-consensus proposal, electronic approval requires a majority vote across all TC voting members [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].
- **Charter Amendments:** Changes to the TC Charter require approval by two-thirds of the TC and final approval by the Governing Board [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].

## Hosted Technical Projects

The TC oversees prominent foundational open-source agent projects, including Model Context Protocol (MCP) and [goose](../resources/goose.md) at the Impact Stage [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-8f2953e0].

proposed_concept.title: Slack Community Audit
proposed_concept.description: Read-only diagnostic inspection skill auditing AAIF Slack channels, message hygiene, cross-posting, and unsolicited sales pitches.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-audit-slack` skill provides read-only diagnostic and administrative tooling for inspecting the health, configuration, and conversational integrity of AAIF community Slack workspaces [^evt-community-events-pr-61]. It operates out-of-band from state reconciliation engines like [aaif-sync](../skills/aaif-sync.md), producing terminal-only reports without mutating workspace content or storing untrusted message text on local disks [^evt-community-events-pr-61].

# Architecture / Specification

## Sales and Spam Detection Engine

The audit suite includes `skills/aaif-audit-slack/scripts/audit_spam.py`, a specialized inspection script that evaluates public message activity and direct message telemetry to score accounts exhibiting uninvited commercial outreach [^evt-community-events-pr-61]. Scored heuristics include:

- Unsolicited service offerings and vendor partnership solicitations [^evt-community-events-pr-61].
- Direct invitation requests ("DM me") and financial incentives [^evt-community-events-pr-61].
- LinkedIn account rental propositions [^evt-community-events-pr-61].
- Cross-posting identical message payloads across three or more public channels [^evt-community-events-pr-61].
- Promotional pitches posted outside dedicated promotional channels [^evt-community-events-pr-61].

Shared partner vendor rooms (`ext-*`) and administrative organizer rooms (`*-organizers`) are explicitly excluded from scoring [^evt-community-events-pr-61]. Audit outputs represent lead indicators for human administrative review in the workspace console rather than automated enforcement triggers [^evt-community-events-pr-61].

## Security and Allowlist Boundaries

The audit tool extends the approved `aaif_events.slack.ALLOWED_METHODS` allowlist with read-only endpoints `conversations.replies` and `search.messages` [^evt-community-events-pr-61]. Untrusted message snippets and user display names are strictly sanitized and bounded inside `<<msg>>` terminal wrappers to prevent log escape and prompt injection vulnerabilities [^evt-community-events-pr-61].

## Slack API Pagination Defenses

Live empirical evaluations revealed that passing the `oldest=` timestamp parameter to Slack's `conversations.history` API occasionally returns empty channel payloads despite active conversations within the queried window [^evt-community-events-pr-61]. To ensure complete audit coverage, the scanner pages sequentially through channels without `oldest` and terminates traversal manually upon encountering the window cutoff [^evt-community-events-pr-61].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy & Reliability Survey
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral 16-question empirical survey assessing production agent system architectures, human verification practices, failure consequences, and industry priorities.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Accuracy & Reliability Survey is a 16-question, platform-neutral empirical instrument designed by the [Accuracy & Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) to gather firsthand operational data from practitioners deploying AI agent systems into real-world workflows [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891]. Designed to be completed in approximately 20 minutes, the survey explicitly disallows identifying or confidential details and aggregates responses to prioritize open foundation engineering initiatives [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].

# Architecture / Specification

## Eligibility Gating and Focal-System Anchoring

The survey utilizes a strict gating mechanism in Question 1 based on personal experience during the preceding six months [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891]:

- **Qualifying Cohorts:** Practitioners with experience in serious pilots (testing in intended work settings), limited deployments (normal work for some users), broad deployments (normal work for most users), paused or retired deployments, or unclassified real-world systems continue to the full survey [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].
- **Early-Exit Cohorts:** Respondents reporting only demo, prototype, or generic research work, secondhand knowledge, or no relevant system experience are routed directly to an early-exit closure [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].
- **Focal System Principle:** Qualified respondents evaluate one focal system throughout questions 2 through 16 to preserve observational consistency across operational metrics [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].

## Survey Inquiry Domains

The instrument assesses agent operations across five distinct analytical areas [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891]:

1. **System Profile (Q2–Q6):** Practitioner roles (design, testing, operation, human review), domain areas, structural composition, human verification checkpoints, and organizational scale [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].
2. **Benefits and Constraints (Q7–Q8):** Measurable productivity gains weighed against deployment bottlenecks [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].
3. **Accuracy and Reliability Failures (Q9–Q13):** Incident frequency, contributing error sources, pre-impact failure detection rates, severity of adverse outcomes, and primary evidentiary validation methods [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].
4. **Industry Priorities (Q14–Q15):** Cross-industry standardization needs and preferred open-source technical resources [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].
5. **Optional Closing Context (Q16):** Unstructured commentary regarding operational reliability hurdles [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].

proposed_concept.title: URACE Specification
proposed_concept.description: Blueprint specification providing 72 portable architectural primitives, recursive runtime loops, cognitive resume compaction, and deterministic rule-graph tracking.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Universal Recursive Autonomous Co-Founder Engine (URACE) is an open-source, blueprint-first specification designed to govern recursive multi-agent software engineering loops without dependency bloat or runtime vendor lock-in [^evt-project-proposals-issue-60]. Dedicated to the public domain under the CC0 1.0 license, URACE was proposed to the AAIF under the Sandbox lifecycle stage to decouple agent lifecycle coordination logic from concrete execution platforms [^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].

# Architecture / Specification

## Blueprint Primitives

URACE delivers an install-as-bootstrap standard (`URACE.md`) containing 72 modular building blocks categorized into architectural patterns, data schemas, authority mechanisms, and regression contracts [^evt-project-proposals-issue-60]. Developers import structural primitives natively into target codebases without packaging dependencies [^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].

## Ecosystem Interoperability

URACE integrates across foundational AAIF standards and execution engines [^evt-project-proposals-issue-60]:

- **Dynamic Counterpart to AGENTS.md:** While [AGENTS.md](../standards/agents-md.md) establishes static repository boundaries and guidance for incoming agents, URACE acts as the dynamic, state-tracking runtime loop interpreting evolution objectives and validating active modifications [^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].
- **Pluggable Execution Harnesses:** URACE decouples lifecycle state transitions from code generation, consuming Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients and runtimes such as [goose](../resources/goose.md) as modular "Executors" while URACE independently manages rule graphs and boundaries [^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].

## Core Capabilities

- **Token-Preserving Compaction (`urace /compact`):** Implements an algorithmic lifecycle compaction protocol that summarizes linear execution histories into an evolving semantic Cognitive Resume to prevent context window degradation over extended recursive sessions [^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].
- **Deterministic Rule-Graph Tracking (`urace /rules`):** Maps every proposed codebase modification against an immutable, queryable snapshot graph of approved permissions to guarantee auditable lineage back to human policy decisions [^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].
- **Zero-Dependency Bootstrapping:** Executes through single-document definitions triggered via local environment launchers [^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].

proposed_concept.title: nono
proposed_concept.description: Open-source agent runtime security tool providing kernel-enforced sandboxing, credential isolation, and Sigstore-based instruction verification.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

nono is an open-source agent runtime security tool providing low-latency, kernel-enforced sandboxing, credential isolation, and instruction verification across coding agents, custom frameworks, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61] Created in February 2026 by Luke Hinds, nono was proposed for entry into the [Project Lifecycle](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) as an Agentic AI Foundation Sandbox project sponsored by Sambhav Kothari of Bloomberg.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61] The tool intercepts execution at the operating system layer to enforce policy boundaries that remain external to the agent's context and control.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61]

# Architecture / Specification

nono structures agent execution security through layered host-level protections, composable policies, and cryptographic provenance checks:[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61]

- **Kernel-Enforced Sandboxing**: Isolates agent process execution, restricting access to designated filesystem paths, system calls, and network interfaces on Linux and macOS hosts.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61]
- **Credential Management & Isolation**: Confines secrets and sensitive tokens away from agent memory, injecting credentials strictly into authorized per-command tool invocations.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61]
- **Instruction and Skill Provenance**: Verifies the source-code origin and integrity of policy-covered instruction files—including [AGENTS.md](../standards/agents-md.md) specifications—using Sigstore digital signatures to reject unsigned or tampered prompts at the system access level.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61]
- **MCP Server Confinement**: Enforces least-privilege host permissions on MCP server processes, binding their reachable endpoints, local files, and environment variables.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61]
- **Host-Network Boundary Division**: Operates at the host boundary, designed to complement network-level reverse proxies and routers such as [agentgateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) by mediating local process capability while relaying egress traffic upstream.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61]

# Lifecycle History

The project originated in February 2026 and utilizes an open governance structure managed by a Maintainer Council, handling architectural changes through nono Enhancement Proposals (NEPs).[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61] In October 2026, nono submitted an application for AAIF Sandbox status under the Apache 2.0 license, citing production adoption across enterprise toolchains including Datadog and Okta, and formal integration with runtimes such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md).[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61]
