proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing open threat models, security design patterns, and operational controls for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is a technical body within the Agentic AI Foundation chartered to establish vendor-neutral threat models, architectural design patterns, and operational controls across the agent lifecycle.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c] Led by elected chair Alex Frazer, the group coordinates core deliverables with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and cross-links terminology initiatives with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group maintains multiple active workstreams advancing normative guidance and technical controls:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c]

- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns**: Merges reusable architectural primitives into the [Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md), including the [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md), [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md), and [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) patterns.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c]
- **Threat Modeling and Risk Assessment**: Develops comparative gap analyses across OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, and NIST frameworks to publish structured agentic threat profiles.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c]
- **Security Best Practices Guide**: Authors implementation guidelines for developers and enterprises, standardizing runtime hooks and boundary enforcement in [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c]
- **Cross-Working Group Review**: Implements the [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md) to audit external project proposals and interoperability standards.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c]

# Lifecycle History

Chartered in May 2026 following initial formation in February 2026, the working group transitioned its repositories to public operation in June 2026.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c] To accommodate global participation, the group introduced an alternating Asia-Pacific (APAC) meeting track alongside its standard schedule in late 2026.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c] Technical deliverables follow GitHub-based peer review workflows, requiring independent review sign-offs before merging into main branches.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c]

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining vendor-neutral standards, delegation frameworks, and verification test suites for agent identity and trust.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Identity and Trust Working Group is an AAIF technical body tasked with defining open identity standards, cryptographic delegation frameworks, and operational verification suites for autonomous agents.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-18] The group models edge-case lifecycle semantics, such as disputed delegation-tree revocation, identifier re-registration, and post-compromise key recovery, validating specifications against standardized evidentiary test vectors.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-18] [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-20]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group focuses on architectural trust boundaries and formal delegation state machines:[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-18] [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-20]

- **Delegation Tree Lifecycle**: Resolves conflict states where parent authority is revoked while active child subagent delegations remain presented, establishing deterministic rejection semantics for downstream verifiers.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-18]
- **Identifier Re-Registration & Continuity**: Defines verifiable mechanisms linking historical [Action Records](../taxonomy/action-record.md) and revoked identifiers to freshly provisioned agent keys without carrying stale grants forward.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-18] [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-20]
- **Recovery Attestations**: Evaluates recovery profiles where registry signatures and Responsible entity attestations combine over software attestation proofs to carry revocation records and dispute histories forward while invalidating compromised signing authority.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-20]
- **Test Vector Conformance**: Coordinates formal test vector corpora with projects like `agent-evidence-vectors` to benchmark deterministic verification tools and mandate consistent outcome assertion across interoperable agent harnesses.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-18] [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-20]

# Lifecycle History

In October 2026, the working group initiated formal review of delegation lifecycle test suites addressing disputed revocation in delegation hierarchies, key loss recovery, and identifier re-registration.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-18] [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-20]

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing open threat models, security design patterns, and operational controls across agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared engineering discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6]. The group develops open threat models, architectural security design patterns, operational security guidelines, and assessment checklists that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to secure autonomous agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6].

# Leadership and Governance

The working group is chaired by Alex Frazer (Runlayer) and co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google), appointed by the Platinum and Gold members of the group [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6]. The Technical Committee (TC) established that chair term boundaries align with the annual anniversary of charter approval rather than calendar years [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

To accommodate global participation across multiple time zones, the working group conducts two alternating biweekly meeting tracks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6]:
- **Primary Meeting:** Held biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6].
- **APAC Meeting:** Held biweekly on Mondays at 9:00 PM ET on alternate weeks to provide a working-hours session for contributors across Asia-Pacific [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

# Deliverables and Workstreams

- **Threat Modeling:** Completed the initial deliverable, the [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md), analyzing methodologies including STRIDE and PASTA against dynamic runtime systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93]. Ongoing work focuses on building operational threat models extending MITRE ATLAS and OWASP frameworks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
- **Design Patterns Catalog:** Authoring standardized architectural patterns, including initial merged drafts for [approval-checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md), [attested-isolated-runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md), and [kill-switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
- **Security Best Practices Guide:** Published the first draft of the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) guide and opened the repository to external community contributions via pull requests [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
- **Cross-WG Security Reviews:** Driving cross-group alignment with the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](observability-and-traceability.md) on telemetry seams and the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](agentic-commerce.md) on identity and transaction boundaries via the [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
- **Taxonomy and Terminology:** Contributing domain definitions and security terms in collaboration with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting workstream curating vendor-neutral SKOS-Lite taxonomies, definition merge standards, and agent ecosystem classifications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative establishing a vendor-neutral, shared vocabulary and ecosystem classification for agentic AI [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]. Co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream defines canonical concepts across technical domains to ensure conceptual consistency throughout the foundation [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].

# Governance and Merge Rules

The workstream operates an asynchronous editorial model anchored by designated Domain Editors nominated as working group delegates [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]. Domain Editors draft candidate definitions originating in their respective working groups and conduct peer reviews [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].

Under merge rules adopted in September 2026:
- A terminology pull request may merge asynchronously once two Domain Editors have approved it and all review comments have been resolved [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].
- Synchronous live votes during workstream meetings are reserved strictly for contested or debated terms [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].
- A structured "Ready for Review" milestone prioritizes pull requests that have successfully completed the intake workflow [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].

# Operational Status

In September 2026, the workstream merged seven definitions across four pull requests (`Human curated`, `Meta-harness`, `Human in the loop`, `Trust`, `Identifier`, `Attestation`, and `Delegation`), expanding the confirmed taxonomy baseline from 1 to 8 terms [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]. An additional 25 definitions are progressing through review across member working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].

On 14 September 2026, the workstream formally agreed to pause development of the [Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md) deliverable to concentrate full reviewer capacity on processing the taxonomy backlog [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]. Resuming Landscape intake is subject to Technical Committee review and agreement on objective inclusion criteria [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].

# Overview

The Agentic AI Landscape is an ecosystem directory, catalog, and schema-validated metadata registry designed to track open-source projects, enterprise frameworks, protocols, and tooling across the agentic AI landscape [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-19b34556]. The project was initiated under the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to provide interactive visibility into ecosystem components [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-19b34556].

# Operational Status and Roadmap

On 14 September 2026, the Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream agreed to pause Landscape contributions and maintenance to focus collective reviewer effort entirely on taxonomy definitions [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]. Contribution guidelines were updated via pull request #61 to redirect external submissions to the terminology stream [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].

Resuming active Landscape development requires formal acknowledgment from the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and established inclusion criteria [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]. Because determining vendor, platform, and project eligibility impacts foundation neutrality, proposed inclusion criteria and categorization granularity will be presented to the Technical Committee before Landscape intake reopens [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide provides practical implementation guidance, runtime policy enforcement standards, and architectural defensive controls for deploying autonomous agents securely [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93]. Authored within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guide translates high-level threat models into concrete hardening recommendations for agent developers and platform operators [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

# Publication and Review Status

The first complete draft of the best practices guide was published in October 2026 and opened to external community contributions through the established GitHub pull request review process [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

Key areas under review include:
- Network gate boundaries and egress filtering for agent runtimes.
- Sandboxing and capability authorization models.
- Inline credential masking and token mediation controls [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

Contribution triage is coordinated by working group leads, with periodic community review calls highlighted in working group monthly reports [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

proposed_concept.title: Attestation and Evidence Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF technical working group defining vendor-neutral standards, verification taxonomies, and portable evidence bundles for independently checkable agent actions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Attestation & Evidence Working Group (AE-WG) is a cross-cutting technical body proposed within the Agentic AI Foundation to make AI agent actions, decisions, authorizations, and outcomes independently verifiable across organizational boundaries [^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6]. While sibling working groups address specific aspects of agent behavior—such as identity in [Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), telemetry in [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), and execution history in [Workflows & Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)—AE-WG focuses on the second-party and third-party verifiability of durable evidence records without requiring reliance on a central authority [^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6].

# Architecture / Specification
The proposed working group operates across four core focus areas [^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6]:
- **Bilateral and Multi-Party Attestation**: Establishing protocols where each party to an interaction seals its own observations, deriving agreement or divergence through verifiable comparison rather than assertion.
- **Portable Evidence Bundles**: Designing self-describing, offline-verifiable bundles that declare their completeness and disclosure boundaries, returning artifacts, signed refusals, or cryptographic proofs of absence.
- **Witness and Root-of-Trust Taxonomies**: Categorizing and standardizing verification primitives across transparency logs, cosigners, timestamp authorities, Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), Hardware Security Modules (HSMs), and secure elements.
- **Cross-WG Coordination**: Maintaining liaison seats with sibling working groups such as [Governance, Risk & Regulatory](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) for regulatory mapping and [Security & Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) for privacy-preserving disclosures.

## Scope Boundaries
- **In-Scope**: Evidence vocabularies and class hierarchies, action attestation, commitment prior to observation, boundary evidence interchange, and verifiable disclosure mechanisms [^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6].
- **Out-of-Scope**: Direct identity credentialing, telemetry wire formats, evaluation scoring or benchmark verdicts, threat modeling, payment operations, hardware attestation mechanisms themselves, and foundation-operated ledgers [^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6].

# Lifecycle History
- **Proposed Charter**: Submitted as an initial cross-working-group charter proposal by Steven Mih (Action State) with a 90-day ramp plan targeting an initial Evidence Vocabulary v0, sibling evidence requirement matrices, and a gap analysis for [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) review [^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Working Group Monthly Report Skill
proposed_concept.description: Procedural agent skill automating the generation, evidence ledger compilation, and submission validation of AAIF working group monthly reports to the Technical Committee.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-wg-monthly-report` skill automates the compilation of evidence-backed monthly progress reports submitted by working group chairs to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-b41d2241e043-0366462a]. The skill executes locally within working group repositories, assembling an audit ledger from GitHub pull requests, issues, releases, and meeting notes, and formats the output to `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md` adhering to [working-group-reporting-template](../guidelines/working-group-reporting-template.md) [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-b41d2241e043-0366462a].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill enforces a five-stage operational workflow [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-b41d2241e043-0366462a]:
1. **Contract Establishment**: Resolves the working group identity, reporting period, local templates (`reporting/TEMPLATE.md`), and authoritative Technical Committee reporting constraints.
2. **Evidence Ledger Compilation**: Queries GitHub via CLI (`gh pr list`, `gh issue list`, `gh release list`) and reads meeting notes to extract verified achievements, dates, outcomes, and objective alignments [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-b41d2241e043-0366462a].
3. **Report Drafting**: Generates standard sections including Summary, Progress Against Objectives, Ecosystem Highlights, Blockers and Risks, Decisions Needed from the TC, Next Month's Focus, and Metrics / Links [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-f863c50ea9a7-ebe3d9f2].
4. **Validation**: Verifies that every assertion links to durable evidence, confirms calendar date boundaries, ensures TC decisions carry actionable recommendations, and checks PR title and file path conventions [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-b41d2241e043-0366462a].
5. **Handoff**: Delivers the completed report draft and pull request instructions to the working group chair for review and submission [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-b41d2241e043-0366462a].

# Lifecycle History
- **Authoritative Definition**: Consolidated in `aaif/working-group-chairs` under `skills/aaif-wg-monthly-report/SKILL.md` alongside the canonical `template.md` [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-b41d2241e043-0366462a] [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-f863c50ea9a7-ebe3d9f2].

mutations.rationale: Align reporting template guidelines with the authoritative template structure, required section schemas, and PR conventions specified in the working group chairs repository.

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Reporting Template Guideline
proposed_concept.description: Standardized reporting template, filing conventions, and required evidence sections for AAIF working groups reporting monthly to the Technical Committee.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Reporting Template defines the canonical document structure and submission protocol for monthly status reports submitted by AAIF working groups to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-f863c50ea9a7-ebe3d9f2]. Maintained in the `aaif/working-group-chairs` repository and executed via [aaif-wg-monthly-report](../skills/aaif-wg-monthly-report.md), this format ensures asynchronous scannability and verifiable progress tracking across foundation workstreams [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-b41d2241e043-0366462a].

# Architecture / Specification
Reports must be saved to `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md` (e.g., `reporting/2026-06-report.md`) and submitted via pull request titled `[Report] <YYYY-MM>` with the `monthly-report` label [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-f863c50ea9a7-ebe3d9f2]. Reports are due on the final business day of the reporting month, initiating a 7-calendar-day TC review window [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-f863c50ea9a7-ebe3d9f2].

## Required Schema Sections
- **Frontmatter Metadata**: Captures working group name, reporting period, chair names with affiliations, and submission date [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-f863c50ea9a7-ebe3d9f2].
- **Summary**: A concise 2–3 sentence executive synopsis [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-f863c50ea9a7-ebe3d9f2].
- **Progress Against Objectives**: Concrete deliverables tied to charter goals, prior month commitments, or tracked KPIs [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-f863c50ea9a7-ebe3d9f2].
- **Ecosystem Highlights**: External cross-group engagements such as OWASP, AARM, or MCP [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-f863c50ea9a7-ebe3d9f2].
- **Blockers and Risks**: Identified impediments with associated impact, dependencies, and owners [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-f863c50ea9a7-ebe3d9f2].
- **Decisions Needed from the TC**: Explicit, actionable requests with deadlines and recommended motions [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-f863c50ea9a7-ebe3d9f2].
- **Next Month's Focus**: Top 2–3 prioritized objectives [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-f863c50ea9a7-ebe3d9f2].
- **Metrics / Links**: Verified URLs to merged PRs, releases, issues, and dashboard milestones [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-f863c50ea9a7-ebe3d9f2].

# Lifecycle History
- **Standardized**: Merged into `aaif/working-group-chairs` as the authoritative template under `skills/aaif-wg-monthly-report/template.md` [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-f863c50ea9a7-ebe3d9f2].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Implementation guide establishing architectural controls, runtime hook enforcement, and network gateway boundaries for secure agent deployments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide establishes architectural controls, runtime boundary enforcement, and threat mitigation standards for deploying autonomous AI agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42]. Developed by the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guideline defines isolation profiles across host environments, hardware execution layers, and credential management boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42].

# Architecture / Specification
The framework defines layered security baselines covering process isolation, memory protection, and authorization token delegation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42].

## Confidential Computing and Credential Boundaries
In confidential computing architectures (such as Intel TDX or AMD SEV), hardware isolation cryptographically protects guest memory from unauthorized access by the host hypervisor and co-located workloads [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42]. However, security guidelines clarify that hardware protection does not eliminate bearer token exposure risks within the execution environment [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42]:
- Bearer tokens released to guest software grant access to any entity possessing the token, as specified in RFC 6750 §1.2 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42].
- Exposure risk is determined by token permissions, audience scoping, and temporal validity rather than physical memory isolation alone [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42].
- Guest software threat models (such as Intel TDX guest profiles) treat in-guest software compromise as a distinct security boundary separate from hypervisor isolation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42].

# Lifecycle History
- **Credential Exposure Revision**: Proposed under PR#42 in `aaif/wg-security-and-privacy` to correct the Section 2 isolation matrix regarding hardware-protected credential assumptions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream curating a shared SKOS-Lite taxonomy and ecosystem map across foundation technical working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream serves as the horizontal architectural bridge across all top-level technical working groups in the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-65b1abe3]. Approved on June 21, 2026, the workstream is chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and co-chaired by Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-e6083ea5]. Its core mandate is curating an authoritative, pre-competitive living vocabulary (`taxonomy/taxonomy.json`) and an interactive CNCF-style ecosystem landscape (`landscape.yml`) to eliminate terminology silos, prevent duplicated ecosystem research, and provide an enterprise architectural blueprint[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-e6083ea5].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream enforces the "Horizontal Index" architectural principle to preserve domain sovereignty across specialized working groups:
- **Horizontal Index (In-Scope):** Consolidation, harmonization, and cross-cutting arbitration of core concepts affecting two or more working groups, published via a SKOS-Lite metadata schema (`prefLabel`, `altLabel`, `broaderTerm`, `scopeNote`, `relatedTerms`, `contrastsWith`)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-65b1abe3][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-e6083ea5].
- **Domain Payloads (Out-of-Scope):** Deep vertical whitepapers, wire protocol designs, and execution-level helper schemas remain the exclusive purview of vertical working groups such as [Security & Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-65b1abe3][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-e6083ea5].
- **Operational Scope Constraint:** Only taxonomy modifications are currently admitted; landscape contributions remain paused until an approved intake process is formally established[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-bb61ada3][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-65b1abe3].
- **Epistemological Disambiguation:** Mandates explicit counterpart differentiation for adjacent concepts (such as Tool versus Skill or Primitive versus Protocol) via `contrastsWith` and `relatedTerms`, preventing conflation into ambiguous definitions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-65b1abe3].
- **Anti-Erasure Safeguards:** Deletion or aliasing of established terms requires written concurrence from the owning working group's designated Domain Editor[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-65b1abe3].

# Governance & Operations
- **Meeting Cadence:** Weekly on Mondays at 8:30 AM PT / 11:30 AM ET / 4:30 PM BST (30 minutes)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-e6083ea5].
- **Channels:** Mailing list `ws-taxonomy-landscape@lists.aaif.io`, Discord `#ws-taxonomy-landscape`, and GitHub repository `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-e6083ea5].
- **Key Performance Indicators:** Falsifiable metrics including citation utility across AAIF specifications, corporate contribution limits (no single corporate entity exceeding 50% of merged entries), ecosystem coverage (each active WG maintaining at least 10 reviewed terms), and quarterly arbitration velocity[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-65b1abe3].

# Lifecycle History
- 2026-06-21: Workstream charter formally approved with Junjie Bu and Gala Malbasic as chairs[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-e6083ea5].
- 2026-07-27: Workstream consensus established initial flat check-in policy, deferring `category`, `broaderTerm`, and `definition` backfilling during phase-one term ingestion[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025].

mutations.rationale: Update contributor and agent operational instructions with SKOS-Lite validation rules, deferred fields policy, CI review gating, and local development setup.

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy Contribution Workflow
proposed_concept.description: Operational instructions and validation guardrails for contributing SKOS-Lite terms to the AAIF Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream repository.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy Contribution Workflow governs how autonomous agents and human contributors propose, validate, and document terminology additions within `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-65b1abe3]. The workflow enforces strict JSON data schemas, phased term-first admission criteria, pre-commit validation tests, and review-gated continuous integration pipelines[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-bb61ada3][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-c952cbc5].

# Architecture / Specification
### Schema Constraints (`taxonomy/taxonomy.json`)
Contributions must conform to the SKOS-Lite JSON schema verified by Zod validation suites[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-bb61ada3][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025]:
- `term`: Sentence-case string, globally unique across the file[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025].
- `aliases`: Array of strings for strict synonyms; use `[]` if none[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025].
- `scopeNote`: Optional context, meeting references, or cross-workgroup boundary notes[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025].
- `relatedTerms`: Array of associative `skos:related` concepts[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025].
- `contrastsWith`: Array linking explicit paired counter-concepts[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025].
- `workgroups`: Array of owning or collaborating working groups; `"Universal"` is strictly prohibited (use `[]` if universal)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025].

### Deferred Fields Protocol
Under the initial check-in consensus established on 2026-07-27, terms are admitted before final definitions are ratified[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025]:
- `definition`: Must use exact placeholder string `Definition pending — term accepted; definition under working group discussion.`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025].
- `category`: Set to empty string `""` until ontology categories are reinstated[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025].
- `broaderTerm`: Set to `null` to maintain a flat initial hierarchy pending cross-WG scope mapping[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025].

### Local Development and Validation
1. Local preview server: Run `python3 -m http.server 8000` or `npx serve -l 8000` and inspect `http://localhost:8000/taxonomy/`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-bb61ada3].
2. Dependency setup: `npm ci --ignore-scripts`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-bb61ada3].
3. Automated test execution: Run `npm run check` to validate `taxonomy/taxonomy.json` against the Zod schema and run regression tests[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-bb61ada3].

### CI Security & Review Gating
CI data validation (`validate-taxonomy.yml`) is restricted to the `pull_request_review` event (when submitted or edited by maintainers) and manual `workflow_dispatch`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-c952cbc5]. This mitigates compute-abuse vectors from unvetted push events while enforcing strict JSON validation before merging[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-c952cbc5].

mutations.rationale: Document September 2026 progress including the merging of seven taxonomy terms, the evidence-first Goose baseline pivot, and focus group initiatives.

proposed_concept.title: Observability & Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, OpenTelemetry semantic conventions, and cross-boundary execution tracing.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group defines vendor-neutral telemetry standards, execution trace models, and cross-boundary correlation protocols across agent harnesses, models, tools, and platforms. Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the working group bridges distributed tracing standards such as OpenTelemetry and W3C Trace Context with runtime agent execution dynamics[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its technical roadmap across four primary focus areas:
- **[Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md):** Specification standardizing agent continuity, retries, approvals, and effects across heterogeneous runtimes, pivoting in September 2026 to an evidence-driven reference implementation using the open-source [Goose](../resources/goose.md) agent harness[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869].
- **Cross-Boundary Observability:** Systematic telemetry propagation mapping across runtime boundaries, including local CLI subprocesses, MCP server interfaces, and agent-to-agent interactions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869].
- **LLM Primitives & Protocols:** Lower-layer protocol observability linking resource discovery, policy decisions, and tool invocation using W3C Trace Context, evidenced by lifecycle observability proposals in [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869].
- **State, Context & Reasoning:** Scoping deliverable tracks for concrete agent state-space representation, harness-independent state inference, and multi-agent topology observability[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869].

# Lifecycle History
- 2026-07: Published initial Working Methods, living Prior Work Survey, and living Use Case Inventory[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869].
- 2026-09-28: Merged seven core observability terms into the shared [Taxonomy & Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) repository: Reasoning, Agent Trajectory, Context Propagation, Context Assembly, Memory Access, Retrieval, and Traceability[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry and correlation specification standardizing OpenTelemetry semantic conventions and execution trace models across agent lifecycles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a vendor-neutral observability specification developed by the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]. It defines shared telemetry data contracts, OpenTelemetry semantic conventions, and correlation identifiers capturing autonomous agent trajectories, multi-turn tool loops, and human-in-the-loop decisions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869].

# Architecture / Specification
### Evidence-Driven Reference Methodology
Following an analysis of production coding agents and agent SDKs that revealed severe OpenTelemetry GenAI implementation inconsistencies—including conflicting span hierarchies, incompatible session attributes, outdated token usage schemas, and nonexistent approval event structures—the working group adopted an evidence-first empirical approach[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869].

The specification uses the open-source [Goose](../resources/goose.md) agent runtime as its baseline reference implementation to evaluate four foundational operational questions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]:
1. **Continuity:** Maintaining session identity, thread persistence, and agent identity across long-running, multi-turn executions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869].
2. **Calls and Retries:** Capturing deterministic tool invocations, retries, contextual failovers, and internal model recovery loops[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869].
3. **Approvals:** Formally instrumenting human-in-the-loop checkpoints, policy gate evaluations, and credential release events[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869].
4. **Effects:** Tracing observable external state changes, tool outputs, and downstream environment mutations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869].

### Implementation & Gap Analysis
Observed discrepancies between real-world agent telemetry emissions and existing OpenTelemetry conventions are cataloged in an active gap register to formulate concrete upstream extension proposals for OpenTelemetry GenAI working groups[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869].

# Lifecycle History
- 2026-09-29: Merged execution plan and shifted deliverable strategy to an empirical evidence-first approach led by Matthew Lee, establishing the Goose baseline capture setup and opening follow-on issues for shared contracts and cross-agent comparison[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e] The group develops open threat models, domain-specific taxonomy terms, architectural security patterns, and actionable implementation guidelines that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to share responsibility for trustworthy agentic AI.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e]

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Leadership
The working group is guided by chairs appointed by the Platinum and Gold members of the foundation for the term March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e]
- **Chair**: Alex Frazer (Runlayer)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e]
- **Co-Chair**: Junjie Bu (Google)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e]

Workstream deliverables merge via peer review within the repository and do not require pre-merge approval from the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), though monthly progress reports are filed with the committee.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]

## Meeting Cadence
The group operates two alternating meeting sessions so contributors across time zones can participate:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e]
- **Primary Meeting**: Biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT (USA Pacific Time).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e]
- **APAC Meeting**: Biweekly on Mondays at 9:00 PM ET (USA Eastern Time), alternating weeks with the primary session to align with Asia-Pacific working hours.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]

## Deliverables and Workstreams
The working group organizes technical output into several coordinated tracks:
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Curates reusable architectural patterns including [approval-checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md), [attested-isolated-runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md), and [kill-switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md), structured in the [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]
- **Security Best Practices**: Authors practitioner guidance in [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) and translates guidelines into static-analysis rules.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]
- **Threat Modeling**: Evaluates structural risks and threat frameworks across the agent landscape, maintained in the [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]
- **Cross-WG Reviews**: Formulates review criteria for external deliverables in the [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]
- **Taxonomy**: Directly contributes SKOS-Lite security terms to the cross-cutting [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]

# Lifecycle History
The working group held its initial orientation on February 17, 2026, and confirmed Alex Frazer as chair on March 3, 2026.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314] Its charter and initial deliverables were approved unanimously on April 14, 2026, followed by formal Technical Committee charter approval on May 26, 2026.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314] The group transitioned its GitHub repositories to public access on June 23, 2026, and initiated the alternate-week APAC meeting schedule in October 2026.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]

proposed_concept.title: Delegated-Authority Conformance Cases
proposed_concept.description: Eight-case evaluation framework assessing agent delegated authority designs against Reference Architecture invariants while mandating explicit residual disclosure.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Delegated-Authority Conformance Cases define an eight-part evaluation matrix proposed for the Identity and Trust Reference Architecture to test system designs against normative delegation, attenuation, and revocation invariants.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22] Rather than evaluating systems via a binary pass/fail checklist that rewards unstated boundaries, the framework enforces a strict residual disclosure rule requiring every evaluated architecture to explicitly declare what it knowingly leaves uncovered and which operational trade-offs it accepts.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]

# Specification

The framework maps reference invariants from the Identity and Trust Reference Architecture v1 into observable failure conditions, audit evidence requirements, and mandatory residual disclosures across eight operational cases:[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]

1. **Delegator Revoked After Downstream Delegation**: Tests that revocation of an upstream [principal](../taxonomy/principal.md) cascades to all downstream derived authority within declared time bounds, failing if an agent or subagent continues to be accepted.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]
2. **Valid Delegation, Wrong Object or Action**: Evaluates enforcement of grant constraints (actions, counterparties, limits, validity) at the time of use (§3.5.1), failing if a grant valid for one target is accepted for another or replayed.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]
3. **Acting on Stale Revocation Information**: Assesses whether relying parties establish grant status from verifiable evidence at the time of use rather than self-reported assertions, failing if decisions rely on status data exceeding max age bounds.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]
4. **Escalation Authority Unavailable**: Verifies fail-closed behavior during approval timeouts or approver absence, proving that authority never widens when an escalation authority is unavailable.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]
5. **Amplification Across Multi-Hop Delegation Chains**: Enforces strict attenuation (§3.5.3), requiring proof that each delegation hop only narrows constraints and never expands authority in scope or number.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]
6. **Identity Valid, Authority Expired**: Proves independent lifecycle checking between identity credentials and delegated authority grants, preventing valid identity tokens from executing expired or revoked grants.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]
7. **Delegation Chain Surveillance Graph**: Measures privacy protections ensuring relying parties verify that an accountable principal exists without learning the intermediate delegation chain graph or sibling agent identities.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]
8. **Wrongful or Disputed Revocation**: Audits tamper-evident revocation recording (§3.6) and declared contestation or re-issuance remedies, documenting whether derived grants survive or reverse following a dispute.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-10**: Proposed by Sparsh Agarwal in [WG Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) as an appendix to Reference Architecture v1 following discussion of MintID, Proofable, and Alakris reference implementations.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining vendor-neutral standards, delegation frameworks, and verification taxonomies for agent identity and authorization.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Identity and Trust Working Group is an AAIF technical body establishing vendor-neutral standards, delegation architectures, and verification criteria for autonomous agents, human principals, and interacting services.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22] Its work addresses foundational security primitives, including cryptographic agent identity, multi-hop delegation chains, time-of-use verification, and cascading credential revocation across organizational trust boundaries.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group's Reference Architecture v1 standardizes core operational rules governing agentic authority:[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]

- **Time-of-Use Verification**: Mandatory validation of five essential grant elements at the moment of execution rather than relying on self-reported agent assertions.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]
- **Separation of Chains**: Structural separation between delegation chains (authorizing specific capabilities) and accountability chains (resolving liability to a verifiable [principal](../taxonomy/principal.md)).[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]
- **Hop Attenuation**: Monotonic narrowing of permissions across multi-hop delegation paths, preventing authority amplification.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]
- **Cascading Revocation**: Time-bounded propagation of revocation events from root authorities through all derived downstream grants.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]
- **Privacy-Preserving Accountability**: Relying-party verification that an accountable principal exists at a designated assurance level without exposing the intermediate delegation topology.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]

To validate implementations against these invariants, the working group is developing [Delegated-Authority Conformance Cases](../guidelines/delegated-authority-conformance-cases.md) mandating explicit residual disclosure for unaddressed edge cases.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-10-21**: Published Identity and Trust Reference Architecture v1 establishing normative delegation and revocation invariants.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]
- **2026-10-31**: Advanced eight delegated-authority conformance evaluation cases with residual disclosure requirements for addition as an architectural appendix.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]

# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an AAIF technical body developing vendor-neutral threat models, architectural security patterns, and operational best practices for agentic AI deployments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43] The working group establishes runtime boundary controls, cross-working-group review criteria, and defensive design patterns addressing agent-specific vulnerabilities such as privilege escalation, context poisoning, and unauthorized tool execution.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group coordinates several foundational security workstreams across the foundation:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43]

- **Best Practices Guide**: A living operational manual detailing runtime hook enforcement, credential boundaries, and network gating; opened to external community contributions in October 2026 under designated maintainer reviews.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43]
- **Agentic Threat Modeling**: An analytical framework synthesizing STRIDE and PASTA methodologies with MITRE ATLAS and OWASP Artificial Security Intelligence (ASI) matrices to classify agent failure modes.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43]
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: A library of reusable architectural controls, including the [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) pattern and containment mechanisms for credential revocation protocols.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43]
- **Cross-WG Security Review Checklist**: Review workflows aligning observability, [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md), and governance workstreams against unified baseline controls.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-10-26**: Merged core security and privacy vocabulary into the foundation-wide cross-WG taxonomy.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43]
- **2026-10-27**: Reviewed kill switch credential revocation protocol mappings within the design patterns track.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43]
- **2026-10**: Launched an alternate-week APAC meeting track on Mondays at 9 pm Eastern to support distributed global community participation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43]

proposed_concept.description: Classification schema defining structural workflow dimensions and evidentiary standards for cataloging production agent deployments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Use Case Classification Schema establishes a structured categorization framework for analyzing real-world agent deployments within the [Agentic Use Case Inventory](../resources/agentic-use-case-inventory.md).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-59] Maintained by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), the schema provides dimensional metadata to classify autonomy bounds, orchestration topologies, and human-in-the-loop oversight mechanisms.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-58]

# Specification

The classification schema structures each documented production use case across key organizational and technical dimensions:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-58][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-59]

- **Workflow Topology and Shape**: Categorizes execution structures (e.g., single-agent loops, parallel fan-out, hierarchical delegation); actively proposed to transition nomenclature from "Workflow Pattern" to "Workflow Shape" to avoid conflation with foundational Reference Architecture patterns and primitives.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-58]
- **HITL Oversight**: Defines interaction boundaries and approval checkpoints; actively proposed to transition from "HITL Pattern" to "HITL Shape".[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-58]
- **Evidentiary Citation Standard**: Mandates that every cataloged deployment cite verifiable, publicly accessible primary sources (vendor announcements or production case studies) with publication or retrieval dates.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-59]
- **Link Hygiene and Rot Remediation**: Implements automated link extraction and validation workflows to monitor citation status (200, redirect, 404, or blocked) and flag stale evidence without corrupting evidentiary compliance.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-59]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-10**: Issue #58 proposed renaming schema pattern dimensions to "shapes" to disambiguate use case metadata from reference architecture patterns.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-58]
- **2026-10**: Issue #59 initiated scheduled CI automation to extract and verify external citation links against link rot.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-59]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an AAIF technical body standardizing telemetry, distributed tracing, and audit instrumentation across autonomous agent runtimes, tool boundaries, and multi-agent protocols.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-21c321e2] Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group develops vendor-neutral semantic conventions, protocol boundary tracing models, and correlation mechanisms connecting language model execution spans with infrastructure events.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-21c321e2]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group focuses on core areas of agentic observability:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-21c321e2]

- **Semantic Conventions**: Extending [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) standards for agent execution lifecycles, memory retrieval spans, tool invocation boundaries, and model evaluations.
- **Protocol Boundaries**: Analyzing telemetry propagation across Model Context Protocol ([Agent MCP Server Boundary](../resources/agent-mcp-server-boundary.md)) and subprocess execution layers ([Agent Tool CLI Boundary](../resources/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md)).
- **Technical Committee Reporting**: Adhering to standardized monthly reporting templates capturing progress against objectives, blockers, and required decisions for asynchronous governance review.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-21c321e2]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-10**: Codified standardized monthly reporting template and governance workflows under co-chairs Pavan Sudheendra and Matthew Lee.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-21c321e2]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Create Chapter Skill
proposed_concept.description: Automated provisioning and maintenance skill managing chapter Google Drive assets, OOXML rebranding, map dot repositioning, and four-surface chapter renaming.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-create-chapter` skill is an automated operational pipeline for provisioning and maintaining AAIF city chapters within the Foundation's Google Drive estate[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a]. The skill orchestrates the cloning of the canonical `TemplateCity` directory into new regional chapters, executing surgical token replacement across Office Open XML (OOXML) documents, attendee spreadsheets, presentation decks, and folder structures while safeguarding template placeholders for downstream event execution skills[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a]. It is paired with the `rename_chapter.py` utility to perform comprehensive, four-surface in-place renames across Drive folder identifiers, file paths, document metadata, and archive content parts[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].

Operational dependencies and environment verification are coordinated via [aaif-check-setup](../skills/aaif-check-setup.md), while ongoing estate reconciliation is managed through [aaif-sync](../skills/aaif-sync.md) and [community-event-operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md).

# Architecture / Specification

## Tooling Rules and Execution Constraints

The provisioning and rebranding runtime operates under strict execution constraints[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a]:

- **CLI Mediation**: All reads, copies, exports, and writes against Google Drive must route through the authenticated `gws` CLI driven by Python[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].
- **Native Format Preference**: Native Google Workspace types (`application/vnd.google-apps.*`) are manipulated directly via Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides APIs[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a]. Byte-level OOXML zip surgery is permitted only on stored binary `.docx`, `.pptx`, and `.xlsx` artifacts to preserve embedded fonts and untouched package parts[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].
- **Prohibition of Desktop Office Suites**: The use of headless desktop office suites (including LibreOffice, `soffice`, or `unoconv`) is strictly prohibited for edits, conversions, and local visual previews[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a]. These suites substitute local system typefaces for brand fonts and silently drop unhandled OOXML elements, corrupting output files[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].
- **API-Driven Previews**: Previews must be generated via API rendering endpoints (e.g., slide PNG generation via `aaif_events.slides_export` or PDF exports through Drive) rather than local rendering engines[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].

## Rebranding and Token Substitution Rules

Cloning a chapter from `TemplateCity` replaces city identity tokens while isolating operational event content[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a]:

- **City Names**: `San Francisco` and `SAN FRANCISCO` are transformed into the target city name using case-matched substitution across document bodies and file/folder names[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].
- **Abbreviation Expansion**: The `SF` abbreviation (such as `AAIF · SF`, `SF CHAPTER`, or document properties) expands to the full city name in Title Case or uppercase as context dictates[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].
- **Luma Slugs**: Target slugs (`aaif-<slug>`) are updated across hyperlinks and references, following slug-normalization conventions[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].
- **Content Preservation**: Specific event metadata—such as calendar dates, placeholder speaker names (e.g., "Maya Chen"), agendas, and venue neighborhood placeholders—represent template content that must not be altered during chapter provisioning[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].
- **Network Map Dot Repositioning**: On slide 5 ("THE NETWORK") of `Event Template/Slides.pptx`, the green "you-are-here" dot and its `<CITY> · TONIGHT` label are repositioned from the San Francisco baseline to the target city's real geographic coordinates using explicit `--lat`/`--lon` arguments or Nominatim geocoding[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].

## Four-Surface Renaming Architecture

Renaming an existing chapter is executed through `rename_chapter.py` across four distinct surfaces to avoid partial migration drift[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c]:

1. **Root Folder Identity**: Renames the top-level Drive chapter folder[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].
2. **File and Subfolder Paths**: Updates all member file and nested folder names (e.g., `[City] CRM.xlsx`)[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].
3. **OOXML Text Streams**: Mutates document body XML parts inside `.docx`, `.pptx`, and `.xlsx` archives[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].
4. **Document Metadata**: Updates package metadata properties in `docProps` parts[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].

To preserve external routing and archive integrity during renames:
- **Luma Slug Isolation**: Luma slugs are never renamed automatically during a city rename unless explicitly requested with `--slug-from` and `--slug-to`, preventing broken external URLs (HTTP 404) when a chapter retains its legacy event URL[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].
- **Relationship Integrity**: Package relationship files (`.rels`) receive slug replacements only and are excluded from generic city-name substitution to avoid creating dangling relationship targets that corrupt the document package[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].
- **Safety Controls**: The tool generates pre-mutation backups under `backups/rename-<UTC>/`, previews every targeted string before execution, and executes a full re-read verification pass across Drive files upon completion[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].

# Lifecycle History

- **Prompt Modernization**: Legacy Word-based prompt files (`SKILLS.md.docx`) were retired and converted into structured, executable repository skills[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].
- **Map Geolocation**: Dynamic coordinate calculation and label repositioning on slide 5 of `Slides.pptx` was introduced to fix an issue where rebranded chapters left the locator dot positioned at San Francisco[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].
- **Four-Surface Migration Framework**: Following the 2026-08 capital-city migrations where folder-only renames caused metadata and document body mismatches, the unified `rename_chapter.py` script was formalized with pre-write diff previews and `.rels` boundary guards[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Create Chapter Skill
proposed_concept.description: Automated provisioning skill managing chapter Google Drive asset hierarchies, OOXML presentation rebranding, and web banner rendering.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Create Chapter skill automates the provisioning, asset rebranding, and Drive estate configuration for regional AAIF community chapters. It creates isolated chapter directory hierarchies, copies required presentation and governance templates, and executes text and branding transformations across templates to prepare chapters for local organizers.[^evt-community-events-pr-65]

# Architecture / Specification

Chapter provisioning orchestrates several sequential transformation stages:

- **Drive Hierarchy Provisioning**: Duplicates chapter workspace templates into target regional directories, provisioning folder trees for banners, decks, and operating documentation.
- **OOXML Rebranding**: Modifies OpenXML presentation payloads directly to substitute template naming tokens with authorized chapter titles.
- **Web Banner Rendering**: Rather than copying static template PNG assets—which historically produced city name mismatches across chapter directories—the workflow renders `Web Banner.png` directly from the fourth slide of `Banners/Square Logo.pptx` using `render_web_banner.py` and Google Slides export APIs.[^evt-community-events-pr-65]
- **Verification Guards**: Asserts that rendered slide text strictly contains "AAIF Community Events" concatenated with the chapter name.[^evt-community-events-pr-65] Generated banners are stamped with the source presentation's `md5Checksum` and chapter name within Drive `appProperties` to ensure idempotency and permit safe re-runs without duplicate exports.[^evt-community-events-pr-65]
- **Error Handlers**: A failed banner render exits with code 2 during creation and halts dirty resumes, while temporary Slides export copies that fail trashing cleanly trigger operational errors.[^evt-community-events-pr-65]

# Lifecycle History

Originally, chapter generation duplicated `Web Banner.png` byte-for-byte from TemplateCity, causing at least 37 chapters to retain default template imagery.[^evt-community-events-pr-65] PR #65 introduced dynamic rendering from slide templates and automated verification stamps across all active chapter estates.[^evt-community-events-pr-65]

- [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md)
- [AAIF Check Setup](../skills/aaif-check-setup.md)

proposed_concept.description: Read-only diagnostic skill validating runtime readiness, API connection tokens, and credential precedence for community operations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Check Setup skill (`aaif-check-setup`) is a zero-dependency, read-only diagnostic utility that validates runtime environment readiness, client token configuration, and tool access for community event operators.[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7] Designed for non-technical operators running automated skills via [Goose](../resources/goose.md) or Claude Desktop, it audits prerequisites and provides plain-text remediation paths without assuming real-time assistance from an administrative helper.[^evt-community-events-pr-66][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9]

# Architecture / Specification

The diagnostic engine runs strictly on standard library Python so it can execute out of packaged zip archives and standalone plugin installations without virtual environments.[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7]

### Operational Verifications

The tool evaluates system and operational prerequisites across several critical services:[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7]
- **Python Runtime & Plugin Health**: Validates runtime installation integrity and execution path invariants.
- **Google Workspace (`gws`) Access**: Inspects local Google connection configuration files and intake spreadsheet edit permissions, reporting missing connection files directly rather than triggering interactive sign-in paths that cannot succeed in headless harness environments.[^evt-community-events-pr-66]
- **Communication & Event APIs**: Validates Slack user/bot tokens and Luma API access.
- **Browser Automation**: Confirms local Google Chrome availability.

### Credential Precedence Audit

The skill mirrors and verifies the canonical secret resolution order used across community event tools:[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9]
1. Active shell environment variables
2. Repository-root `.env` file
3. macOS Keychain (`aaif-slack-read-token`, `aaif-slack-write-token`, and `luma-api-key`)

Because installed plugins lack direct shell environments and updates overwrite repo-level `.env` files, Keychain Access is recommended as the primary durable mechanism for desktop operators.[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7]

# Lifecycle History

Setup documentation was separated into first-time administrator steps (Slack app manifests, Google client provisioning) and subsequent operator onboarding.[^evt-community-events-pr-66] PR #66 removed historical assumptions of interactive sign-in helpers and aligned `aaif-check-setup` with file-based connection transfers and keychain secrets.[^evt-community-events-pr-66]

# References

- [Goose](../resources/goose.md)
- [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md)
- [AAIF Create Chapter](../skills/aaif-create-chapter.md)

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Check Setup
proposed_concept.description: Read-only diagnostic skill validating runtime readiness, API connection tokens, and per-operator credential configuration across Google Workspace, Slack, and Luma.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-check-setup` is a read-only diagnostic skill within the AAIF Community Events Toolkit that verifies local machine readiness before executing administrative operations.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451] It inspects local Python dependencies, Google Workspace authentication via the `gws` command-line tool, edit permissions on the Community Intake sheet, user-scoped Slack tokens, and Luma calendar API keys.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451] It explains configuration gaps and actionable remediation steps in plain language without exposing private keys or credentials.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451]

# Architecture / Specification

## Diagnostic Scope and Checks
The diagnostic runner executes `python3 <skill-root>/scripts/check_setup.py` as a non-destructive probe.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451] The script performs read-only validations:
- **Google Workspace (`gws` CLI):** Verifies CLI installation, Google OAuth login state, and Drive edit access against Google Sheets metadata without modifying any resources.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451]
- **Slack:** Invokes `auth.test` against the Slack API using an operator's individual user token (`xoxp-`).[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451][^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-8ce1fa27]
- **Luma:** Validates calendar access permissions by calling the `calendars/get` endpoint.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451]
- **System Binaries:** Verifies availability of Python 3 and Google Chrome (required for headless PDF report rendering).[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451]

Exit code `0` signals that all required subsystems are functional, while exit code `1` denotes one or more blocking failures.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451] Text generation and copywriting tasks (e.g., drafting announcements or speaker bios) operate independently and do not require external credentials to function.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451][^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-23a10754]

## Tooling Invariants and File Handling
The skill enforces strict tooling conventions for asset interaction:[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451]
1. **API-Driven Google Formats:** Native Google files (`application/vnd.google-apps.*`) must be inspected and edited exclusively via the `gws` CLI driven by Python through native Docs, Sheets, and Slides APIs.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451]
2. **Byte-Level OOXML Surgery:** Stored Office files (`.docx`, `.pptx`, `.xlsx`) are manipulated via zip-part byte-level editing to preserve embedded fonts and metadata.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451]
3. **Ban on Desktop Office Suites:** Desktop converters and headless suites such as LibreOffice (`soffice`) and `unoconv` are strictly prohibited due to local font substitution and corruption of unrecognized OOXML namespaces.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451] Visual previews must be rendered via API endpoints or PDF export pipelines.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451]

## Credential Isolation Model
AAIF community event tooling mandates per-operator credential creation rather than shared credentials:[^evt-community-events-pr-67]
- **Google OAuth Isolation:** Each operator provisions an independent Google connection configuration because internal OAuth clients cannot authenticate cross-organization accounts.[^evt-community-events-pr-67]
- **Slack User Tokens:** Operators generate dedicated user tokens (`xoxp-`) from an installed Slack application manifest rather than using shared bot tokens or shared operator tokens.[^evt-community-events-pr-67][^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-8ce1fa27] Because user tokens inherit the caller's privileges (including direct message search via `search:read` and impersonated posting via `chat:write`), sharing tokens creates critical security and privacy boundary violations.[^evt-community-events-pr-67][^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-8ce1fa27]
- **Keychain Hygiene:** On macOS, mismatched or corrupted keys require purging `gws-cli` entries from Keychain Access and logging out before reauthenticating with explicit scopes.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451]

# References
- Portable Agent Skill packaging rules: [Agent Skills specification](../standards/agent-skills.md)[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-8ce1fa27]
- Operational pipeline: [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md)[^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-23a10754]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body convening practitioners, platform vendors, and standards organizations to standardize agent observability signals, execution traces, and telemetry conventions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d] The working group focuses on the intersection of agent reasoning, state transitions, and tool interactions with standard distributed tracing frameworks, emphasizing vendor-neutral interoperability across heterogeneous agent runtimes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d]

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Leadership
The working group operates under technical foundation governance with leadership appointed by Platinum and Gold members:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d]
- **Chair:** Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d]
- **Co-Chair:** Matthew Lee (Datadog)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d]
- **Term of Office:** March 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d]
- **Meeting Cadence:** Biweekly on Wednesdays at 10:00 AM Pacific Time.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d]

GitHub issues and pull requests serve as the primary source of record for durable status and consensus tracking, supported by recorded meetings and public mailing list archives.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d]

## Core Deliverables and Workstreams
The working group maintains several foundational assets:
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model (ABTM):** A structured execution plan and vendor-neutral specification establishing semantic conventions for agent execution graphs, turns, and step spans.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f5077fe55915-f29d3cf9]
- **Prior Work Survey:** A living comparative survey evaluating current agent observability specifications, APM tools, and distributed tracing protocols.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d]
- **Observability Use Cases Inventory:** A practitioner-focused catalog documenting requirements across agent debugging, cost attribution, and behavioral compliance.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d]

## Liaison and Coordination Network
The working group maintains an active liaison roster tracking bidirectional coordination across industry standards and internal AAIF groups:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f5077fe55915-f29d3cf9]
- **External Standards:** Primary liaison with the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG (advancing turn and step span proposals), Agent Trace (Cursor), AGNTCY, libp2p, HOL, and Agent Action Capsule.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f5077fe55915-f29d3cf9]
- **Foundation Workstreams:** Active collaboration with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) (aligning terminology such as Turn and Agent Step), the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) (capturing agent evaluation telemetry), and the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f5077fe55915-f29d3cf9]
- **Platform Reference Proving Grounds:** Coordination with AAIF implementation efforts including Goose, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f5077fe55915-f29d3cf9]

# References
- Specification work: [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d]
- Ecosystem analysis: [Agent Observability Prior Work](../resources/agent-observability-prior-work.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d]
- Requirements mapping: [Agent Observability Use Cases](../resources/agent-observability-use-cases.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d]
