proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Process with Human Approval
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture enforcing an immutable human approval gate between an agent proposal and external execution to ensure non-probabilistic authorization at the point of effect.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Single-Agent Process with Human Approval reference architecture establishes an enforceable structural break between a probabilistic agent's proposal and a protected external effect[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-2fb150b7]. In this architecture, an agent investigates, calculates, and constructs an action proposal, but lacks the credentials and capabilities to invoke the protected effect directly. A named human reviewer evaluates the immutable proposal, and a dedicated, workflow-controlled executor executes the action only after recording explicit human authorization[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-2fb150b7].

This architecture was unanimously approved as the Workflows & Process Integration Working Group's second voted deliverable at its September 17, 2026 plenary session[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e].

# Architecture / Specification
The reference architecture addresses jobs where an agent's output can alter real systems (such as issuing refunds, executing configuration changes, or sending outbound communications) and requires strict attribution of authority, risk bounding, or auditability[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-2fb150b7].

### Composition of Patterns
The architecture is composed from three core workflow patterns:
- [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md): Enforces that intent generation, approval, and execution belong to separate roles[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-2fb150b7].
- [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md): Intercepts the workflow, requiring explicit authentication and approval from an authorized human before proceeding[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-2fb150b7].
- [Durable Wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md): Ensures the workflow state is durably persisted so that multi-hour or multi-day waits for human authorization survive process restarts, deployments, and crashes without losing state or repeating completed steps[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-2fb150b7].

### Core Invariants
Implementations of this architecture guarantee:
1. **Strict Authority Separation**: The executor capability and credentials that cause the protected effect are inaccessible to the agent. Separation of authority is mandatory even if the executor shares a host process with the agent[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-2fb150b7].
2. **Immutable Authorization**: The executor executes precisely what the human authorized without revisions, re-evaluations, or model-driven modifications[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-2fb150b7].
3. **Complete Attribution Chain**: Every workflow run terminates in an explicit, known terminal state, recording the complete intent-to-decision-to-effect chain (proposer, approver, and executor) in an immutable system of record[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-2fb150b7].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-09-17**: Voted unanimously and merged on main by the Workflows & Process Integration Working Group plenary[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e].
- **2026-10-02**: Terminology follow-up (PR #50) merged, adopting "activity" for workflow subunits and "business task" for business-level work requests[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e].

proposed_concept.title: Proposal/Execution Split
proposed_concept.description: Architectural governance pattern separating probabilistic agent intent generation, policy or human authorization, and workflow-controlled execution into distinct, auditable roles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Proposal/Execution Split is an architectural governance pattern that enforces authorization and attribution boundaries when intent originates from a probabilistic AI agent[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2]. Probabilistic models cannot provide non-repudiable audit guarantees or hold organizational accountability. The pattern enforces a fundamental precept: intent, authorization, and execution belong to distinct roles, each recorded separately in the system of record[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2].

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern divides the execution pipeline into three strictly separated roles:
1. **Proposer (Agent)**: Generates an immutable proposal containing structured intent data, but lacks capability or authorization to execute real-world actions[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2].
2. **Authorization Authority**: An explicit human principal or deterministic policy engine that evaluates the exact proposal payload and emits an authorization decision[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2].
3. **Executor (System)**: A workflow-controlled, non-probabilistic component holding the credentials required to invoke the external protected effect, acting only upon receiving valid authorization evidence[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2].

### Invariants
Any compliant implementation must maintain the following invariants:
- **Proposals are data, not actions**: The artifact crossing from the proposer to the gate is inert state[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2].
- **Fail-closed authorization**: An absent, expired, or invalid authorization decision routes strictly to terminal or recovery pathways; permission is never inferred by default[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2].
- **Exact payload binding**: The executor only executes the exact payload authorized by the authority; any modification invalidates authorization[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2].
- **Separate audit attribution**: Proposer identity, authorization decision evidence, and execution outcomes must be logged as distinct records in the audit trail[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2].

### Related Architectures and Patterns
This pattern serves as a foundational building block for:
- [Single-Agent Process with Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2]
- [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2]
- [Human Approval Gate](human-approval-gate.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2]
- [Durable Wait](durable-wait.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2]

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture governing iterative, autonomous problem resolution within predefined task bounds, deterministic verification gates, and fail-safe escalation paths.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Bounded Autonomous Remediation is a reference architecture designed to autonomously resolve discrete, well-bounded problems without requiring per-attempt human intervention[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-d009744e]. It serves as a contrasting companion to the [Single-Agent Process with Human Approval](single-agent-human-approval.md): while it permits autonomous model iterations, it prevents unbounded autonomy and uncontrolled effects by enforcing explicit task boundaries, isolated work areas, independent deterministic acceptance gates, and fail-safe escalation paths[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-d009744e].

# Architecture / Specification
The architecture applies to business tasks where scope, tools, budgets, and measurable acceptance criteria can be declared in advance, and the resulting external effect is constrained and low-impact or reversible (e.g., opening a remediation pull request or generating reconciliation batches)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-d009744e].

### Composition of Patterns
The architecture composes three core patterns:
- [Bounded Convergence Loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md): Limits agent retries and token/time budgets to prevent runaway execution loops[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-d009744e].
- [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md): Employs independent programmatic checks (unit tests, schema validators, lint rules) rather than agent self-evaluation to judge candidate outputs[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-d009744e].
- [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md): Isolates the candidate result from the external executor, preventing direct write actions by the agent[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-d009744e].

### Qualification Checklist
To determine if an operational problem fits this architecture, five conditions must be satisfied:
1. **Pre-declared Problem Bounds**: The task contract, allowed scope, permitted tools/data, and acceptance conditions must be established prior to execution[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-d009744e].
2. **Independent Deterministic Evaluation**: Objective tests, schemas, or reconciliation rules evaluate candidate outputs without relying on model self-judgment[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-d009744e].
3. **Constrained External Effect**: Permitted real-world actions are strictly limited and ideally reversible[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-d009744e].
4. **Fenced Agent Environment**: The agent operates inside an isolated workspace with least-privilege credentials and strict resource limits[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-d009744e].
5. **Safe Non-Convergence Route**: Budget exhaustion, validation errors, or out-of-scope conditions cleanly halt execution and escalate to human operators[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-d009744e].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08-29**: Architecture PR #26 merged on main[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e].
- **2026-09-15**: Validation record (PR #37) merged on main[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e].
- **2026-09-30**: PR #43 (minimum evidence rules based on blast radius and reversibility) and PR #49 (terminology cleanup) remain in active review prior to plenary vote scheduling[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Observability Use Cases Catalog
proposed_concept.description: Living catalog categorizing agent observability requirements across debugging, cost, attribution, evaluation, safety, compliance, and multi-agent coordination.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Observability Use Cases Catalog is a living reference document authored by the AAIF Observability Working Group that establishes a comprehensive taxonomy of practitioner requirements for visibility into agent behavior[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-fb30ebcb]. The catalog details what data observability layers must capture across heterogeneous operational environments, evaluates gaps in existing specifications and platforms, and articulates cross-cutting requirements for trustworthy telemetry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-fb30ebcb].

# Architecture / Specification
Each use case entry defines practitioner needs, target audiences, required telemetry payloads, and current tooling gaps across nine core functional categories[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-fb30ebcb]:
- **Category A: Debugging and Root Cause Analysis**: Diagnosing unexpected decisions, identifying execution bottlenecks or retry loops, and reproducing agent execution histories[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-fb30ebcb].
- **Category B: Cost Management and Optimization**: Measuring token expenditures per session, calculating cost per successful outcome, and eliminating operational waste[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-fb30ebcb].
- **Category C: Code Attribution and Provenance**: Tracking line-level AI-generated code, attribution tracing, and security reviewing automated diffs[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-fb30ebcb].
- **Category D: Evaluation and Quality Assurance**: Task-level performance benchmarking, automated regression detection, and cross-model comparative scoring[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-fb30ebcb].
- **Category E: Safety and Compliance**: Tracking world-altering side effects, verifying authorization scopes, maintaining regulated audit trails, and generating tamper-evident records for dispute resolution[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-fb30ebcb].
- **Category F: Multi-Agent Systems**: Distributed trace propagation across agent boundaries and auditing agent-to-agent negotiation protocols[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-fb30ebcb].
- **Category G: Operational Monitoring**: Real-time agent health metrics, error rates, and fleet capacity planning[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-fb30ebcb].
- **Category H: Research and Improvement**: Uncovering novel failure modes, harvesting fine-tuning datasets, and cross-implementation benchmarking[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-fb30ebcb].
- **Category I: Identity and Ownership**: Resolving agent and principal identities across heterogeneous operational surfaces[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-fb30ebcb].

### Cross-Cutting Telemetry Requirements
The specification defines five non-functional requirements that apply across all cataloged use cases:
1. **Source and Trust**: Telemetry must explicitly distinguish agent self-reporting from external vantage points (frameworks, gateways, sandboxes, operating systems) and denote cryptographic signing or tamper-evidence metadata without presuming completeness[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-fb30ebcb].
2. **Privacy and Governance**: Fields must incorporate policy tags for data minimization, tenant residency, retention, and redaction; raw credentials and secrets must never be collected[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-fb30ebcb].
3. **Completeness and Sampling**: Telemetry records must indicate sampling decisions and collection gaps, differentiating discardable telemetry from audit-mandated records[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-fb30ebcb].
4. **Schema Evolution**: Events must declare schema, model, tool, and harness versions to ensure long-term interpretability[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-fb30ebcb].
5. **Correlation and Causality**: Systems must track stable identifiers and causal graph links across asynchronous, queued, and distributed agent sessions rather than relying solely on wall-clock time or strict parent-child span trees[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-fb30ebcb].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Sync
proposed_concept.description: Procedural operations pipeline orchestrating community estate reconciliation, safe chapter retirement, drift reporting, and organizer invitation workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-sync` skill automates the reconciliation of community operational assets across GitHub, Google Drive, Luma, Slack, and CRM systems[^evt-community-events-pr-68]. It checks intake records against active infrastructure, generates deterministic drift reports, flags inconsistencies, and selectively writes back verified state updates to maintain synchronized community operations[^evt-community-events-pr-68].

# Architecture / Specification
The pipeline is orchestrated primarily via `sync.py` along with specialized submodules including `invite_organizers.py`, `sync_crm.py`, and `resolve_slack_ids.py`[^evt-community-events-pr-68].

### Reconciliation and Drift Classification
To prevent reporting pending changes as fully synchronized, the sync workflow evaluates run findings into distinct operational statuses:
- **DRIFT**: Assigned when clean execution (exit code 0) yields actionable findings prefixed with `apply with --write` or `re-run --write`, denoting unapplied pending changes[^evt-community-events-pr-68].
- **NEEDS REVIEW**: Assigned when open findings require manual human intervention or adjudication, leaving exit codes intact[^evt-community-events-pr-68].
- **WROTE**: Denotes successful application of updates during a write-enabled execution[^evt-community-events-pr-68].
- **PARTIAL**: Dominant terminal state assigned if any sub-operation fails or halts mid-run[^evt-community-events-pr-68].

### Identity Resolution and Invite Safety
The invitation workflow (`invite_organizers.py`) applies strict safeguards to prevent duplicate or invalid invitations:
- **Account Disambiguation and Holds**: Individuals associated with multiple active Slack accounts or conflicting reviewed intake rows are automatically held; held organizers are recorded in the execution log and excluded from automated invitations[^evt-community-events-pr-68].
- **Stale Identifier Pruning**: Column IDs corresponding to deactivated accounts yield to confirmed live accounts[^evt-community-events-pr-68].
- **Identity Suggestions**: Identity resolution runs with `--suggest` by default, ensuring candidate name and email matches are proposed for review and never written automatically[^evt-community-events-pr-68].

proposed_concept.title: Deterministic Acceptance Gate
proposed_concept.description: Architectural pattern evaluating candidate agent outputs against explicit, repeatable checks and scope rules rather than model self-assessment.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

A Deterministic Acceptance Gate evaluates candidate results using explicit, repeatable checks rather than relying on model self-assessment [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677]. In agent-assisted workflows, models that evaluate their own output are prone to confident but invalid self-certification [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677]. The gate validates candidates against pre-declared criteria—such as unit tests, schema validators, policy rules, and contract suites—alongside task scope constraints before granting workflow progression [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677].

Passing a deterministic gate serves as evidence that a declared acceptance condition was met, not as a general guarantee that the result is globally correct [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677]. The pattern is frequently paired with the [Bounded Convergence Loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md), [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md), and [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md) reference architecture [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677].

# Architecture / Specification

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    I["Candidate result + declared scope"] --> G["Run explicit checks and validate policy"]
    G -->|"accepted and scope-valid"| E["Record acceptance evidence"]
    G -->|"not accepted or insufficient evidence"| W["Return gate result to workflow control"]
```

The candidate result and declared scope are submitted to the gate, which executes deterministic checks and validates policy rules [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677]. Scope validation checks target boundaries (systems, databases, or files), permitted change classes, data access permissions, allowed tool invocations, and external side effects [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677].

Control flow is decoupled from gate evaluation: the gate reports acceptance or non-acceptance with cryptographic or digest-bound evidence, while the enclosing workflow orchestrates downstream retries, escalations, or terminations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677].

### Invariants

- **Pre-declared criteria:** Acceptance criteria must be declared prior to candidate evaluation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677].
- **Independent evaluation:** The gate must run independently of the generative model or agent that produced the candidate result [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677].
- **Candidate digest binding:** Acceptance evidence must bind cryptographically or uniquely to the exact evaluated version or digest [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677].
- **Mandatory scope conjunction:** A result cannot pass if technical checks succeed but policy or scope checks fail [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677].
- **Fail-closed:** Ambiguous, unexecuted, or failing checks must default to non-acceptance [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677].
- **Auditability:** The workflow engine must log inputs, evaluation results, and control decisions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677].
- **Authority limits:** Gate authority is strictly bounded to its declared contract; downstream effects require explicit authorization controls [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677].

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Convergence Loop
proposed_concept.description: Architectural pattern safely iterating an agent-driven task within explicit budget limits until a deterministic gate passes or defined termination triggers.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Bounded Convergence Loop governs iterative agent remediation tasks—such as dependency updates, lint corrections, or documentation fixes—where solutions require repeated attempts [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8]. The pattern provides the benefits of iterative execution without permitting unbounded retries, open-ended objectives, or self-declared completion [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8].

Every candidate iteration must be assessed by an independent [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8]. The pattern is used directly within the [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md) reference architecture and interfaces with the [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) and [Durable Wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md) patterns [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8].

# Architecture / Specification

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Admit bounded business task"] --> B["Agent attempts permitted work"]
    B --> G["Deterministic gate evaluates result"]
    G -->|"accepted"| E["Exit to controlled effect"]
    G -->|"not accepted"| C{"Configured retry criteria permit?"}
    C -->|"yes"| B
    C -->|"no"| S["Escalate, stop, or fail"]
```

The workflow admits an explicitly defined task, restricts agent capabilities to the declared scope, and subjects every output to a deterministic gate [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8]. If non-accepted, retries are evaluated against preconfigured constraints including maximum iteration counters, execution deadlines, and cost allocations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8].

### Invariants

- **Pre-execution constraints:** Task scope, tool access boundaries, and acceptance criteria must be declared before the loop initiates [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8].
- **External evaluation:** The agent cannot certify its own completion; an external deterministic gate evaluates all candidate results [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8].
- **Explicit budgets:** Each retry loop requires an explicit iteration cap and at least one time or token/monetary budget limit [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8].
- **State persistence:** The workflow logs the attempt counter, gate verdicts, and termination reasons, resuming from recorded checkpoints rather than resetting budgets upon restart [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8].
- **Fail-bounded:** Failed gates terminate strictly in bounded retries, escalations, human intervention, or recorded failure [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8].
- **Scope enforcement:** Output passing technical checks but violating scope cannot proceed to side-effect execution [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8].

proposed_concept.title: Zeko
proposed_concept.description: Open-source agentic rollup protocol providing verifiable shared state, fast local confirmation, and zero-knowledge proof aggregation across agent applications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Zeko is an open-source agentic rollup protocol designed to maintain verifiable shared state across distributed AI agent applications [^evt-project-proposals-issue-68]. Submitted as an AAIF Sandbox proposal, Zeko provides instant transaction confirmation at the rollup tier, enabling autonomous agents to coordinate against accepted state without waiting for base-layer blockchain finality [^evt-project-proposals-issue-68]. Systems leverage this shared state for task commitments, resource reservations, cross-agent accounting, and conditional machine payments [^evt-project-proposals-issue-68].

Originating from Mina cryptography and ZK smart contracts, Zeko also supports an Ethereum settlement architecture via SP1 zero-knowledge proof aggregation [^evt-project-proposals-issue-68].

# Architecture / Specification

Zeko allows operators to deploy sovereign rollups with localized keys, access policies, and hosting models, such as confidential computing enclaves [^evt-project-proposals-issue-68]. Its architectural components include:

- **Rollup State Ordering:** Resolves competing state transitions from concurrent agents with immediate local confirmation [^evt-project-proposals-issue-68].
- **Recursive Proof Aggregation:** Employs zero-knowledge proofs to allow multi-agent systems to verify complex state updates without re-executing computations or exposing private inputs [^evt-project-proposals-issue-68].
- **AAIF Ecosystem Integrations:** Interoperates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) interfaces for coordinated tool actions and reservations; [Goose](../resources/goose.md) for external policy-enforced resource limits; [AgentGateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) for shared multi-gateway budgets; [Open Responses](../standards/open-responses.md) for state-linked receipts; and [OpenSandbox](../resources/opensandbox.md) for reproducible execution receipts [^evt-project-proposals-issue-68].

# Lifecycle History

Zeko was proposed for AAIF Sandbox status via Issue #68 on `aaif/project-proposals` [^evt-project-proposals-issue-68]. As an unmerged proposal, it remains in `draft` status within foundation tracking [^evt-project-proposals-issue-68].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Implementation guide establishing architectural controls for secrets management, workload identity, secure tool invocation, and MCP threat mitigation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide, curated by the Security and Privacy Working Group, defines operational and architectural controls for production agent deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99]. It addresses five core functional areas: secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99]. Delegated identity architectures (such as SPIFFE/SVID and UCANs) are coordinated with the Identity and Trust Working Group and surfaced via the [Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99].

# Architecture / Specification

### Secrets Management

Static and long-lived credentials in agent environments present persistent extraction vectors via prompt injection or deserialization exploits (e.g., CVE-2025-68664) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99]. The guide mandates transitioning from stored static assets to ephemeral attestations across a hierarchy of patterns [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99]:

1. **Workload Identity:** Primary baseline utilizing cloud OIDC attestation (IRSA, GCP Workload Identity, Azure Managed Identity) to supply 1-hour credentials [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99].
2. **Dynamic Secrets:** On-demand short-lived credentials via tools like HashiCorp Vault for third-party databases and APIs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99].
3. **Network-Layer Injection:** Sidecar proxies handling credential attachment out-of-band for legacy systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99].
4. **Confidential Computing:** Hardware memory encryption (Intel TDX, AMD SEV-SNP) for high-sensitivity regulatory or multi-tenant agent workloads, bound to short-lived token lifetimes [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99].
5. **OAuth Token Exchange (RFC 8693):** Downstream token scope narrowing per delegation hop [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99].

### Secure Tool Invocation and MCP Security

The guide highlights vulnerability patterns in Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystems, including tool description poisoning (Unicode tag injection), server rug pulls, cross-server shadowing, and sampling abuse [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99]. Mitigations include mandatory pre-deployment static scanning, public advisory cross-referencing, enforcement of OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and RFC 8707 audience binding on HTTP transports, and sandboxing local stdio executions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99]. Proposals also investigate C2PA Content Credentials to verify publisher provenance across agent skills [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-49].

proposed_concept.title: Runkite
proposed_concept.description: Self-hosted agent control plane and runner dispatch service providing run admission, connector governance, human approvals, and MCP tool endpoints.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Runkite is an open-source, self-hosted control plane for AI agents that decouples agent operations, dispatch, and governance from model-loop execution frameworks [^evt-project-proposals-issue-69]. Implemented as a core Go binary with distinct Python and TypeScript execution runners, Runkite coordinates thread and run lifecycles, human approval workflows, connector access control, spend accounting, and audit logging across heterogeneous agent software development kits (SDKs) [^evt-project-proposals-issue-69].

In March 2026, Runkite was submitted as an open proposal for Sandbox entry within the Agentic AI Foundation under the [Project Proposal Process](../policies/project-proposal-process.md) [^evt-project-proposals-issue-69]. It connects directly to the Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem by exposing configured agents as callable MCP tools and mediating outbound MCP server interactions through authorization checkpoints [^evt-project-proposals-issue-69].

# Architecture / Specification

Runkite partitions agent system responsibilities into a centralized management daemon and isolated runtime workers [^evt-project-proposals-issue-69]:

- **Control Plane Daemon**: A compiled Go service managing client authentication, thread and run state, connector credentials, budget and spend enforcement, audit event emission, and an embedded administrative web interface [^evt-project-proposals-issue-69]. Persistence relies on SQLite with an in-process queue for single-node deployments, or PostgreSQL paired with Redis for high-availability deployments [^evt-project-proposals-issue-69].
- **Runner Protocol**: A gRPC interface over which the control plane dispatches task assignments to external, language-specific execution runners (such as Python or TypeScript) that run standard framework loops natively [^evt-project-proposals-issue-69].
- **Client Interfaces**: External consumers invoke agents and inspect progress via an Agent Protocol HTTP API supporting Server-Sent Events (SSE) and WebSocket streaming [^evt-project-proposals-issue-69]. Additionally, Runkite exposes a standalone decision API allowing external orchestrators to query policy and approval gates without handing over run lifecycle control [^evt-project-proposals-issue-69].
- **MCP Surface**: Implements an HTTP `/mcp` endpoint using the official MCP Go SDK, translating tool invocations into managed agent runs. Outbound MCP connectors enforce access grants and [Human-Approval Gates](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) [^evt-project-proposals-issue-69].
- **Boundary Limits**: Runkite does not supply inference routing or external secret storage, and its internal `a2a` endpoint denotes local subagent dispatch rather than the AAIF Agent2Agent protocol specification [^evt-project-proposals-issue-69]. Native tools invoked directly within a runner bypass Runkite's connector mediation boundary [^evt-project-proposals-issue-69].

# Lifecycle History

- **July 2026**: Public repository established under the Apache-2.0 license as a founder-maintained project [^evt-project-proposals-issue-69].
- **March 2026**: Proposed for AAIF Sandbox status via issue #69 in `aaif/project-proposals`, seeking neutral community governance and standardized multi-SDK operational contracts [^evt-project-proposals-issue-69].

[^evt-project-proposals-issue-69]: GitHub Issue aaif/project-proposals#69, '[Project Proposal] Runkite', https://github.com/aaif/project-proposals/issues/69
